packaged_documentation.TheDarkness.pc.example.toml:
# PC settings schema 1.
#
# These are the Enhanced PC defaults. Without a TheDarkness.pc.toml beside
# TheDarkness.exe the game runs exactly these values; the settings launcher
# and the in-game settings overlay save your changes into TheDarkness.pc.toml
# (created from this file). The Original / Xbox-Compatible configuration is
# the packaged preset presets/original_720p.toml. Select any file explicitly
# with --pc-config <path>.
# Portable save/profile data defaults to runtime_data beside the executable.
# Launchers may select a managed writable directory with
# --user-data-root <path>; this does not change original game content.
# The game reads its configuration once at startup; the in-game overlay
# applies the settings it marks live at once and the rest at the next start.

pc_config_version = 1

# Output/window resolution. Supported presets include native, 720p, 1080p,
# 1440p, 4k, and explicit WIDTHxHEIGHT values up to 8192x8192. In a decorated
# window this selects the physical presentation surface. Borderless fullscreen
# follows the selected monitor's desktop surface; the value remains the
# restored window size. The guest-facing Xbox mode remains the verified
# 1280x720 compatibility mode.
output_resolution = "native"

# Optional window overrides. Leave at zero to follow the resolution preset.
window_width = 0
window_height = 0
fullscreen = true
# Explicit PC mode. `auto` is retained only for legacy ReXGlue configurations;
# this project supports decorated windowed and borderless desktop modes, not
# exclusive fullscreen.
window_mode = "borderless"
monitor = 0

# Internal Xenos render scale, independent of output size. For the title's
# 1280x720 reference buffers, 2 produces 2560x1440 and 3 produces 3840x2160.
# 0 is Automatic: the first time, the game times the graphics card on the
# title screen (stored per card in the user data folder as
# gpu_calibration.toml) and from the next start picks the highest scale that
# keeps the busiest street at the recommended frame rate (60-120 FPS); until
# then it guesses from video memory (2, 3 for 4K on 16 GB cards, 1 below
# 6 GB or 1000 output lines). Scale 1 is the Original value.
resolution_scale = 0
# Title data-pass annotations that internal scaling requires (three RGB
# lookup-table passes and the bloom chain keep the native grid, the native
# bloom is enlarged by native bilinear reconstruction where it is consumed,
# which needs native_resolve_region_tracking; targets narrower than 640 pixels
# stay native). Not settings: the game adds them itself when a configuration
# raises resolution_scale without them.
draw_resolution_scale_threshold = 640
draw_resolution_scale_native_grid_rules = "B29F0BF45937C4C4:FDC5E32EC6045BE1:1:324:18:6;B29F0BF45937C4C4:37AC93F53126ABB7:0:324:18:26;B29F0BF45937C4C4:54D655FC471D594A:0:324:18:26;B29F0BF45937C4C4:69779AD07425E356:0:324:18:26;B29F0BF45937C4C4:FAE3BACA27F09CC9:0:1280:720:6:filter;B29F0BF45937C4C4:FAE3BACA27F09CC9:0:1280:720:26:filter;B29F0BF45937C4C4:9F1D2D64E5F75924:0:1280:720:26:filter;B29F0BF45937C4C4:9F1D2D64E5F75924:0:160:90:6:filter;B29F0BF45937C4C4:8F96D5C280D780BC:0:1280:720:26:filter;EC4685ADB9CCBC13:207D40E674A7C916:0:1280:720:26:filter_scaled:source=native;4FA9486610B42A92:22FC55CE134777AC:1:1280:720:26:filter_scaled:source=native;4FA9486610B42A92:A59B41D0BD79484B:1:1280:720:26:filter_scaled:source=native"
native_resolve_region_tracking = true

# Post-process AA: none (the original output), fxaa, fxaa_extreme or smaa
# (SMAA 1x: edges without FXAA's blur, same cost as fxaa_extreme). Temporal
# AA and the upscalers are graphics.temporal_aa below.
swap_post_effect = "smaa"

# Anisotropic filtering: -1 (title-selected), 0 (disabled), 1/2/3/4/5
# (1x/2x/4x/8x/16x). The Original preset forces 4x (3).
anisotropic_override = 5

[general]
# Xbox title language. The extracted multi-language release contains these
# exact options: english, german, french, spanish, and italian. "auto"
# follows the Windows display language like the console's dashboard language
# (English when the game does not ship that language).
language = "auto"
# Shows a toast in the game window for each newly unlocked achievement. The
# unlocks are stored either way (content/achievements/545407EE.toml).
achievement_notifications = true

[graphics]
# false selects the exact sibling shader permutations that remove only the
# camera motion blur while retaining exposure, RGB-map color grading, glow
# and gamma behavior. true is the Xbox title-native final composite.
# motion_blur_off_shader_pack: empty = the built-in patch of those shaders;
# a path = a shader replacement pack file to use instead.
motion_blur = false
motion_blur_off_shader_pack = ""
hd_textures = false
temporal_aa = "off"
# Temporal upscaler (#3, #23): off, dlss (NVIDIA RTX), fsr (AMD FSR 3.1) or
# xess (Intel XeSS) builds a larger image from the internal scale:
# upscale_mode native (anti-aliasing only, DLAA), quality (1.5x), balanced
# (1.7x), performance (2x) or ultra_performance (3x).
upscaler = "off"
upscale_mode = "quality"
# Scene MSAA (#16): "4x" keeps the console's normal 4x all the time (on PC
# also the faster mode above internal scale 1x: the 2x mode needs about twice
# the graphics time there); "2x" always uses the game's 2x mode (faster only
# at 1x); "auto" is the game's own switch, which drops to 2x when the slowest
# of its last 10 frames is below 32 FPS and returns above 38 (a loading hitch
# or a 37.5 FPS menu on a 75 Hz screen can keep it on 2x).
msaa_mode = "4x"
# Glow reconstruction, above internal scale 1x: "on" keeps the glow around
# lights and in bright flashes as smooth as on the console; "off" draws it as
# in 0.9.0, with a little banding in bright flashes (a fallback if the glow
# looks wrong on your graphics card). The in-game overlay (F1) applies a
# change at once.
glow_reconstruction = "on"

[present]
# Upscaling: how the rendered image is fitted to the screen.
#   "auto"     - AMD FSR 1 when the internal image is smaller than the output
#                (for example 1x on a 1440p screen); a 1:1 image is untouched.
#   "fsr"      - AMD FSR 1 always (sharpens a 1:1 image with CAS).
#   "bilinear" - plain bilinear filtering (the original presentation).
#   "cas"      - AMD CAS sharpening (and resampling up to 2x).
# FSR 1 and CAS run on any graphics card; the overlay applies changes at once.
effect = "auto"
# Preserve the complete Xbox 16:9 image on non-16:9 displays. Wider displays
# receive pillarboxes and taller displays receive letterboxes; no title image
# is stretched or cropped while safe aspect expansion is still under audit.
letterbox = true
allow_overscan_cutoff = false
safe_area_x = 100
safe_area_y = 100

[display]
# vsync: VSync On - synchronized, tear-free default; G-SYNC/FreeSync
#        displays still follow the frame rate
# immediate: VSync Off - unsynchronized presentation; tearing may be visible
# vrr: presents without waiting (tearing allowed) for variable-refresh
#      displays; tears on fixed-refresh displays. Without DXGI tearing
#      support it falls back to synchronized presentation
present_mode = "vsync"

# Number of frames that DXGI may queue. 1 lowers latency most aggressively;
# 2 is the compatibility value; 3 may smooth heavily loaded systems.
max_frame_latency = 1

# Low latency: "on" keeps the game at most two frames ahead of the display,
# the wait ending half a frame before the awaited present so the frame rate
# holds (VSync 144 Hz: input to present 24.9 -> 16.8 ms at 144 FPS); at 60 FPS
# the game never runs further ahead. Only with VSync (present_mode = "vsync"):
# with VSync off frames are shown at once and it does nothing (measured
# uncapped: it would cost frame rate). "off" lets the frame queue fill.
low_latency = "on"

# Custom frame cap in frames per second, used when frame_rate = "custom".
# Zero means no cap.
frame_limit = 0

# Frame rate. The title's world keeps its fixed 30 Hz tick in every mode, so
# movement, scripted scenes, animation and audio stay real-time.
#   "original"     - the game's own pacing (30 FPS in gameplay). Restart to change.
#   "60"           - 60 FPS.
#   "half_refresh" - half the display refresh (72 on a 144 Hz display).
#   "refresh"      - the display refresh (144 on a 144 Hz display).
#   "custom"       - frame_limit above.
#   "uncapped"     - no cap; use with present_mode "vrr" or "immediate".
#   "120", "144"... - any whole number from 20 to 1000 caps at that rate.
# With present_mode = "vsync", rates that divide the display refresh are paced
# by the display and look even; other rates (for example 120 on 144 Hz)
# alternate between one and two refreshes unless the display has VRR.
frame_rate = "refresh"

# Menus, the title screen and loading: "reduced" runs them at about 60 FPS
# at most (a whole divisor of the refresh with VSync, 48 on 144 Hz) - the
# menu backdrop costs more GPU time per frame than gameplay; "full" uses
# the gameplay frame rate.
menu_frame_rate = "reduced"
widescreen = false

[streamline]
# Experimental NVIDIA DLSS Frame Generation (#3): generated frames per rendered
# frame, 0 = off. Only test builds offer it (DARKNESS_EXPERIMENTAL=frame_generation);
# otherwise it is always 0.
frame_generation = 0

[cheats]
# The developers' own cheats (runtime_cheats.h), off by default. god_mode is
# not kept in saves; give_all (every weapon, highest Darkness and Demon Arm
# levels) is. No achievements unlock while a cheat is on.
god_mode = false
give_all = false

[camera]
# The decoded title viewport's original horizontal FOV is 95 degrees. The
# setting changes only the verified main gameplay viewport; scripted and
# cutscene setters remain title-owned and are not globally scaled.
field_of_view = 86.0

[audio]
# Final host PCM output only. 1.0 preserves the exact title mix; 0.0 silences
# physical playback without changing guest mixing, callbacks, or timing.
master_volume = 1.0

[input]
# Keyboard and mouse from the focused game window are merged into controller
# slot 0; a connected controller keeps working. false preserves the physical
# Xbox/XInput path exactly. Changing it or its controller slot requires a
# restart; sensitivity and inversion also apply live from the overlay.
keyboard_mouse = true
keyboard_mouse_user_index = 0
mouse_sensitivity = 1.0
# Optional bounded per-physical-event acceleration. 0.0 is exact linear input;
# 1.0 reaches at most 2x gain for a 32-count-or-larger event.
mouse_acceleration = 0.0
# Optional two-sample smoothing at the guest-poll boundary. 0.0 is exact
# identity; 1.0 averages adjacent polls and has at most one poll of tail.
mouse_smoothing = 0.0
mouse_invert_y = false
# Button prompts: "auto" shows the bound keys while you play with keyboard and
# mouse and Xbox buttons again after controller input; "xbox" or "keyboard"
# fixes one (applies live from the overlay).
button_prompts = "auto"
# "native" turns the camera with the title's own look command: raw mouse
# counts, 1:1, no stick dead zone, ramp or turn cap. "stick" keeps the
# older mouse-to-right-stick bridge. Changing it requires a restart.
mouse_look = "native"
# Opens the in-game settings overlay (F1, F2, F4-F8 or F11; Esc also
# closes it). Changing it requires a restart.
overlay_key = "F1"
# These are standard Xbox profile preferences consumed by The Darkness through
# its native controller setup. They do not add host-side analog shaping.
controller_sensitivity = "medium" # medium, low, high
controller_invert_y = false
# Physical motor output only. 1.0 preserves the exact guest request; 0.0
# disables rumble without changing guest input, packet state, or return codes.
vibration_scale = 1.0
# Key binding defaults of this file: 2 = jump on Space, use on E (0.9.1). A
# configuration without it is from 0.9.0 (use on Space, jump on E); its first
# start moves those two keys to the new defaults if they were never changed.
bindings_revision = 2

[input.controller_bind]
# Optional physical XInput digital-button remapping. Keys are guest actions;
# values are physical button names or "none". The identity map below preserves
# the original controller exactly. Analog triggers/sticks and title dead zones
# remain untouched.
dpad_up = "dpad_up"
dpad_down = "dpad_down"
dpad_left = "dpad_left"
dpad_right = "dpad_right"
start = "start"
back = "back"
left_stick = "left_stick"
right_stick = "right_stick"
left_shoulder = "left_shoulder"
right_shoulder = "right_shoulder"
guide = "guide"
a = "a"
b = "b"
x = "x"
y = "y"

[input.bind]
# Rebindable physical keys. Mouse motion uses SDL's native relative mode while
# focused/captured, avoiding desktop-edge clipping or cursor-warp deltas.
a = "E"
b = "Shift"
x = "R"
y = "Space"
left_trigger = "RMB"
right_trigger = "LMB"
left_shoulder = "Q"
right_shoulder = "F"
lstick_up = "W"
lstick_down = "S"
lstick_left = "A"
lstick_right = "D"
lstick_press = "C"
rstick_press = "MMB"
dpad_up = "Up"
dpad_down = "Down"
dpad_left = "Left"
dpad_right = "Right"
back = "Tab"
start = "Escape"
guide = ""

# Mouse 4/5 use X1/X2. Physical wheel detents use WheelUp/WheelDown and are
# preserved as bounded one-poll pulses so quick scrolling cannot become a
# permanently held guest button.

[diagnostics]
# Bounded to 128 native viewport setter events when enabled. Keep disabled for
# normal play and performance measurements.
camera_state = false

route.title: Attach the prepared direct player
route.instruction: Select TheDarkness.exe, set the complete extracted runtime directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the exact intent and request Play separately. The settings launcher’s default command is this same program without extra arguments. The native parser defaults to normal Run and resolves the existing configured game location or prepared game/default.xex; it does not require a fabricated private-cache path or launcher environment. Finish missing/unsupported game setup upstream before retrying. The game runs in the selected native process.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact supported code upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own The Darkness Xbox 360 USA/Europe (En/Fr/De/Es/It), title 545407EE. The documented disc SHA256 is 46f7305c1e1972e888d3624f15b0ed483923aeeb50ecad0c6bf5b42f69d52a90; default.xex SHA256 is aace35a8f9bcdc7f28aeab9ff8cf3bdf200353f5c83705f6284487347acb3c5f. Upstream can accept localized headers/text when its decoded code, structure and required data match; that is not a claim every region or title update works. Finish TheDarknessSettings.exe setup, data validation and settings outside Portcove, retaining independent originals. No disc, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed by this guide.

persistence.title: Preserve Saved Games and migration recovery
persistence.instruction: The normal root is the Windows Saved Games location, usually %USERPROFILE%/Saved Games/Estacado, with TheDarkness.pc.toml, content/ saves and other player data. Per-user logs, caches and diagnostics also use the separate %LOCALAPPDATA%/Estacado root (or the runtime’s actual local fallback); preserve it too. Use the actual Windows known-folder locations if Saved Games or Local AppData has been relocated. An already existing portable.txt beside TheDarkness.exe instead keeps the legacy package-local configuration/runtime_data; explicit external config/user-data roots also remain authoritative. Upstream’s 0.9.0 transition copies and checks old data, keeps originals and writes SAVES_MOVED.txt; if copying fails it can retain the old layout and retry. Preserve all old/new roots, screenshot/data copies, original images and the configured game-location pointer. This guide creates no marker and performs no import, migration, backup or deletion.

limitations: Select TheDarkness.exe after setup. Preserve the actual Saved Games, portable or legacy roots and retained migration copies; another Darkness implementation and settings/updater processes have separate ownership.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Which USA ROM revision/digest is accepted by the selected SpaceRanger build?

packaged_documentation.SpaceRanger/README.txt:
SpaceRanger  (pre-release)
==========================

A native PC port of Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue (N64), made by
statically recompiling the original game with N64Recomp and rendering it with
RT64. Unofficial fan project; no game data is included. Built with help
from AI coding assistants (Anthropic's Claude, and OpenAI's ChatGPT/Codex).

You need your own copy of the game
----------------------------------
Supported ROM: Toy Story 2 (N64, USA). .z64, .n64 and .v64 dumps all work.

First launch
------------
1. Run SpaceRanger.exe.
2. On the title screen choose "Load ROM" and select your ROM. It is checked
   and copied into the "spaceranger-config" folder next to the exe, so you
   only do this once. (You can also put the ROM next to SpaceRanger.exe and
   it is found automatically.)
3. Choose "Start Game".

Settings and saves live in "spaceranger-config". Delete that folder to start
fresh (you will be asked for the ROM again).

Source code (GPL-3.0, see LICENSE.txt):
  https://github.com/Capridog/SpaceRanger

Problems and bug reports: https://github.com/Capridog/SpaceRanger/issues
Please include your GPU, monitor refresh rate and what you were doing.

route.title: Attach the ordinary title-screen route
route.instruction: Select SpaceRanger.exe, use the complete extracted SpaceRanger directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the intent and request Play separately, then use the upstream Start Game option with the already validated ROM. The normal native entry sets its directory, initializes the UI and runs the linked runtime in process. Asset checks, overlay checks, input replay and TS2_AUTOSTART are different diagnostic paths; this guide enables none. Complete missing data/setup outside the attached attempt.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact USA Rev0 source
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Toy Story 2: Buzz Lightyear to the Rescue N64 USA Rev0 ROM. The selected game registration checks normalized ROM bytes with XXH3-64 FD53C5EC8CE2530A; this is the actual revision-matching digest, not a SHA1, ownership test or package signature. The pinned runtime normalizes supported .z64/.v64/.n64 byte orders first. Other regions, revisions and console editions remain unsupported. Finish Load ROM upstream before attachment and retain the independent original.

persistence.title: Preserve the whole portable tree
persistence.instruction: Keep spaceranger-config beside SpaceRanger.exe, including its validated ROM copy, settings and any existing player data, plus assets, logs and previously established external paths. The source explicitly registers that portable root and declares no cartridge save type; neither that declaration nor a directory’s presence establishes real game-save, Controller Pak or restore support. Upstream’s FAQ reset deletes the whole spaceranger-config folder to reselect a ROM: retain complete independent recovery copies before any upstream reset, and do not treat registration removal as such a reset. This guide performs no deletion, migration, backup or save conversion.

limitations: Keep spaceranger-config intact; it includes the validated ROM and settings/player data. USA Rev0 matching and static Windows observations do not qualify saves, all levels or another platform.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Review official player setup and data/persistence boundaries for the specific offered route; metadata alone does not qualify execution.

pe_prefix.scope: bounded header only; no execution, complete imports, ABI or dependency resolution

packaged_documentation.wg3d-recomp-v0.8.1/README.txt:
W.G. 3D Hockey: Recompiled  v0.8.1
https://github.com/geno55/wg3d-recomp

A native Windows port of Wayne Gretzky's 3D Hockey (N64), made by static recompilation with
N64Recomp, N64ModernRuntime and RT64. Unofficial fan project.

NO GAME DATA IS INCLUDED. You need your own ROM of the USA V1.0 release
(sha1 400aa84811f1f2f6c62c756b43b54d534d5a5ec8 as .z64; .v64 and .n64 dumps work too).

REQUIREMENTS
  Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a GPU with Direct3D 12 or Vulkan.

FIRST RUN
  Run wg3d.exe and choose Choose ROM... in the launcher (or drag the ROM onto wg3d.exe, or run
  wg3d.exe path\to\your\rom.z64). The ROM is checked and copied to %APPDATA%\WG3DRecomp.
  After that, run wg3d.exe and pick Start game.

SETTINGS MENU
  Esc, or a controller's Back (View) button, opens the settings menu over the paused game. Settings
  in the launcher opens the same menu. Tabs: General, Controls, Graphics, Sound.
  Up/down picks a setting, left/right changes it, Enter (A) selects, Esc (B) goes back,
  Q/E (LB/RB) switches tabs. The mouse works too. Changes apply at once and are saved.
  Controls > Bindings: choose a slot, press Enter (A), then press the key or controller input to use;
  Del (X) clears a slot.

CONTROLS
  Keyboard (port 1): arrows/WASD = stick, X = A, C = B, Z/Left Shift = Z, Enter = Start,
  Q/E = L/R, I/J/K/L = C buttons, T/F/G/H = D-pad.
  Gamepads (Xbox layout) take ports 1-4 in the order they are connected.
  All of this can be changed in the settings menu (Controls) or in controls.json (below).
  Alt+Enter or F11: toggle fullscreen (remembered).

SETTINGS AND SAVES  (%APPDATA%\WG3DRecomp)
  graphics.json  resolution (Original/Original2x/Auto), antialiasing (None/MSAA2X/MSAA4X/MSAA8X),
                 window_mode (Windowed/Fullscreen), graphics_api (Auto/D3D12/Vulkan), and more
  general.json   pak_port_1..4: which ports have a Controller Pak (all four by default),
                 pause_when_unfocused (true/false)
  controls.json  keyboard_port (1-4, 0 = off), deadzone (percent), pads (per port, part of a controller's
                 name to put on that port), and the keyboard and gamepad bindings: up to two keys or
                 controller inputs per N64 button and stick direction, e.g. "A": ["X", "Space"] or
                 "Z": ["lefttrigger"] (controller inputs: a b x y start leftshoulder rightshoulder dpup
                 dpdown dpleft dpright leftstick rightstick, lefttrigger righttrigger, leftx- leftx+
                 lefty- lefty+ rightx- rightx+ righty- righty+)
  sound.json     master_volume (0-100), mute_when_unfocused (true/false)
  window.json    window size and position (remembered automatically)
  saves\controllerpak_port<N>\   Controller Pak saves
  logs\wg3d.log  log of the last run (the two before it are kept as wg3d.1.log and wg3d.2.log);
                 crash reports are saved next to it as crash-<date>-<time>.txt
  The files are created on first run. The settings menu edits them; to edit them by hand, close the
  game first.
  wg3d.exe --console also shows the log in a console window.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS
  - A correctness pass is in progress; report problems on GitHub (attach the log or crash report).
  - High frame rate (Settings > Graphics > Frame rate > Display) generates frames between the game's 30
    per second, up to your monitor's rate. The menus and 2D screens stay at 30.
  - Widescreen (Settings > Graphics > Aspect ratio > Expand) widens the rink only; menus and the HUD stay
    4:3 in the middle, and at very wide ratios the corners of the arena can show black where the game
    has no scenery.

LICENSE
  GPL-3.0 (LICENSE.txt). wg3d.exe contains this project's code (GPL-3.0), N64ModernRuntime (GPL-3.0) and
  other open-source libraries; see THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.
  Source: https://github.com/geno55/wg3d-recomp (tag v0.8.1).

wg3d.pdb lets crash reports name the function that crashed; keep it next to wg3d.exe.
The msvcp140/vcruntime140 DLLs are the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime, included so no separate install is needed.

route.title: Attach normal player startup
route.instruction: Select wg3d.exe, use the complete extracted package directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the exact intent and request Play separately, then use the upstream UI to start the already selected game. The native entry starts the linked runtime in process and saves window state on return. Its --frames, speed, capture and console options are diagnostic controls, not normal Play arguments. Finish missing-ROM setup outside the attached attempt.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact USA revision
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Wayne Gretzky’s 3D Hockey USA V1.0 ROM. The selected source identifies big-endian ROM SHA1 400aa84811f1f2f6c62c756b43b54d534d5a5ec8 and validates normalized bytes with XXH3-64 B615F7ACDFB899B4. Supported .z64/.v64/.n64 byte orders are normalized before that runtime check; their raw file digests are not interchangeable. This is source matching, not ownership or package authentication. Finish upstream ROM selection before attachment and keep the independent original.

persistence.title: Preserve Roaming data and the actual Controller Paks
persistence.instruction: Keep the whole active data root, normally %APPDATA%/WG3DRecomp on Windows, including the validated ROM copy, settings/input/window files, logs/wg3d.log and saves/controllerpak_port<N>/ for the corresponding controller ports. An already established --data-dir can choose an external root; preserve that exact directory too. The source declares no cartridge save type and routes saves to Controller Paks; do not replace them with another title’s EEPROM file or infer real save compatibility. This guide performs no import, migration, backup or deletion.

limitations: Use USA V1.0 and the actual WG3DRecomp data root. Controller Pak storage, other revisions, devices and real save compatibility remain distinct.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Review official player setup and data/persistence boundaries for the specific offered route; metadata alone does not qualify execution.

packaged_documentation.UltraCombo-Windows/shaders/README.txt:
Shader presets for the Filter / Shader option, in libretro's GLSL format.

Bundled here, from https://github.com/libretro/glsl-shaders (licence headers
kept in each file):
  crt/crt-lottes*        public domain (Timothy Lottes)
  crt/crt-hyllian*       MIT (Hyllian)
  crt/crt-nobody         MIT
  crt/crt-1tap, 2tap     public domain
  scalefx/               MIT (Sp00kyFox)
  xbr/                   MIT (Hyllian)

lola-retro/ is Lola Retro's arcade-15khz preset (MIT, Zoki; licence in that
folder), from https://github.com/zoran123456/lola-retro. Its slang passes are
converted to GLSL by its own tools/make_glsl.py, through tools/lola_retro.py
(`make shaders-lola`). The files are generated, so don't edit them.

`make shaders-extra` installs more into shaders/extra/: xBRZ, crt-guest,
crt-royale, crt-geom, crt-easymode, zfast-crt and crt-aperture. Those are
GPL-licensed; they are separate files read at run time, and keep their
licence headers. Any other libretro .glslp preset works too: put it (with
the files it uses) anywhere under this folder.
packaged_documentation.UltraCombo-Windows/README.md:
# UltraCombo

Native PC ports of the Killer Instinct arcade games, for Windows and Linux:

| | Plays | MAME set | Versions |
|---|---|---|---|
| **UltraCombo** | Killer Instinct (1994) | `kinst` | L1.5D (default), L1.4 |
| **UltraCombo 2** | Killer Instinct 2 (1996) | `kinst2` | L1.4 |

Both are one program. It runs the arcade games' own code, translated to C
for your PC, with the board around it emulated: the Midway DCS sound board
and the IDE hard disk. On top come the things a home version needs: shaders
and CRT looks, rebindable controls and gamepads, save states, rewind,
run-ahead, training mode and rollback netplay.

**No game files are included.** You need your own copies of the arcade
games' files: the ROMs and the hard disk image (CHD) of MAME's sets.

## Setup

Put the files of one game or both in `run/`, the files of MAME's sets as
they come:

**Killer Instinct** (`kinst`):

- `ki-l15d.u98`: boot ROM, version L1.5D; `ki-l14.u98` (L1.4) is optional
- `u10-l1` … `u13-l1`, `u33-l1` … `u36-l1`: sound ROMs
- `kinst.chd`: the hard disk

**Killer Instinct 2** (`kinst2`):

- `ki2-l14.u98`: boot ROM, version L1.4
- `ki2_l1.u10` … `ki2_l1.u13`, `ki2_l1.u33` … `ki2_l1.u36`: sound ROMs
- `kinst2.chd`: the hard disk

The two games' file names don't clash. A CHD can also sit in a folder named
after its set (`run/kinst/kinst.chd`, `run/kinst2/kinst2.chd`), the way MAME
keeps it. A raw disk image (`kinst.raw`, `kinst2.raw`, from `chdman
extractraw`) works too, and is used if both are there. Each game's file
paths can also be set in its settings file (`ki1.ini`, `ki2.ini`).

The disk images are only ever read. A game's settings, audits and high
scores (the first 32 KB of its disk) go to `saves/<boot ROM>.settings`, one
file per game version. A raw image that an earlier version of this program
wrote to keeps its settings: they are copied into that file on the first
launch. `ultracombo --game ki2 --write-raw kinst2.raw` writes a disk out as
a raw image, the same as `chdman extractraw`, if you ever need one.

### Checking your files

These are the files of MAME's `kinst` and `kinst2` sets (the dumps MAME
lists as good). At startup the program compares your files with them and
warns, naming the file, if one doesn't match. To check them yourself use
`md5sum` (Linux), `certutil -hashfile FILE MD5` (Windows) or any ROM
manager. Every ROM is 524,288 bytes.

### Starting

Start `ultracombo` (`UltraCombo.exe` on Windows; the AppImage on Linux).
With both games installed it asks which to play: left/right (or a click)
chooses, Enter or the controller select button starts (shown on screen).
It remembers the last choice. With one game installed it starts that one
straight away. Menu → **Change game** goes back
to the choice, and `--game ki1` or `--game ki2` skips it (for shortcuts).

The first time you play each game, and each version of it, the program shows
"PREPARING THE GAME FOR THIS PC": it boots your game files on its
interpreter until the game has loaded its code, snapshots that code,
translates it to C, along with the sound board's DSP program from the sound
ROMs, and compiles it into a native module. That takes about a
minute, once; the module is cached in `cache/` (a new one is made if the
game files change). The compiler used is the first that works of:

1. Zig, bundled in `tools/zig`, which the release packages include
2. a C compiler already installed (`cc`, `gcc` or `clang`)
3. TinyCC, bundled in `tools/tcc`: it builds in seconds, but its code runs
   at roughly half the speed (still well above full speed on most PCs)

If none works the game runs on the interpreter, with a warning; see
`build.log` in `cache/src-*/`. All three produce code that behaves
identically, so netplay works between them.

Settings (`ki1.ini`, `ki2.ini`), the games' saves, the logs, screenshots,
states and the cache are written next to the program if that folder is
writable, else into the user data folder (`%APPDATA%\UltraCombo\` on
Windows, `~/.local/share/UltraCombo/` on Linux), whose `run/` folder is also
searched for the game files. With the AppImage, make a `run/` folder beside
the `.AppImage`: the game files go in it, and settings and the cache go
beside the AppImage too.

## Controls

| Action | Player 1 | Player 2 | Pad (Xbox names) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Move | Arrow keys | I J K L | D-pad / left stick |
| Quick / Medium / Fierce punch | A S D | T Y U | X / Y / RB |
| Quick / Medium / Fierce kick | Z X C | G H B | A / B / RT |
| Start | 1 | 2 | Start |
| Coin | 5 | 6 | Back |

The games run in **free play** by default (the board's coinage DIP
switch): from the attract demo, the first Start goes to the title screen
and the second starts the game, as on a free-play cabinet. In UltraCombo 2,
with free play off, `auto_coin` makes Start insert the coins it needs. The
first pad connected is player 1, the second player 2.

| Hotkey | |
|---|---|
| Esc or F1 | Menu (pad: Guide, or Back+Start) |
| F5 / F7 | Save / load state in the current slot |
| F6 | Next state slot (1-9) |
| Backspace (hold) | Rewind |
| Tab (hold) | Fast-forward |
| P | Pause |
| . | Frame advance (pauses first) |
| F11 or Alt+Enter | Fullscreen |
| F12 | Screenshot to `screenshots/` |
| F3 | Input display |
| F4 | Training mode |
| F8 / F9 | Record / play the training dummy |
| F10 | Performance overlay |
| = / - / M | Volume up / down / mute |
| F2 | Operator test menu |
| 9 | Service credit |
| Page Up / Page Down | The cabinet's own volume buttons |

Each game keeps its own settings; changes made in the menu are saved to its
`.ini` file when the menu closes.

## The menu

**Graphics:** fullscreen (borderless, or exclusive at a chosen display
mode), window size, scaling (fit 4:3, integer, stretch), shader, shader
parameters, frame pacing and the performance overlay.

**Controls:** rebind both players' keys, the gamepad buttons and all hotkeys
(select one, press the new key or button; Backspace unbinds). Also there:
**left+right = neutral** (SOCD cleaning, on by default: left and right
together count as neither, up and down together as up, like fight sticks),
**rumble** when your character is hit, and the stick deadzone.

**Game & system:**

- **Game version** (Killer Instinct: L1.5D or L1.4, when both boot ROMs are
  there): pick it, then Enter switches. That resets the game, like swapping
  the ROM on the cabinet; each version keeps its own settings and high
  scores. L1.4 is the original release, with the bugs and infinite combos
  that L1.5D fixed.
- **CPU difficulty** (Extra easy to Extra hard): written to the disk's
  adjustments exactly as the game's operator menu does, so it applies after
  Reset.
- **Free play, blood level, finishing moves, attract-mode sound** and, in
  Killer Instinct, **blood colour** (red or white): the board's DIP
  switches, read at power-on, so they apply after Reset.
- Volume, mute or pause in the background, auto-coin (UltraCombo 2),
  run-ahead and rewind.

Button labels follow the last controller used; keyboard input switches menu
prompts back to keyboard names. Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo Switch layouts
are detected through SDL. Before a controller is used, and for controllers
SDL cannot identify, labels fall back to Xbox-style A/B/X/Y names. Controls →
P1/P2 button labels overrides the detected family when an adapter hides it;
Positions remains available for South/East/West/North names. This changes
labels only, not the bindings. SDL's Nintendo letter-based and positional
mappings are both respected, including the exchanged A/B and X/Y positions.
The shared gamepad-binding page shows labels for the last pad used.

The window's size and position are remembered between runs.

## Graphics

**Shaders** are drawn by the GPU. Four are built in:

- **Sharp**: crisp pixels, evenly sized at any window size
- **Smooth**: sharpened bicubic; suits the games' pre-rendered 3D art
- **Scanlines**, **CRT**: simple, fast CRT looks

Any **libretro GLSL preset** (`.glslp`, the format of RetroArch's shader
collection) under `shaders/` works too, multi-pass presets, lookup
textures and all. Bundled: crt-lottes, crt-hyllian, crt-nobody, crt-1tap/2tap,
ScaleFX and xBR. `make shaders-extra` adds xBRZ, crt-guest-dr-venom,
crt-royale, crt-geom, crt-easymode, zfast-crt and crt-aperture (GPL
licensed, kept as separate files in `shaders/extra/`). Each preset's
`#pragma parameter` settings can be adjusted live in Shader parameters, and
are remembered. `ultracombo --test-shaders` checks that every preset
compiles.

**Lola Retro** (`lola-retro/arcade-15khz`, and `-flat` without curvature)
models a 15 kHz arcade monitor on RGB: the beam, slot mask, glow and curved
glass, built from a real tube's measurements. Its parameters set the colour,
curvature, mask strength, glow and overscan. Set **Around the tube** to 1 to
draw the monitor's casing in a room (2–11: moving scenes), and use the
*stretch* scaling so it fills the window. The tube itself stays 4:3. It is
the heaviest preset: it needs OpenGL 3.3 and a reasonably recent GPU. From
[Lola Retro](https://github.com/zoran123456/lola-retro) by Zoki (MIT); `make
shaders-lola` regenerates it.

Without OpenGL the game falls back to plain SDL drawing (sharp or smooth).

## Training mode

Turn it on with F4 or in Menu → Practice. Health refills a moment after each
combo ends (so you can still read the damage) and the round clock stops.
In Killer Instinct this works on each of a fighter's two health bars.

For a sparring partner, start a two-player game (press 2 to join), then:

1. **F8**: record. Your controls now drive player 2 (up to 10 seconds).
2. **F8**: stop recording.
3. **F9**: the dummy repeats the recording on a loop; F9 again stops it.

Directions are recorded as pressed (left/right on screen), so record from
the side the dummy will be on.

F3 shows both players' recent inputs in numpad notation (6 = forward when
facing right, 2 = down, 5 = neutral) with the number of frames each was held.

## Netplay

Two players over the internet with rollback netcode: your own inputs
respond immediately, the opponent's are predicted and corrected, and the
game stays perfectly in sync. Linux and Windows can play each other.

- **Host:** Menu → Netplay → *Host a game* (or `ultracombo --game ki2
  --host`). Your UDP port (`port` in the game's `.ini`, default 7845) must
  be reachable: forward it on your router, or both use a VPN such as
  Tailscale or ZeroTier.
- **Join:** Menu → Netplay → *Address* (type the host's IP or name), then
  *Join a game* (or `ultracombo --game ki2 --join HOST[:PORT]`).

Both players need the same game, version, ROM and disk image (checked when
connecting); the host's settings sectors and DIP switches are used. When
the other player connects, both games restart at the title screen. You
play with your usual controls whichever side you are on. The corner shows
ping, input delay and the last rollback.

**Input delay** (default 2 frames) trades a little responsiveness for
fewer corrections: 1-2 for nearby players, 3-4 across a continent.
During netplay the game cannot be paused, rewound or reloaded, and both
sides run at the arcade's 58.96 Hz.

## Save states, rewind and run-ahead

States go to `states/slot1.ki1s` … `slot9.ki1s` (Killer Instinct) and
`slot1.ki2s` … `slot9.ki2s` (Killer Instinct 2), about 6 MB each. They
include the disk's settings sectors, and only load into the same build,
game and version.

Rewind keeps about 50 seconds by default (`rewind_mb = 256`).

Killer Instinct 2 shows the result of an input one frame after it reads it.
Run-ahead 1 hides that frame by quietly emulating one frame ahead each frame;
it costs about one extra frame of CPU time. Killer Instinct has no such lag
(a press shows on the very next frame), so run-ahead is off by default for
both, as the arcade played.

Everything above can be changed in the games' `.ini` files, which are
written with comments on first run. They also have video scaling (`fit`,
`integer`, `stretch`), smoothing, frame pacing, audio latency and the boot
skip.

## Frame pacing

The games run at 58.96 Hz. With `pacing = auto` a ~60 Hz display is driven
by vsync for perfectly smooth motion (the game runs 1.7% fast to match);
other refresh rates are timed by the sound card at the original speed.

## Building

Needs gcc, SDL2 and python3:

    make            # ultracombo: both games; their code is built at first launch
    ./ultracombo

For developers, `make recomp` links Killer Instinct 2's translated code into
the program instead (it boots your KI2 files once, about a minute). The
generated C goes to `build/rec/`, derived from your ROM: that binary contains
game code and must not be shared. `tools/regress.sh` runs a fixed scripted
fight and prints a state hash, to check that a change doesn't alter
emulation (see `CLAUDE.md`).

### State file tests

`make test-state-files` runs state-file admission and restoration tests with synthetic RAM,
disk settings and fixed-size device serializers; no SDL or game files are needed.
It checks valid round trips, truncated cores/pages/literals, invalid run lengths,
zero-progress tokens, incompatible headers and trailing data. A rejected file must
leave live memory, devices and rewind history unchanged. The on-disk format is
unchanged. These are file-format tests, not an original-game regression run.

### Controller label tests

`make test-controller-labels` runs controller-label, last-device prompt and configuration tests
without game files. It uses SDL virtual controllers to check both Nintendo mapping
modes, physical south-button activation and its displayed label, manual overrides,
disconnection, axis noise and keyboard/controller prompt switching. Legacy action
bindings must survive configuration load/save unchanged. Physical controller checks
still need real hardware; virtual devices do not establish hardware compatibility.

### Windows

Cross-compiled from Linux with MinGW-w64 (`gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64`) and the
official SDL2 MinGW package, unpacked into `deps/sdl2-mingw/`:

    make windows    # -> dist/windows/UltraCombo.exe

On Windows each game's log goes to `ki1.log` / `ki2.log` beside the
executable. Linux and Windows builds emulate identically (same state after
the same inputs).

### Release packages

    make packages   # -> dist/UltraCombo-Windows.zip, dist/UltraCombo-Linux.tar.xz,
                    #    dist/UltraCombo-x86_64.AppImage and its .zsync

These hold the program, Zig and TinyCC, SDL2 (Linux: in `lib/`), shaders and
licences: no game files and no game code. They expect, in `deps/`:

- Zig 0.17 for Linux and Windows (`zig-linux/`, `zig-windows/`);
- TinyCC's `libtcc.so` built with that Zig against glibc 2.31
  (`tcc-lnx231/`), and `libtcc.dll` (`tcc-win/`);
- SDL2 2.32.10 built with that Zig against glibc 2.31 into
  `deps/sdl2-lnx/build` (configure with
  `-DCMAKE_LIBRARY_ARCHITECTURE=x86_64-linux-gnu` and `-idirafter
  /usr/include` so it finds the X11/Wayland/audio headers);
- the SDL2 MinGW package (`sdl2-mingw/`);
- AppImage's static runtime (`dl/appimage-runtime/runtime-x86_64`, from
  github.com/AppImage/type2-runtime).

The Linux program is built with Zig against glibc 2.31, so it runs on
distributions from about 2020 on. The AppImage is the Linux package packed
with `mksquashfs` behind that runtime.

The AppImage carries update information for AppImageUpdate: the newest
GitHub release, pre-release or not, and its `UltraCombo-x86_64.AppImage.zsync`.
`zsyncmake` makes that file (package `zsync`; without root, `apt-get download
zsync` and `dpkg-deb -x` it into `deps/zsync`); upload it to every release
next to the AppImage, or updating breaks.

route.title: Attach only this prepared game
route.instruction: Select UltraCombo.exe, use the complete extracted UltraCombo-Windows directory as working directory and set arguments to --game ki2. This documented selector binds this record even if both games are installed. Review the exact intent and request Play separately. The selected normal game continues in the same player. Change game restarts the program and removes the selector; finish game changes outside the attached attempt instead of assuming successor tracking. Do not use --write-raw, --recomp, headless, tracing or network-host commands as normal Play.

source_setup.title: Prepare this exact arcade set upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete UltraCombo copy and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own kinst2 arcade set. Supply ki2-l14.u98 (524,288 bytes, SHA1 aa7a2a9d72a47dd0ea2ee7b2776b79288060b179), the eight sound ROMs ki2_l1.u10 through ki2_l1.u13 and ki2_l1.u33 through ki2_l1.u36, and kinst2.chd. The CHD content SHA1 reported by chdman info is e7c9291b4648eae0012ea0cc230731ed4987d1d5; it is not the SHA1 of the compressed container. Keep the full originals independently. The accepted boot revision is L1.4; the first game and its ROMs are not substitutes.

persistence.title: Preserve this game and revision separately
persistence.instruction: Keep ki2.ini, saves/<boot-ROM-name>.settings with disk settings/audits/high scores, states/slot1.ki2s through slot9.ki2s, logs, screenshots, cache/ and the originals. The player normally writes beside the executable when writable, otherwise under %APPDATA%/UltraCombo; preserve the actual active root, external paths and any former writable-directory data. CHD/raw originals are now read-only, but an older played-on raw disk can carry settings that upstream copies into the separate settings file. States are accepted only for the same build/game/version and are distinct from cabinet settings sectors. This guide performs no conversion, migration, backup or deletion.

limitations: Keep the kinst2 originals, active data root and per-version settings/states. First-use compilation, game switching and netplay remain upstream-owned operations.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Review official player setup and data/persistence boundaries for the specific offered route; metadata alone does not qualify execution.

packaged_documentation.UltraCombo-Windows/shaders/README.txt:
Shader presets for the Filter / Shader option, in libretro's GLSL format.

Bundled here, from https://github.com/libretro/glsl-shaders (licence headers
kept in each file):
  crt/crt-lottes*        public domain (Timothy Lottes)
  crt/crt-hyllian*       MIT (Hyllian)
  crt/crt-nobody         MIT
  crt/crt-1tap, 2tap     public domain
  scalefx/               MIT (Sp00kyFox)
  xbr/                   MIT (Hyllian)

lola-retro/ is Lola Retro's arcade-15khz preset (MIT, Zoki; licence in that
folder), from https://github.com/zoran123456/lola-retro. Its slang passes are
converted to GLSL by its own tools/make_glsl.py, through tools/lola_retro.py
(`make shaders-lola`). The files are generated, so don't edit them.

`make shaders-extra` installs more into shaders/extra/: xBRZ, crt-guest,
crt-royale, crt-geom, crt-easymode, zfast-crt and crt-aperture. Those are
GPL-licensed; they are separate files read at run time, and keep their
licence headers. Any other libretro .glslp preset works too: put it (with
the files it uses) anywhere under this folder.
packaged_documentation.UltraCombo-Windows/README.md:
# UltraCombo

Native PC ports of the Killer Instinct arcade games, for Windows and Linux:

| | Plays | MAME set | Versions |
|---|---|---|---|
| **UltraCombo** | Killer Instinct (1994) | `kinst` | L1.5D (default), L1.4 |
| **UltraCombo 2** | Killer Instinct 2 (1996) | `kinst2` | L1.4 |

Both are one program. It runs the arcade games' own code, translated to C
for your PC, with the board around it emulated: the Midway DCS sound board
and the IDE hard disk. On top come the things a home version needs: shaders
and CRT looks, rebindable controls and gamepads, save states, rewind,
run-ahead, training mode and rollback netplay.

**No game files are included.** You need your own copies of the arcade
games' files: the ROMs and the hard disk image (CHD) of MAME's sets.

## Setup

Put the files of one game or both in `run/`, the files of MAME's sets as
they come:

**Killer Instinct** (`kinst`):

- `ki-l15d.u98`: boot ROM, version L1.5D; `ki-l14.u98` (L1.4) is optional
- `u10-l1` … `u13-l1`, `u33-l1` … `u36-l1`: sound ROMs
- `kinst.chd`: the hard disk

**Killer Instinct 2** (`kinst2`):

- `ki2-l14.u98`: boot ROM, version L1.4
- `ki2_l1.u10` … `ki2_l1.u13`, `ki2_l1.u33` … `ki2_l1.u36`: sound ROMs
- `kinst2.chd`: the hard disk

The two games' file names don't clash. A CHD can also sit in a folder named
after its set (`run/kinst/kinst.chd`, `run/kinst2/kinst2.chd`), the way MAME
keeps it. A raw disk image (`kinst.raw`, `kinst2.raw`, from `chdman
extractraw`) works too, and is used if both are there. Each game's file
paths can also be set in its settings file (`ki1.ini`, `ki2.ini`).

The disk images are only ever read. A game's settings, audits and high
scores (the first 32 KB of its disk) go to `saves/<boot ROM>.settings`, one
file per game version. A raw image that an earlier version of this program
wrote to keeps its settings: they are copied into that file on the first
launch. `ultracombo --game ki2 --write-raw kinst2.raw` writes a disk out as
a raw image, the same as `chdman extractraw`, if you ever need one.

### Checking your files

These are the files of MAME's `kinst` and `kinst2` sets (the dumps MAME
lists as good). At startup the program compares your files with them and
warns, naming the file, if one doesn't match. To check them yourself use
`md5sum` (Linux), `certutil -hashfile FILE MD5` (Windows) or any ROM
manager. Every ROM is 524,288 bytes.

### Starting

Start `ultracombo` (`UltraCombo.exe` on Windows; the AppImage on Linux).
With both games installed it asks which to play: left/right (or a click)
chooses, Enter or the controller select button starts (shown on screen).
It remembers the last choice. With one game installed it starts that one
straight away. Menu → **Change game** goes back
to the choice, and `--game ki1` or `--game ki2` skips it (for shortcuts).

The first time you play each game, and each version of it, the program shows
"PREPARING THE GAME FOR THIS PC": it boots your game files on its
interpreter until the game has loaded its code, snapshots that code,
translates it to C, along with the sound board's DSP program from the sound
ROMs, and compiles it into a native module. That takes about a
minute, once; the module is cached in `cache/` (a new one is made if the
game files change). The compiler used is the first that works of:

1. Zig, bundled in `tools/zig`, which the release packages include
2. a C compiler already installed (`cc`, `gcc` or `clang`)
3. TinyCC, bundled in `tools/tcc`: it builds in seconds, but its code runs
   at roughly half the speed (still well above full speed on most PCs)

If none works the game runs on the interpreter, with a warning; see
`build.log` in `cache/src-*/`. All three produce code that behaves
identically, so netplay works between them.

Settings (`ki1.ini`, `ki2.ini`), the games' saves, the logs, screenshots,
states and the cache are written next to the program if that folder is
writable, else into the user data folder (`%APPDATA%\UltraCombo\` on
Windows, `~/.local/share/UltraCombo/` on Linux), whose `run/` folder is also
searched for the game files. With the AppImage, make a `run/` folder beside
the `.AppImage`: the game files go in it, and settings and the cache go
beside the AppImage too.

## Controls

| Action | Player 1 | Player 2 | Pad (Xbox names) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Move | Arrow keys | I J K L | D-pad / left stick |
| Quick / Medium / Fierce punch | A S D | T Y U | X / Y / RB |
| Quick / Medium / Fierce kick | Z X C | G H B | A / B / RT |
| Start | 1 | 2 | Start |
| Coin | 5 | 6 | Back |

The games run in **free play** by default (the board's coinage DIP
switch): from the attract demo, the first Start goes to the title screen
and the second starts the game, as on a free-play cabinet. In UltraCombo 2,
with free play off, `auto_coin` makes Start insert the coins it needs. The
first pad connected is player 1, the second player 2.

| Hotkey | |
|---|---|
| Esc or F1 | Menu (pad: Guide, or Back+Start) |
| F5 / F7 | Save / load state in the current slot |
| F6 | Next state slot (1-9) |
| Backspace (hold) | Rewind |
| Tab (hold) | Fast-forward |
| P | Pause |
| . | Frame advance (pauses first) |
| F11 or Alt+Enter | Fullscreen |
| F12 | Screenshot to `screenshots/` |
| F3 | Input display |
| F4 | Training mode |
| F8 / F9 | Record / play the training dummy |
| F10 | Performance overlay |
| = / - / M | Volume up / down / mute |
| F2 | Operator test menu |
| 9 | Service credit |
| Page Up / Page Down | The cabinet's own volume buttons |

Each game keeps its own settings; changes made in the menu are saved to its
`.ini` file when the menu closes.

## The menu

**Graphics:** fullscreen (borderless, or exclusive at a chosen display
mode), window size, scaling (fit 4:3, integer, stretch), shader, shader
parameters, frame pacing and the performance overlay.

**Controls:** rebind both players' keys, the gamepad buttons and all hotkeys
(select one, press the new key or button; Backspace unbinds). Also there:
**left+right = neutral** (SOCD cleaning, on by default: left and right
together count as neither, up and down together as up, like fight sticks),
**rumble** when your character is hit, and the stick deadzone.

**Game & system:**

- **Game version** (Killer Instinct: L1.5D or L1.4, when both boot ROMs are
  there): pick it, then Enter switches. That resets the game, like swapping
  the ROM on the cabinet; each version keeps its own settings and high
  scores. L1.4 is the original release, with the bugs and infinite combos
  that L1.5D fixed.
- **CPU difficulty** (Extra easy to Extra hard): written to the disk's
  adjustments exactly as the game's operator menu does, so it applies after
  Reset.
- **Free play, blood level, finishing moves, attract-mode sound** and, in
  Killer Instinct, **blood colour** (red or white): the board's DIP
  switches, read at power-on, so they apply after Reset.
- Volume, mute or pause in the background, auto-coin (UltraCombo 2),
  run-ahead and rewind.

Button labels follow the last controller used; keyboard input switches menu
prompts back to keyboard names. Xbox, PlayStation and Nintendo Switch layouts
are detected through SDL. Before a controller is used, and for controllers
SDL cannot identify, labels fall back to Xbox-style A/B/X/Y names. Controls →
P1/P2 button labels overrides the detected family when an adapter hides it;
Positions remains available for South/East/West/North names. This changes
labels only, not the bindings. SDL's Nintendo letter-based and positional
mappings are both respected, including the exchanged A/B and X/Y positions.
The shared gamepad-binding page shows labels for the last pad used.

The window's size and position are remembered between runs.

## Graphics

**Shaders** are drawn by the GPU. Four are built in:

- **Sharp**: crisp pixels, evenly sized at any window size
- **Smooth**: sharpened bicubic; suits the games' pre-rendered 3D art
- **Scanlines**, **CRT**: simple, fast CRT looks

Any **libretro GLSL preset** (`.glslp`, the format of RetroArch's shader
collection) under `shaders/` works too, multi-pass presets, lookup
textures and all. Bundled: crt-lottes, crt-hyllian, crt-nobody, crt-1tap/2tap,
ScaleFX and xBR. `make shaders-extra` adds xBRZ, crt-guest-dr-venom,
crt-royale, crt-geom, crt-easymode, zfast-crt and crt-aperture (GPL
licensed, kept as separate files in `shaders/extra/`). Each preset's
`#pragma parameter` settings can be adjusted live in Shader parameters, and
are remembered. `ultracombo --test-shaders` checks that every preset
compiles.

**Lola Retro** (`lola-retro/arcade-15khz`, and `-flat` without curvature)
models a 15 kHz arcade monitor on RGB: the beam, slot mask, glow and curved
glass, built from a real tube's measurements. Its parameters set the colour,
curvature, mask strength, glow and overscan. Set **Around the tube** to 1 to
draw the monitor's casing in a room (2–11: moving scenes), and use the
*stretch* scaling so it fills the window. The tube itself stays 4:3. It is
the heaviest preset: it needs OpenGL 3.3 and a reasonably recent GPU. From
[Lola Retro](https://github.com/zoran123456/lola-retro) by Zoki (MIT); `make
shaders-lola` regenerates it.

Without OpenGL the game falls back to plain SDL drawing (sharp or smooth).

## Training mode

Turn it on with F4 or in Menu → Practice. Health refills a moment after each
combo ends (so you can still read the damage) and the round clock stops.
In Killer Instinct this works on each of a fighter's two health bars.

For a sparring partner, start a two-player game (press 2 to join), then:

1. **F8**: record. Your controls now drive player 2 (up to 10 seconds).
2. **F8**: stop recording.
3. **F9**: the dummy repeats the recording on a loop; F9 again stops it.

Directions are recorded as pressed (left/right on screen), so record from
the side the dummy will be on.

F3 shows both players' recent inputs in numpad notation (6 = forward when
facing right, 2 = down, 5 = neutral) with the number of frames each was held.

## Netplay

Two players over the internet with rollback netcode: your own inputs
respond immediately, the opponent's are predicted and corrected, and the
game stays perfectly in sync. Linux and Windows can play each other.

- **Host:** Menu → Netplay → *Host a game* (or `ultracombo --game ki2
  --host`). Your UDP port (`port` in the game's `.ini`, default 7845) must
  be reachable: forward it on your router, or both use a VPN such as
  Tailscale or ZeroTier.
- **Join:** Menu → Netplay → *Address* (type the host's IP or name), then
  *Join a game* (or `ultracombo --game ki2 --join HOST[:PORT]`).

Both players need the same game, version, ROM and disk image (checked when
connecting); the host's settings sectors and DIP switches are used. When
the other player connects, both games restart at the title screen. You
play with your usual controls whichever side you are on. The corner shows
ping, input delay and the last rollback.

**Input delay** (default 2 frames) trades a little responsiveness for
fewer corrections: 1-2 for nearby players, 3-4 across a continent.
During netplay the game cannot be paused, rewound or reloaded, and both
sides run at the arcade's 58.96 Hz.

## Save states, rewind and run-ahead

States go to `states/slot1.ki1s` … `slot9.ki1s` (Killer Instinct) and
`slot1.ki2s` … `slot9.ki2s` (Killer Instinct 2), about 6 MB each. They
include the disk's settings sectors, and only load into the same build,
game and version.

Rewind keeps about 50 seconds by default (`rewind_mb = 256`).

Killer Instinct 2 shows the result of an input one frame after it reads it.
Run-ahead 1 hides that frame by quietly emulating one frame ahead each frame;
it costs about one extra frame of CPU time. Killer Instinct has no such lag
(a press shows on the very next frame), so run-ahead is off by default for
both, as the arcade played.

Everything above can be changed in the games' `.ini` files, which are
written with comments on first run. They also have video scaling (`fit`,
`integer`, `stretch`), smoothing, frame pacing, audio latency and the boot
skip.

## Frame pacing

The games run at 58.96 Hz. With `pacing = auto` a ~60 Hz display is driven
by vsync for perfectly smooth motion (the game runs 1.7% fast to match);
other refresh rates are timed by the sound card at the original speed.

## Building

Needs gcc, SDL2 and python3:

    make            # ultracombo: both games; their code is built at first launch
    ./ultracombo

For developers, `make recomp` links Killer Instinct 2's translated code into
the program instead (it boots your KI2 files once, about a minute). The
generated C goes to `build/rec/`, derived from your ROM: that binary contains
game code and must not be shared. `tools/regress.sh` runs a fixed scripted
fight and prints a state hash, to check that a change doesn't alter
emulation (see `CLAUDE.md`).

### State file tests

`make test-state-files` runs state-file admission and restoration tests with synthetic RAM,
disk settings and fixed-size device serializers; no SDL or game files are needed.
It checks valid round trips, truncated cores/pages/literals, invalid run lengths,
zero-progress tokens, incompatible headers and trailing data. A rejected file must
leave live memory, devices and rewind history unchanged. The on-disk format is
unchanged. These are file-format tests, not an original-game regression run.

### Controller label tests

`make test-controller-labels` runs controller-label, last-device prompt and configuration tests
without game files. It uses SDL virtual controllers to check both Nintendo mapping
modes, physical south-button activation and its displayed label, manual overrides,
disconnection, axis noise and keyboard/controller prompt switching. Legacy action
bindings must survive configuration load/save unchanged. Physical controller checks
still need real hardware; virtual devices do not establish hardware compatibility.

### Windows

Cross-compiled from Linux with MinGW-w64 (`gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64`) and the
official SDL2 MinGW package, unpacked into `deps/sdl2-mingw/`:

    make windows    # -> dist/windows/UltraCombo.exe

On Windows each game's log goes to `ki1.log` / `ki2.log` beside the
executable. Linux and Windows builds emulate identically (same state after
the same inputs).

### Release packages

    make packages   # -> dist/UltraCombo-Windows.zip, dist/UltraCombo-Linux.tar.xz,
                    #    dist/UltraCombo-x86_64.AppImage and its .zsync

These hold the program, Zig and TinyCC, SDL2 (Linux: in `lib/`), shaders and
licences: no game files and no game code. They expect, in `deps/`:

- Zig 0.17 for Linux and Windows (`zig-linux/`, `zig-windows/`);
- TinyCC's `libtcc.so` built with that Zig against glibc 2.31
  (`tcc-lnx231/`), and `libtcc.dll` (`tcc-win/`);
- SDL2 2.32.10 built with that Zig against glibc 2.31 into
  `deps/sdl2-lnx/build` (configure with
  `-DCMAKE_LIBRARY_ARCHITECTURE=x86_64-linux-gnu` and `-idirafter
  /usr/include` so it finds the X11/Wayland/audio headers);
- the SDL2 MinGW package (`sdl2-mingw/`);
- AppImage's static runtime (`dl/appimage-runtime/runtime-x86_64`, from
  github.com/AppImage/type2-runtime).

The Linux program is built with Zig against glibc 2.31, so it runs on
distributions from about 2020 on. The AppImage is the Linux package packed
with `mksquashfs` behind that runtime.

The AppImage carries update information for AppImageUpdate: the newest
GitHub release, pre-release or not, and its `UltraCombo-x86_64.AppImage.zsync`.
`zsyncmake` makes that file (package `zsync`; without root, `apt-get download
zsync` and `dpkg-deb -x` it into `deps/zsync`); upload it to every release
next to the AppImage, or updating breaks.

route.title: Attach only this prepared game
route.instruction: Select UltraCombo.exe, use the complete extracted UltraCombo-Windows directory as working directory and set arguments to --game ki1. This documented selector binds this record even if both games are installed. Review the exact intent and request Play separately. The selected normal game continues in the same player. Change game restarts the program and removes the selector; finish game changes outside the attached attempt instead of assuming successor tracking. Do not use --write-raw, --recomp, headless, tracing or network-host commands as normal Play.

source_setup.title: Prepare this exact arcade set upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete UltraCombo copy and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own kinst arcade set. Supply ki-l15d.u98 (524,288 bytes, SHA1 607394d4ba1713f38c2cb5159303cace9cde991e), the eight sound ROMs u10-l1 through u13-l1 and u33-l1 through u36-l1, and kinst.chd. The CHD content SHA1 reported by chdman info is 81d833236e994528d1482979261401b198d1ca53; it is not the SHA1 of the compressed container. Keep the full originals independently. Killer Instinct also supports optional L1.4 boot ki-l14.u98, SHA1 07254f20707377f7195e64675eb6458e663c1a9a; its settings and compatibility remain separate.

persistence.title: Preserve this game and revision separately
persistence.instruction: Keep ki1.ini, saves/<boot-ROM-name>.settings with disk settings/audits/high scores, states/slot1.ki1s through slot9.ki1s, logs, screenshots, cache/ and the originals. The player normally writes beside the executable when writable, otherwise under %APPDATA%/UltraCombo; preserve the actual active root, external paths and any former writable-directory data. CHD/raw originals are now read-only, but an older played-on raw disk can carry settings that upstream copies into the separate settings file. States are accepted only for the same build/game/version and are distinct from cabinet settings sectors. This guide performs no conversion, migration, backup or deletion.

limitations: Keep the kinst originals, active data root and per-version settings/states. First-use compilation, game switching and netplay remain upstream-owned operations.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Which USA/Europe default.xbe revisions and digests does the selected Xbox setup accept?

pe_prefix.scope: bounded header only; no execution, complete imports, ABI or dependency resolution

glslang 15.4.0 (https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glslang)
glslang compiles the Vulkan renderer's shaders to SPIR-V at runtime.
The license text of the glslang repository follows unchanged.

Here, glslang proper means core GLSL parsing, HLSL parsing, and SPIR-V code
generation. Glslang proper requires use of a number of licenses, one that covers
preprocessing and others that covers non-preprocessing.

Bison was removed long ago. You can build glslang from the source grammar,
using tools of your choice, without using bison or any bison files.

Other parts, outside of glslang proper, include:

- gl_types.h, only needed for OpenGL-like reflection, and can be left out of
  a parse and codegen project.  See it for its license.

- update_glslang_sources.py, which is not part of the project proper and does
  not need to be used.

- the SPIR-V "remapper", which is optional, but has the same license as
  glslang proper

- Google tests and SPIR-V tools, and anything in the external subdirectory
  are external and optional; see them for their respective licenses.

packaged_documentation.readme.txt:
OpenShao
A native PC port of Mortal Kombat: Shaolin Monks.

The game is not included. You need your own USA/Europe Xbox copy.


REQUIREMENTS

- Windows 10 1903 or later, or Linux with glibc 2.38 or later
- x64 CPU with SSE4.2 and POPCNT
- Direct3D 12 GPU, or Vulkan 1.2 with dynamic rendering and timeline semaphores


GETTING STARTED

1. Open OpenShao.
2. Choose your game: an ISO, XISO, ZIP, extracted folder or default.xbe.
3. Select Play.

Keep the game image or folder where it is. OpenShao reads it in place.
On Windows, choose Direct3D 12 or Vulkan under Graphics API on the launcher's Play page.
Direct3D 12 is the default. Linux uses Vulkan.


UPDATES

The launcher checks for a new version when it opens. Select Update to install it.
Saves, settings and mods are kept.
To turn off the check, open Files and clear Updates.

To update manually, download the package for your system and extract it to a new folder:
Windows: OpenShao-<version>-Windows-x64.zip
Linux:   OpenShao-<version>-Linux-x64.tar.gz
https://github.com/OAleex/OpenShao/releases/latest


SETTINGS AND CONTROLS

Game settings are in Konfigure Recompilation, in the main menu and in the SELECT pause menu.
With V-Sync enabled, Graphics targets the current monitor's refresh rate. With V-Sync disabled, choose 60 or 120 FPS. Simulation stays at 60 Hz.
In the main menu's Enhancements, Cinematic Bars adds animated black bands to in-game cutscenes. It is off by default.
Solo campaign health, combo counters, multipliers and praise follow the upper-left screen corner. Tutorial panels, text and confirmation prompts follow the bottom edge without stretching the artwork.
The achieved frame rate depends on performance and the display's refresh rate when V-Sync is enabled.
The pause menu lists Continue, Options, Konfigure Recompilation, Exit Game and Exit to Desktop. Exit Game returns to the main menu.
Mods and language packs are in the launcher's Mods page.

In Ko-op, use keyboard and mouse for player 1 and one controller for player 2, or use two controllers.
If player 1's controller disconnects, the keyboard and mouse take over player 1.
Connected controllers keep their player slots. A replacement fills an empty slot.
Any connected controller can navigate Konfigure Recompilation and remap controls.
In Versus, Start skips character introductions. Release it before pressing Start again to pause.

F9   show the version and frame rate
F10  release or capture the mouse

If the game does not start after a display change, open the launcher and select Files > Video > Restore.


FOLDERS

Open Files in the launcher to open or move your saves and data.
Diagnostic ZIP files are stored in the data folder under reports.


KNOWN ISSUES

Most graphical issues have been fixed, but some can still appear.
Any problem is worth reporting. Open an issue with a screenshot: https://github.com/OAleex/OpenShao/issues
Mortal Kombat II and The Suffering demo do not run.
Supported asset pipelines are prepared while an area loads, including on the first run.
Common menu, particle and screen-effect pipelines are prepared when their shaders load.
Other effects can still pause briefly on first use. Observed pipelines are reused in later sessions.


HELP

Project page: https://github.com/OAleex/OpenShao
Open Support in the launcher and select Generate report.
Select Report a bug to open GitHub.
Attach the diagnostic ZIP and describe how to reproduce the problem.

Reports include up to three session logs, selected settings and installed mod versions.
Manual reports also include the latest completed crash dump when available.
Automatic crash reports include the dump captured for that crash when one can be created.
New session logs and exported text logs filter account and computer names, personal paths, network addresses and credentials.
ZIP reports exclude saves, game files and screenshots. Nothing is uploaded automatically.

After an unexpected launcher or game exit, a separate process creates the crash ZIP immediately.
The error message shows the ZIP location. Select OK to open its folder.
Reopening the launcher is not required to create the crash report.

Development uses AI assistance. The maintainer reviews every change.

Code license: GPL-2.0-or-later. See licenses/LICENSE.txt and the other notices in licenses/.
The license does not cover the original game or its assets.

route.title: Attach the remembered-source player
route.instruction: After setup, select OpenShao.exe, set the complete extracted package directory as working directory and use the documented --no-launcher argument. Review the intent and request Play separately. The host uses its remembered game-source.toml selection and the linked game; finish any missing/invalid-source prompt, update, mod installation or restart upstream before retrying. Mortal Kombat II and The Suffering demo are explicitly unsupported; this guide does not admit them.

source_setup.title: Prepare the supported original upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player and components you are independently permitted to use, with your own USA/Europe Xbox Mortal Kombat: Shaolin Monks, title 4D570029. The selected profile identifies entry 000F40CA and XDK 5849. The runtime compares default.xbe SHA1 against the exact original used when that player was built; CMake generates that constant from the build input. Its actual release-input SHA1 is not published in the reviewed profile, so an exact independently established release digest remains Unknown. Do not replace this check with a title-name assumption or mismatch bypass. Finish upstream game selection/validation before attachment.

persistence.instruction: Normally keep %LOCALAPPDATA%/OpenShao for settings.toml, game-source.toml, paths.toml, logs, cache, crashes, reports and mods, and the actual Windows Saved Games/OpenShao directory for saves. Known folders may be relocated. The Files page can move data and saves independently; an existing --data-dir, --save-dir or --portable-saves changes the layout. Preserve every actual root, locator, original and older named folder before the first 0.3+ startup: upstream can move eligible legacy data/saves and rewrite their paths. This guide performs no migration, restore, backup or deletion.

limitations: The exact release-input XBE SHA1 remains Unknown. Keep both data and Saved Games roots plus legacy recovery; unsupported bundled demos are not admitted.

packaged_documentation.defaults/narutorise.toml:
# narutorise - immutable factory template; copied once to the active data folder.
# Select the data folder in Settings > Advanced or with --data_root / REX_DATA_ROOT.
# Runtime preferences are read from that folder, never written to this template.
# dlc_source_path = "dlc" uses data/dlc; "" disables scanning.
# Custom user_data_root selects the exact guest content tree, with no saves/ suffix.

gpu_plugin = "xenos"
# Renderer: "native" (the default) or "xenos" (the emulated GPU),
# in builds with the native renderer; builds without it always use Xenos.
# Linux builds have only the native renderer.
renderer = "native"
# Show the initial menu before the game. Can be changed under Settings > Advanced.
show_startup_menu = true
# Native graphics API: "d3d12" or "vulkan" when included in the build.
# Omit to use D3D12, or Vulkan in a Vulkan-only build (Linux). Fixed for the
# session.
# native_backend = "d3d12"
# Graphics card by its name as the system lists it, for both renderers;
# empty = automatic.
graphics_device = ""
d3d12_readback_resolve = true
skip_intro_videos = true

# Optional uploads of native crash dumps, technical details and startup timing.
# Dumps may contain personal data. Saves and game files are never attached.
# Asked over the first frame of the game, then crash_reporting_asked = true.
# Also available in Settings > Advanced; enabling there after a refusal needs a restart.
crash_reporting = false

# Game language: 1 = English, 4 = French, 3 = German, 5 = Spanish, 6 = Italian.
user_language = 1
# Folder under mods/ in the active data folder. Example: "pt-br-demo".
# Translation mods currently use English as their base; restart after changing.
translation_mod = ""

# Fix da piscada preta nas lutas: draws fullscreen sem clipping fazem o
# estimador de EDRAM alegar o EDRAM inteiro e corromper o buffer de cena via
# transferencias de ownership (default do SDK agora tambem e true).
execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu = true

log_verbose = false
log_level = "info"

protect_zero = false

input_backend = "sdl"
# Keyboard and mouse as a controller, next to a connected one. While exploring,
# the mouse turns the camera itself at mnk_sensitivity (1.0 = 100%, about one
# turn every 2,100 pixels); elsewhere it stands in for the right stick.
mnk_mode = false
mnk_mouse = true
mnk_sensitivity = 1.0
# Keys of each controller input: alternatives separated by commas, with the
# SDK's key names (LMB, RMB and MMB for the mouse buttons). Shift, Control and
# Alt can be keys of their own. Configure them under Settings > Controls.
keybind_a = "Space"
keybind_b = "E,Backspace"
keybind_x = "LMB,J"
keybind_y = "RMB,K"
keybind_left_shoulder = "Q"
keybind_right_shoulder = "R"
keybind_left_trigger = "Control"
keybind_right_trigger = "Shift"
keybind_lstick_press = "C"
keybind_rstick_press = "MMB,V"
keybind_start = "Return,Escape"
keybind_back = "Tab"
keybind_lstick_up = "W"
keybind_lstick_down = "S"
keybind_lstick_left = "A"
keybind_lstick_right = "D"
keybind_rstick_up = "Up"
keybind_rstick_down = "Down"
keybind_rstick_left = "Left"
keybind_rstick_right = "Right"
keybind_dpad_up = "1,Numpad8"
keybind_dpad_down = "2,Numpad2"
keybind_dpad_left = "3,Numpad4"
keybind_dpad_right = "4,Numpad6"
keybind_guide = ""

fullscreen = true
vsync = true
d3d12_host_vsync = true
video_mode_refresh_rate = 60.0
resolution_scale = 1
draw_resolution_scale_x = 1
draw_resolution_scale_y = 1
d3d12_allow_variable_refresh_rate_and_tearing = true

anisotropic_override = 5

swap_post_effect = "fxaa"
present_effect = "cas"
present_dither = false

show_fps_overlay = false

# Native renderer only (ignored by the Xenos renderer).
# msaa_samples: 0 = the game's 4x, or 2, 4, 8.
msaa_samples = 0
transparency_antialiasing = false
# Frame rate: 30 keeps the game's; 60 to 240 keep the game's logic at its own
# step and interpolate the frames in between.
frame_rate = 60
# 0.5 = the game's brightness.
brightness = 0.5
# Fractional internal scale (1.5 = 1920x1080); 0 = resolution_scale.
internal_resolution_scale = 0.0
max_frame_latency = 1
triple_buffering = false

# Anamorphic Ultrawide (Hells Gate / Xenia Canary style patch).
# 0.0 = native 16:9; 2.3889 = 21:9 (3440x1440); 3.5556 = 32:9.
ultrawide_target_aspect = 0.0

# Menu language: "en" (default), "pt_BR", "fr", "de", "es", "it", "ru".
launcher_language = "en"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Optional: Title Update (TU) folder.
# The SDK mounts this path as "update:\". Some games use it to patch the
# default.xex or game files. Place the extracted Title Update files in a
# "title_update" folder next to your game data, or set the path below.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# update_data_root = "C:/Games/Naruto - Rise of a Ninja/title_update"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Optional: Custom game data: the folder with the extracted files, or the disc
# image itself (.iso, read in place).
# If empty, detect game/ or game_root/ beside the distribution (the external AppImage on Linux).
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# custom_game_root = "C:/Games/Naruto - Rise of a Ninja/game"
# custom_game_root = "C:/Games/Naruto - Rise of a Ninja.iso"
