packaged_documentation.README.txt:
NARUTO: RISE OF A NINJA - PC PORT (0.4.2-beta)

FIRST LAUNCH:
Extract the ZIP to a writable folder and run narutorise.exe.
Choose your original Xbox 360 ISO or the default.xex of a complete extracted
copy. The ISO is read directly; no extraction or installer is needed.
Later launches follow the Show menu at startup preference. Hold Shift while opening, or use
narutorise.exe --setup, to return to the setup screen.

IN GAME:
Press F1 or Back+Start to open Settings, DLC and Exit game.
These shortcuts can be remapped under Controls. The game keeps running while
the menu is open, with game input blocked. Show FPS is a menu option.
Settings include Game, Display, Quality, Controls and Advanced, in seven
interface languages. Graphics options that require a restart are labelled.
Create a desktop shortcut from Settings > Advanced.

UPDATES:
The game notifies you about new releases and opens the release page.
Close the game and extract the new ZIP over the existing package files.
Keep data/ and data_location.json, game/, game_root/ and community mods.
The ZIP contains only defaults/narutorise.toml; your active settings, logs,
saves, mods and DLC packages live in data/. Settings > Advanced shows the active
folder and can select another location after restart. Explicit user_data_root
continues to select its exact save/content folder, without a saves/ suffix.
The first launch copies eligible legacy data and keeps the originals. Back up
the active data folder and any explicit save/content folder before updating.
If import reports a conflict, preserve both copies and resolve the differing
files before retrying. Do not delete .narutorise-migration metadata.
The old narutorise_launcher.exe from a portable copy can be deleted manually.
Registered 0.3.0 installations can use the separately distributed
NarutoRiseInstaller.exe bridge. It replaces shortcuts and removes the launcher
while preserving game data and configuration. Later updates use the ZIP.

TRANSLATIONS:
Brazilian Portuguese is bundled as an immutable seed in defaults\mods\pt-br.
First launch copies it to the active data folder's mods\pt-br if absent,
after importing eligible legacy mods. Select it under Settings > Game > Game
language. Updates and rebuilds preserve active mods, including customized or
partial PT-BR packages. To update a translation, back it up and merge the new
defaults deliberately. The selected language stays in the active TOML.

Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 Redistributable (x64) is required.
Alt+F4 closes the game.

Game files are not included. License and third-party notices: licenses\README.txt.

packaged_documentation.rsc2-windows-x64/README.txt:
RalliSport Challenge 2 - static recompilation, Windows x64 build (v0.6.0)

NO GAME DATA IS INCLUDED. You need your own copy of the game.

1. Put your game files (the folder with default.xbe, Layer0, Layer1, Media,
   Movies, ...) in a folder called "game" next to rsc2.exe.
2. Run rsc2.exe. The launcher opens first; settings are saved to
   %APPDATA%\rsc2\settings.ini.

Requirements: Windows 10 or 11 x64 and a GPU driver with Vulkan 1.3
(current NVIDIA, AMD and Intel drivers include vulkan-1.dll). Nothing else:
the runtime, glslang and SDL2 are built in.

Keys: the keyboard is set up for driving. Left/Right steer, Up/Down
accelerate and brake, Space e-brake, A/Z gear up/down, C camera, V look
back, R car reset, H horn, Esc pauses (and goes back in menus), Enter
accepts. Change any of them in the launcher (Controls > Key bindings).
F11 or Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen, F3 the FPS counter. Xbox controllers work through XInput.
Closing the window (or Alt+F4) quits the game.

Wider screens: with the launcher's aspect ratio set to 16:9, the picture
fills screens wider than 16:9 in fullscreen (ultrawide monitors): the view
is widened, not stretched, and the HUD keeps its shape.

The menus run at 60 fps, as on the console; races can go up to the
launcher's frame rate limit. On a display that isn't 60 or 120 Hz the
menus may judder.

HDR: turn on "Use HDR" in Windows display settings, then set the
launcher's Display > HDR to on ("HDR brightness" sets paper white).
Not yet tested on Windows.

Shaders are prepared in the background: the first time a new effect
appears it may briefly be drawn a little differently, and later starts
prepare everything while the intro plays, so races do not stutter.

The launcher's "Add to Steam" button adds the game to your Steam
library as a non-Steam game (quit Steam first).

The game copies some of its files into a cache at every start
(%LOCALAPPDATA%\xboxrecomp\Cache), as it does on the console's hard disk.

This binary contains code translated from the game's executable. It is for
owners of the game; source: https://github.com/Mortify7612/RallisportChallenge2-decomp

Keep the real game/ tree in that CWD. Do not add finite-frame, replay, tracing, Steam-shortcut or compiler actions to normal Play. Review the exact intent and request Play separately.

source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own NTSC Xbox RalliSport Challenge 2, title 4D530039. If LocalAppData cannot be resolved, source falls back to SaveData/ under CWD. This is not a title-specific directory by name: preserve other games already using that root and do not merge or delete it. Keep original data, existing environment overrides, previous CWD data and any external paths. This guide performs no migration, restore, backup or deletion.

packaged_documentation.PointBlank-PC-Port-v1.1.0-windows-x64/RE:
[![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/TekRantGaming/point-blank-recompiled?style=for-the-badge&label=release&color=ff4f9a&labelColor=101433)](https://github.com/TekRantGaming/point-blank-recompiled/releases/latest) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/TekRantGaming/point-blank-recompiled/total?style=for-the-badge&color=2f7bff&labelColor=101433)](https://github.com/TekRantGaming/point-blank-recompiled/releases) ![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platforms-Windows-00acc1?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=101433) ### Namco's Point Blank on PC, running natively. Shoot with your mouse or an Xbox controller, no light gun needed. [](https://github.com/TekRantGaming/point-blank-recompiled/releases/latest) The original PlayStation game code, translated to native PC code with PSXRecomp. No game files included: bring your own disc image of Point Blank (PlayStation, North America, SLUS-00481).

## Highlights
**Aim with your mouse**
The game thinks a real Namco GunCon is plugged in. Point the cursor at the screen and click to shoot, exactly where you aim. 		**Or with a controller**
Xbox, PlayStation and other controllers work too. The sticks move an on-screen sight, and the right trigger fires. 		**Two players**
Plug in a second controller and Player 2 gets their own gun and sight, red against blue, just like the arcade.
**Straight to the action**
The long opening movies are skipped, so the title screen is up in seconds. You can switch them back on in the launcher's Mods list. 		**Native, not emulated**
Every function of the game was translated from PlayStation code to C and compiled for your PC. Your CPU runs the game directly. 		**One-click builder**
Double-click, pick your disc image, and the builder makes the PC version for you. No technical steps.
## In game
**Every mode is here:** Arcade, the console-only **Arrange** mode with its adventure board and side quests, Training, Beginner and Expert stages, and two-player versus.
### Light gun, without the light gun Point Blank was made for Namco's GunCon light gun, which only works on old CRT televisions. This port emulates the GunCon itself: wherever your mouse cursor or controller sight points on the picture becomes the spot the "gun" reports to the game. The game's own gun calibration and menus work as they did on the console.
### Calibration The first time you play, the game asks you to shoot the centre of the screen. Click the middle of the target (or aim the sight there and pull the trigger), then press **A** to finish.
### Controller sight With a controller, a crosshair is drawn over the game so you can see where you are aiming: **red** for Player 1, **blue** for Player 2. Move the mouse and it hands aiming straight back to the cursor.
### Menus Everything is chosen by shooting it, like the original. Shoot **NO** to skip loading a memory card, then **Arcade** or **Arrange**, and pick a difficulty and stage the same way.
## Controls | Action | Mouse | Controller | | --- | --- | --- | | Aim | move the cursor | left stick (fast) or right stick (fine) | | Shoot | left button | right trigger, A or RB | | Shoot off-screen | back side button, or point outside the picture | left trigger or B | | GunCon **A** (start, skip, confirm) | right button | Start or X | | GunCon **B** | middle button | Back or Y | The first controller plays as Player 1 alongside the mouse; a second controller becomes Player 2. Screens that say **Press the button**, such as the rules, want **A**. ## Getting started **You need:** Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), a graphics card with OpenGL 3.3, and your own disc image of **Point Blank (USA)** as a `.cue` with its `.bin` (Redump `Point Blank (USA)`, serial SLUS-00481). 1. Download the **Windows builder** from the [latest release](https://github.com/TekRantGaming/point-blank-recompiled/releases/latest) and unzip it. 2. Double-click **Build Point Blank.bat**. 3. If it asks, let it install the build tools (Visual Studio Build Tools with Clang, CMake, Ninja and Python). This is a one-time download of about 6 GB. 4. Pick your `Point Blank (USA).cue` when asked. The builder checks that it is the right game. 5. Wait while it builds (15 to 30 minutes). The finished game appears in the **PointBlank** folder, with an optional desktop shortcut. **Why a builder and not a ready-made download?** The PC version is made from the game's own code, which belongs to Namco and can't be shared. The builder makes it on your PC from your own disc, so nothing from the game is ever downloaded or uploaded. The game opens with a launcher where you can change the display, controls and mods. Run `PointBlank_Recompiled.exe --no-launcher` to go straight into the game.
Building by hand (for developers) ```powershell git clone --recursive https://github.com/TekRantGaming/point-blank-recompiled.git cd point-blank-recompiled .\Build-PointBlank.ps1 -Cue "C:\path\to\Point Blank (USA).cue" ``` The script loads the Visual Studio environment and then: 1. builds the recompiler: `cmake -S psxrecomp/recompiler -B build-recompiler -G Ninja`, target `psxrecomp-game psxrecomp-bios` 2. translates the game: `python psxrecomp/psxrecomp_cli.py generate --config game.toml --project-root . --disc ` (writes `generated/`, which is never committed) 3. compiles the runtime with `clang-cl` into `build/` (plain MSVC `cl` cannot build the runtime's C11 atomics); after that, `build.bat` rebuilds Game settings live in [`game.toml`](game.toml); `[controller] guncon_ports = [1, 2]` is what plugs in the guns.
## How it works - **[PSXRecomp](https://github.com/mstan/psxrecomp)** reads the game's PlayStation executable and translates its MIPS R3000 machine code into C, about 2,600 functions. That C is compiled into a normal Windows program and linked with a runtime that behaves like the PlayStation hardware (graphics, sound, CD drive, controllers), with the open-source [OpenBIOS](https://github.com/grumpycoders/pcsx-redux) in place of Sony's BIOS. - PSXRecomp had no light-gun support, so this port adds a **Namco GunCon (NPC-103)** to its controller emulation. The gun answers the game with its ID and the screen position where it "saw" the TV's electron beam. The port works that position out from your cursor or sight and the game's own video timing, the same way the [DuckStation](https://github.com/stenzek/duckstation) emulator does. - Port 2's gun only plugs itself in while a second controller is connected, so the game never waits on a calibration screen for a player who isn't there. - The framework changes are on the [`pointblank` branch of TekRantGaming/psxrecomp](https://github.com/TekRantGaming/psxrecomp/tree/pointblank). ## Credits - **Point Blank** (Gunbullet in Japan) by Namco, PlayStation version 1997. - [**PSXRecomp**](https://github.com/mstan/psxrecomp) by Matthew Stanley and the RetroPortingToolkit team, which does the code translation and runs the game, with [**recomp-ui**](https://github.com/RetroPortingToolKit/recomp-ui) for the launcher. - [**OpenBIOS**](https://github.com/grumpycoders/pcsx-redux) from the PCSX-Redux project, [**SDL**](https://www.libsdl.org/) and [**Dear ImGui**](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui). - [**psx-spx**](https://psx-spx.consoledev.net/) for documenting the GunCon. PSXRecomp is under the [PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0](https://github.com/mstan/psxrecomp/blob/master/LICENSE), so this port is for non-commercial use only. > [!NOTE] > **AI disclosure:** this port was made almost entirely with Claude Code (Anthropic). The repository owner directed and tested the work; the AI did the analysis, code, tools and documentation. > [!IMPORTANT] > This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Bandai Namco Entertainment or Sony. It contains no game code or assets. Do not open issues asking for game files.

# Preloaded mods

Ship reviewed, default-disabled packages here:

```text
packages/<package-id>/<version>/
  manifest.toml
  …
```

Build wiring copies `mods/preloaded/packages` next to the game executable as
`mods/bundled/`. That tree is build output: every build wipes and re-stages it,
so nothing you place there by hand survives.

Player-installed `.psxmod` archives live in `mods/installed/`, which the
launcher owns and no build ever touches. Install them through the launcher Mods
manager rather than committing them here.

See `psxrecomp/docs/MOD_PACKAGES.md`.

format_version = 5
id = "pointblank.skip-intro"
version = "1.0.0"
name = "Skip Intro Movies"
author = "PointBlankRecomp"
description = "Skips Point Blank's long opening and attract-mode movies so the game reaches the title screen in seconds."
resolver = "declarative"
save_compatibility = "shared"

[[target]]
game_id = "SLUS-00481"

[[feature]]
id = "skip-intro"
name = "Skip Intro Movies"
description = "Enabled by default. While a movie plays, the runtime holds START (GunCon A), which the game's movie player treats as a skip. Turn this off to watch the intro."
group = "Quality of Life"
default_enabled = true

[[plugin]]
feature = "skip-intro"
id = "pointblank.skip-intro"

format_version = 5
id = "psx.enhancement.8mb-ram"
version = "1.0.0"
name = "8 MB Main RAM"
author = "psxrecomp"
description = "Enables an opt-in 8 MB main RAM map for patches that require expanded PS1 memory. Disabled by default."
resolver = "declarative"
save_compatibility = "shared"

# Main-RAM geometry is a property of the emulated machine, not of any one disc.
# Only patches written for an 8 MB (development-kit sized) RAM need it; stock
# games keep retail 2 MB mirroring with this off.
[[target]]
game_id = "*"

[[feature]]
id = "8mb-ram"
name = "8 MB Main RAM"
description = "Use expanded 8 MB main RAM instead of stock 2 MB mirroring. Savestates record the active size, so states from one setting do not load under the other. Both netplay peers must use the same setting."
group = "Advanced"
default_enabled = false
hidden = true

[[plugin]]
feature = "8mb-ram"
id = "psx.8mb-ram"

format_version = 5
id = "psx.enhancement.cd-speed"
version = "1.0.0"
name = "CD Speed"
author = "psxrecomp"
description = "Emulated CD drive speed. Shortens loads without speeding the game up, so it does not disturb movement or timing-based routes."
resolver = "declarative"
save_compatibility = "shared"

# Loading speed is a property of the emulated hardware, not of any particular
# disc, so this ships with the framework and applies to every game.
[[target]]
game_id = "*"

[[feature]]
id = "cd-speed"
name = "CD Speed"
description = "Disabled by default. Divides the emulated sector delay, so the drive delivers data sooner while the game itself keeps running at normal speed. Unlike host pacing this changes WHEN the game receives CD interrupts, so a high value can expose timing bugs -- raise it gradually and back off if a load stalls. FMV and CD audio always keep authentic timing."
group = "Quality of Life"
default_enabled = false

[[option]]
feature = "cd-speed"
id = "multiplier"
label = "CD speed multiplier"
description = "1 is authentic 1x. Try 2-32; higher is faster but likelier to trip a timing bug. Any positive value is accepted so you can find this game's limit. Ignored while Instant is ticked."
group = "Quality of Life"
type = "integer"
min = 1
max = 1024
step = 1
default = 4
disabled_by = "instant"

[[option]]
feature = "cd-speed"
id = "instant"
label = "Instant (bounded scheduler)"
description = "Deliver sectors as fast as the bounded instant scheduler allows instead of using a multiplier. Fastest and riskiest."
group = "Quality of Life"
type = "boolean"
default = "false"

[[option]]
feature = "cd-speed"
id = "instant_budget"
label = "Instant sectors per frame"
description = "How many sectors the instant scheduler may deliver per frame. Lower is gentler on games that dislike bursts. Only used while Instant is ticked."
group = "Quality of Life"
type = "integer"
min = 1
max = 256
step = 1
default = 32

[[plugin]]
feature = "cd-speed"
id = "psx.cd-speed"

format_version = 5
id = "psx.enhancement.fast-loading"
version = "1.0.0"
name = "Fast Loading (host pacing)"
author = "psxrecomp"
description = "Speeds up the wall-clock pacing of loads without changing anything the game can observe. Every guest frame, CD interrupt and callback still happens on schedule."
resolver = "declarative"
save_compatibility = "shared"

# Loading speed is a property of the emulated hardware, not of any particular
# disc, so this ships with the framework and applies to every game.
[[target]]
game_id = "*"

[[feature]]
id = "fast-loading"
name = "Fast Loading (host pacing)"
description = "Disabled by default. Host pacing is the safe accelerator: it only changes how fast real time is fed to a load, so the guest cannot desync. It does speed the game up while a load is detected, which some speedrun routes rely on NOT happening -- if that is you, leave this off and use CD Speed instead."
group = "Quality of Life"
default_enabled = false

[[option]]
feature = "fast-loading"
id = "multiplier"
label = "Host speed multiplier"
description = "How much faster than real time a load may run. 1 is authentic. 2-32 is the useful range; larger values keep working but stop helping once the host, not the pacing, is the limit. Ignored while Uncapped is ticked."
group = "Quality of Life"
type = "integer"
min = 1
max = 1024
step = 1
default = 4
disabled_by = "uncapped"

[[option]]
feature = "fast-loading"
id = "uncapped"
label = "Uncapped (as fast as the host allows)"
description = "Run loads at whatever speed this machine can manage, ignoring the multiplier above."
group = "Quality of Life"
type = "boolean"
default = "false"

[[plugin]]
feature = "fast-loading"
id = "psx.fast-loading"

format_version = 5
id = "psx.enhancement.pgxp"
version = "1.0.0"
name = "PGXP Precision (geometry + textures)"
author = "psxrecomp"
description = "Sub-pixel vertex precision and perspective-correct texturing (the PGXP technique): the runtime shadows the GTE's full-precision projections and follows them to the GPU, so 3D polygons stop wobbling between whole pixels and large floor/wall textures stop warping. Visual-only unless its precise culling option is on: the game's own math, culling and readback see exactly what real hardware produces."
resolver = "declarative"
save_compatibility = "shared"

# Sub-pixel precision is a property of the emulated GTE/GPU pair, not of any
# particular disc, so this ships with the framework and applies to every game.
[[target]]
game_id = "*"

[[feature]]
id = "pgxp"
name = "PGXP Precision"
description = "Disabled by default (the faithful floor). Corrections are validated per vertex against the exact packet words the game drew with and clamped to half a pixel, so 2D sprites and UI are never touched and a vertex the tracker cannot prove simply draws the faithful way. Most effective on a build compiled with the PGXP hook variant; on other builds coverage is reduced but never harmful. Needs supersampling >= 2 to be visible."
group = "Visual"
default_enabled = false

[[option]]
feature = "pgxp"
id = "cpu_mode"
label = "CPU-mode propagation"
description = "Also track precision through CPU arithmetic (register repacking math). Off matches the reference implementations' default; on can raise coverage in games that rebuild vertices with integer math. Always safe either way - validation rejects anything stale."
group = "Visual"
type = "boolean"
default = "false"

[[option]]
feature = "pgxp"
id = "culling"
label = "Precise culling"
description = "Also decide which faces the game culls from the same full-precision positions that PGXP draws, so distant rows the hardware rounds to zero height are no longer dropped and leave no gaps between their neighbours. Unlike the rest of PGXP this changes what the game itself computes (its NCLIP results), so it is off unless a game turns it on; netplay always runs without it."
group = "Visual"
type = "boolean"
default = "false"

[[plugin]]
feature = "pgxp"
id = "psx.pgxp"

format_version = 5
id = "psx.presentation.bezel"
version = "1.0.0"
name = "Bezel Artwork"
author = "psxrecomp"
description = "Draws user-selected artwork behind the game image in OpenGL letterbox or pillarbox margins. Disabled by default; with the feature off, margins remain the normal black clear."
resolver = "declarative"
save_compatibility = "shared"

[[target]]
game_id = "*"

[[feature]]
id = "bezel"
name = "Bezel Artwork"
description = "Disabled by default. Select an image file to draw behind the game image whenever the selected aspect ratio leaves side or top/bottom margins. This is presentation-only and does not change guest rendering."
group = "Visual"
default_enabled = false

[[resource]]
feature = "bezel"
id = "artwork"
label = "Bezel image"
description = "Select an image to draw behind the game frame in letterbox or pillarbox margins."
format = "file"
file_patterns = "*.png,*.jpg,*.jpeg,*.bmp"
file_description = "Image files"
required = false

[[plugin]]
feature = "bezel"
id = "psx.bezel"

route.title: Attach the prepared direct player
route.instruction: Select PointBlank_Recompiled.exe, use the complete extracted PointBlank-PC-Port-v1.1.0-windows-x64 folder as working directory and set the documented --no-launcher argument. Review the intent and request Play separately. The integrated launcher and native runtime share the selected process; complete any disc/BIOS/setup prompt upstream first. Do not select an original PS-X executable or an obsolete build wrapper. The runtime reads the remembered source/configuration; keep installed disc files and any external originals in place.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact PlayStation original upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Point Blank PlayStation USA SLUS-00481 CUE and all referenced BIN tracks. The selected profile pins data Track 01 to 297,657,360 bytes and SHA1 367a96937bfbe19ce5089c0b364f513cbe07dd1e; boot executable is SLUS_004.81. A track digest is not a whole-CUE/container signature or permission to obtain the original. Arcade Point Blank and other regions are different sources. Finish Browse For Disc verification, optional Install To Game Folder and settings upstream.

persistence.title: Preserve settings, cards and optional device choices
persistence.instruction: Keep settings.toml, game.toml/game_options.toml, saves/ with both memory-card slots and their configured external paths, mods/ and its state, captures and original CUE/BIN. Source memory-card paths can override the default saves folder; preserve the actual configuration and all prior CWD roots. Card files are distinct from runtime save states. The mouse/controller GunCon emulation is an upstream software feature, not observed physical lightgun or two-player qualification. Online track/TOC identity gates and peers remain separate, untested requirements.

limitations: Use the prepared 1.1.0 PlayStation player and complete USA CUE/BIN. Preserve actual memory-card paths; arcade and physical-lightgun acceptance remain separate.

packaged_documentation.Buffy Chaos Bleeds PC/mods/story-coop/mo:
[Mod]
Name = Story co-op (experimental)
Author = Buffy PC port
Version = 0.5
Description = A second player joins the story. During a level, press Start on controller 2 and pick one of the six story characters on the Character Select - one line, the empty slots kept for character mods (A picks, B backs out); you appear beside player 1 while they keep playing. The inventory is shared - anything either player picks up (keys too) is in both hands - but each player selects their own item; each character keeps their own spells and weapon. Player 2's Start opens their own menu: Continue, Change Character, Drop Out. Player 2's Back brings them to player 1 (for when they get stuck). If player 2 falls they get back up beside player 1 a few seconds later. Player 1's pause menu has a Co-op page: Screens (Two Windows, Split Screen or One Screen), Friendly Fire, Shared Inventory, Back Brings Player 2, Player 2 Respawn time, and Drop Out Player 2 - saved in buffy_settings.ini. StoryCoopScreens below is the starting choice for Screens (1 one screen, 2 two windows, 3 split screen). Early work: only the first mission has been tried.

[Patches]
StoryCoop = 1
StoryCoopScreens = 2

route.title: Attach the actual regional game program
route.instruction: In the prepared installation, select buffy_chaos_bleeds.exe for PAL v2 or buffy_chaos_bleeds_usa.exe for North American v1. Set the complete installed game folder as working directory and leave arguments empty; review the intent and request Play separately. Source resolves default.xbe relative to the executable unless an existing BUFFY_GAME_DIR overrides it. If the other supported region is detected, upstream starts its matching companion and waits for it; do not remove the companion or enable a mismatch override. Missing/unsupported setup belongs in the upstream launcher before attachment.

source_setup.title: Prepare the supported desktop original
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Xbox Buffy: Chaos Bleeds ISO/XISO. Desktop supports European PAL version 2 (region 4, first-section code size 1,196,336 bytes) and North American version 1 (region 3, 1,193,024 bytes), title 56550005. These certificate/section checks are not a whole-disc cryptographic fingerprint. PS2/GameCube discs and other revisions are not admitted. Complete Buffy Launcher.exe installation, optional movie conversion and settings upstream into its chosen game folder, keeping independent originals. No disc, FFmpeg, installer, helper or game is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Preserve real saves and old recovery
persistence.instruction: Keep SaveData/ with BUFFY A.sav, B.sav and C.sav, SaveBackups/, buffy_settings.ini, installed game/movie data, mods/, custom texture replacements/dumps, ShaderCache/, bug_reports/ and logs, plus existing external source paths. Pre-0.4 UDATA saves can be converted on first game start or opening the upstream Saves tab, with originals retained in SaveBackups. Preserve old UDATA/XboxData and every previous installation until existing saves have been checked; this guide does not follow upstream cleanup suggestions or perform conversion, backup, restore or deletion.

limitations: Keep the complete matching regional installation, SaveData and retained old-save recovery. Android is a separate PAL-only route; no game or device was run.

Keep using the existing separate 0.7 HD texture pack; no new pack or
reinstallation is needed for this update. Older HD packs remain compatible
but have less coverage. Full release notes are on the GitHub release page.

Extract the entire ZIP into a new folder, then open Darkwatch Darker Edition.exe.
Keep both EXEs and the payload folder together; do not run them inside the ZIP.
The launcher checks GitHub for a newer release in the background. Check for
Updates retries the check; Install Update downloads a newer Windows release when
clicked. The verified package replaces the required files in this same folder,
then the launcher restarts and updates the installed runtime/content. Saves,
settings and optional packs stay in place. Close the game first. A failed download
leaves the working package intact; restart the launcher to recover an interrupted
file replacement. No download starts without clicking Install Update. Offline
checks do not prevent installation or play. Only releases with the matching
platform package are shown; source, HD-only and prerelease uploads are skipped.
Use a short writable path such as C:/Games/Darkwatch, not Program Files.
Native Windows path handling still has the 260-character limit.
For automatic first-time setup, put one supported Xbox ISO/XISO in the supplied
assets folder and open the launcher. It prepares direct ISO playback; keep the
ISO in that folder. Existing installations are reused. Multiple images open the
source chooser, and an unsupported image produces an error without installation.
Select Game offers three choices for your supported Xbox ISO or XISO:
- Use ISO directly: keep the ISO in place. Unmodified assets are read from the
  disc image; setup still prepares the necessary local resources and shaders.
- Import once: copy the game files locally. The ISO can be removed after setup;
  ordinary play and later updates reuse the installed files.
- Use Existing Install: select your previous launcher folder or GameData and
  reuse its files, saves and add-ons in place.
Setup verifies your own disc and prepares the HD menus, font, HUD and characters.
After setup, choose Play. No ISO, Xbox executable, movies or original game
payloads are included. The prebuilt HD pack is not included either.
Gameplay HD textures are a separate optional download. Download all numbered
texture parts into one folder. Use Install HD Textures in the launcher and select
the .zip.001 file (or the complete texture ZIP). The Graphics toggle stays
unavailable until the pack is installed; HD menus, fonts and HUD remain included.
The existing 0.6 HD pack works without reinstallation. For the added artwork,
install the existing separate 0.7 pack with this launcher. The expanded pack adds
Cassidy's story ragdoll, corrected blood and additional campaign/model textures,
including their distance versions. These additions require the expanded pack.
Earlier 0.4 and 0.5 packs remain compatible but have less character coverage.
Play from this launcher has no ten-minute test timer.

After setup, open Play Darkwatch.exe to start the game directly without
the launcher window. It uses the same installed game, saves and verification.
Shader preparation must finish before play. Both launch paths check the cache;
if preparation is needed, a themed screen reports the completed shaders. Warm
direct launches remain windowless until the game opens. Canceling preparation
before play keeps completed cache entries for the next attempt.
Keep it beside the rest of this extracted package, or create a desktop shortcut
to it. If no game is installed, use Select Game in the launcher first.
The entire extracted folder is portable; move it together with GameData. If you
linked an existing installation elsewhere, keep that folder or select it again
with Use Existing Install after moving it. Direct ISO mode also requires the
source ISO; select it again with Use ISO directly if you move that file.

Requires Windows 10 version 1903 or newer / Windows 11 x64, .NET Framework 4.8,
an x86-64-v2 CPU (including
SSE4.2 and POPCNT), and a Direct3D 12-capable GPU with feature level 11_0.
Python and the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime are included locally;
setup does not install system software or request administrator access.

The supported disc is the original Xbox revision with executable SHA-256:
72fc8033e01df4f22c703121cfd160969c642b18e841248224fc97a8f32050d7
Setup accepts a full Xbox disc image or XISO and checks all 23 original files.
The file picker accepts both .iso and .xiso filenames; no renaming is needed.
Other revisions are rejected. Keep at least 6 GB free per import, plus space
for saves and shader cache. Your source ISO is never modified.

By default the launcher stores everything it installs in GameData/ beside both EXEs.
That includes imported game files, saves, controls, graphics settings and cache.
In Import once mode, the source ISO is only needed for import or repair.
In Use ISO directly mode, keep the source ISO available for play and updates.
Use Open Game Folder to find the imported game, settings and saves. The existing
development build and its saves are not changed or automatically migrated.
Import cancellation or a failed verification keeps the previous complete install.
For a manual update, close the game and launcher and extract the complete new
package over the existing package folder, replacing matching launcher files.
Keep GameData and any retained ISO. If you prefer a separate new folder, choose
Use Existing Install and select your previous Darkwatch folder, GameData folder,
or active game folder. Then choose Update Game. It reuses those files in place;
it does not copy the game or your saves into the new release folder. Keep the
selected GameData folder. You can instead carry GameData into the new package.
Play Darkwatch.exe also applies pending updates before launching. Saves, settings,
optional HD textures, Spanish audio and shader caches remain in place.
Import once with this launcher: normal play and future updates need no ISO.
Direct ISO mode keeps using the selected ISO instead of a full extracted copy.
Setup keeps about 1 MB of private recovery data so content updates can rebuild
their original inputs locally. Older installations without it may require one
final ISO import for a content update; runtime-only updates reuse them immediately.
Select Game remains available to reselect the ISO or import missing/damaged files. A repair
retains the previous installation and preserves saves; normal updates do not
create another full installed copy. Temporary update files need free disk space
and are removed on completion or cancellation. Keep a backup of your saves.
Verify Files checks without running the game. The launcher never deletes your ISO.

Graphics and Controls are available from the main menu and Pause. Esc pauses;
right-click goes back in menus. Configure bindings in Controls. Choose Quit to
Desktop in the main menu to close the game.
Single Player opens rotating character previews. Choices include Jericho,
Civilian Jericho, Cassidy, Spectral Cassidy, Tala, Vampire Tala, Boss Tala, and the
standard, blue and red Darkwatch Troopers. Playable Boss Tala has no wings;
the original NPC boss is unchanged.
Choose a character, then Continue to choose a chapter or resume your save.
Local co-op is under Multiplayer > CO-OP. Choose each player's character in the
left and right co-op panels; both players must select Ready to confirm their choices.
Co-op is a beta feature; full campaign progression and two-player gameplay have
not been fully verified. Character previews and conversion use your own disc;
no original models, animations or voices are included in this package.
Authored Cassidy and regular Tala first-person hand repaints are included.
In co-op, Player 2 pauses with their controller to edit their own controller settings.
Controls supports controller-button rebinding as well as the original layout presets.
Each player's bindings are saved separately. Mouse and keyboard remain Player 1's.
Audio offers Music, Effects and Speech volume plus Stereo or Surround output.
Surround requires a compatible configured device; otherwise output falls back to stereo.
The gameplay HD pack is separate from the HD interface and character selection.
Install Spanish prepares text, subtitles and voices from your European PS2
Darkwatch disc (SLES-53564). Set up your Xbox game first, close the game, then
choose Manage > Install Spanish and select the PS2 ISO. Select Español in Game Language
when the import finishes; the choice applies to the next launch, including
Play Darkwatch.exe. English is always available and uses the original Xbox audio.
Original game text and Spanish audio are not bundled with the launcher.
Older Spanish ZIPs are no longer supported. Existing files stay intact until a
successful PS2 import replaces them atomically, retaining the previous copy.
Import / Repair preserves a verified PS2 language installation and your choice;
older or damaged Spanish files remain in the previous installation folder.
The disc supplies 1,481 dialogue entries and 14 story/intro movie soundtracks.
Its 63 silent/missing entries retain Xbox audio; music and untranslated extras
stay original. Spanish movies use the PS2 stereo mix, while English retains the
Xbox movie surround mix. Spanish presentation needs broader live verification.
PS4 and Switch Pro controllers use matching prompts and controller-layout pages.
Button actions follow physical positions: Switch B confirms and A goes back.
Native USB and Bluetooth paths are enabled but have not been tested on physical
PS4/Switch hardware. If a wrapper exposes an Xbox controller, Xbox prompts apply.
This build disables routine logging, capture hotkeys and development probes.
Fatal errors may still report a short local error to help identify a failure.

This release has not been verified through the full campaign. On release 0.1,
fresh ISO import and shader preparation passed on the test PC, and the player
reported no noticeable stutters on the opening route and boss fight. Preparation
covers the known shader catalogue, not every possible campaign shader. Unseen
shaders, driver work and ordinary loading can still cause pauses. Testing on a
fresh Windows installation remains outstanding.
Cassidy loading, melee audio, co-op HUD placement, Player 2 settings ownership,
character selection and subtitle appearance were accepted in tested scenes.
Controller menu opening/editing and co-op navigation received user acceptance;
the latest transition and profile-startup fixes also passed an agent menu test.
The reported controller-menu crash was traced and its original failure reproduced
in a regression test. This does not establish every controller or machine.
Cassidy hurt audio remains unresolved. Full campaign/co-op progression, story
transitions, every character/weapon combination, surround speaker balance and
Spanish presentation need broader live testing. The mounted-boss fix was accepted
at 240 FPS, and directional audio was accepted with Windows Sonic. These checks
do not establish every encounter or audio device. Linux gameplay, audio and
controllers remain unverified.
The existing 0.6 HD pack remains compatible. Vampire Tala's body and hands use
its matching HD artwork; her head and Boss Tala's body/head retain original
textures where no matching HD artwork exists. Earlier packs have less coverage.
No physical PS4/Switch retest was performed.
Original game content and branding belong to their owners.
Spanish text and audio are prepared from the user's supported PS2 disc.
PC menu translations and compatibility corrections are by Darkwatch: Darker Edition.
See licenses/ for dependency notices and artwork sources.
packaged_documentation.assets/README.txt:
Put your supported original Xbox Darkwatch ISO or XISO in this folder,
then open Darkwatch Darker Edition.exe. On a fresh installation, one disc image
is detected automatically and prepared for direct ISO playback. Keep it here.
The launcher validates the disc first; multiple images require selecting one.
Setup prepares local resources and shaders, without extracting the whole disc.
Existing installations are reused. Updates preserve your ISO, saves and add-ons.
Prefer to remove the ISO after setup? Use Select Game > Import once instead.

route.title: Select the active native runtime explicitly
route.instruction: After successful upstream setup, identify the actual installation root: an installation-location.json can link an external GameData root, whose active.json selects versions/<32-hex-version>/. Select darkwatch_xbe.exe in that active prepared version directory, use that same complete directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the precise intent and request Play separately. This matches the backend normal native command/CWD. Play Darkwatch.exe and its helper return after a one-second startup check, so this guide does not attach them as a wait-through-game wrapper. Do not invent a version value or use the package template. If preparation, content repair or a new version is needed, finish it in the upstream launcher and then review/relink the actual active executable.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact supported original upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own supported Xbox Darkwatch ISO/XISO, title 43430016. The selected supported-disc manifest pins default.xbe to 5,021,696 bytes and SHA256 72fc8033e01df4f22c703121cfd160969c642b18e841248224fc97a8f32050d7, plus individual game-data fingerprints. Finish the upstream 0.7.1 Windows launcher setup and shader preparation outside Portcove. Direct ISO mode retains the original image; Import once and Use Existing Install have different data locations. Keep originals and all recovery records independently. No ISO, importer, helper, shader preparer or game is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Keep the whole installation and data history
persistence.instruction: Preserve the launcher package, GameData or linked installation, installation-location.json, active.json, versions/, darkwatch_xbe_settings.toml, hdd* saves, cache, installed-source/recovery records and all configured external images/data. Do not copy just the executable or point another version at existing saves. Upstream 0.6.1 upgrades may need one final original import because old recovery records were not retained. Preserve old/new data and independent recovery copies before upstream updates; this guide performs no repair, import, migration, backup or deletion.

limitations: Attach only the actual active prepared darkwatch_xbe.exe and its version directory. Keep the full upstream installation; its Play wrapper returns before gameplay ends.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

packaged_documentation.WWE13-Recomp-x64/README.md:
# WWE '13 Recomp

An unofficial static recompilation of the **Xbox 360 version of WWE '13** for 64-bit Windows and Linux. The original PowerPC game code is translated ahead of time to C++ and built into a native executable using the ReXGlue SDK; this is not an Xbox 360 emulator.

## Before you download

You must own a legally obtained Xbox 360 copy of WWE '13 and supply the game files yourself. This project does **not** include the retail `default.xex`, title-update file, game assets, audio, video, DLC, or saves. The executable is a compiled recompilation derived from the game; it is not a substitute for supplying the required game data. See [DISCLAIMER.md](DISCLAIMER.md).

## Required game files

- **Base game** files from your own copy (a game folder, or your own disc image `.iso`).
- **Title update 2.0.1.0** (`default.xexp` and its data files). It is required: the recompilation was built from the updated game, so the game refuses to start without it and tells you why.
- **DLC packs** are optional.

## What you need

- **Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit)**, or **Linux** (glibc 2.38 or newer, e.g. Ubuntu 24.04, with GTK3; on Wayland the game window runs through XWayland, installed by default on most distributions).
- **CPU**: a 64-bit processor with AVX2 (most PCs from 2013 onward: Intel Haswell / AMD Ryzen or newer).
- **Graphics**: a graphics card with up-to-date Vulkan drivers. On integrated graphics, choose 480p.
- About 10 GB of free space for the game files.

## Install and play

1. Download `WWE13-Recomp-v1.5.zip` and extract it to a normal folder such as Documents or Desktop (not `C:\Program Files`).
2. Start **`WWE13 Launcher.exe`** (Linux: `Linux-x86_64/wwe13-launcher`).
3. In **Game files**, do one of the following:
   - put your game folder in the `WWE 13` folder beside the launcher, or
   - press **Find Automatically** to search this PC, or
   - press **Choose a Folder**, or **Use a Disc Image** to extract your own `.iso` once.
4. Add the title update (and DLC packs, if you have them) with **Add TU or DLC**. The launcher accepts the package files you have and installs them where the game expects them.
5. Press **Play**. The very first start takes a few extra seconds while the game prepares its graphics; after that it starts normally.

The launcher checks every file and shows **Game files ready** when everything is correct.

```text
WWE13-Recomp-x64/
├── WWE13 Launcher.exe          # start here (Windows)
├── wwe13.exe                   # the game (started by the launcher)
├── wwe13.toml                  # keyboard keys (change them on the launcher's Controls page)
├── avcodec-58.dll, avutil-56.dll
├── shader-cache/               # pre-built graphics data so the game starts quickly
├── Linux-x86_64/               # Linux launcher + game
├── README.md, DISCLAIMER.md, LICENSE, SHA256SUMS
├── licenses/, third-party-licenses/, ffmpeg-source-*.zip
├── WWE 13/                     # your game folder (default.xex + default.xexp + data)
├── userdata/                   # saves, DLC and settings (created on first run)
└── logs/                       # game logs (created on first run)
```

## Updating

The launcher can keep your copy up to date by itself. When it opens it quietly checks GitHub for a newer
release; if one exists, the Play page shows a **Version X is available** banner with **What's new**,
**Update**, **Not now** and **Skip this version**. Nothing is downloaded or changed until you press
**Update**.

Updating replaces **only the program files** (the game, the launcher, the shared libraries, the read me and
the licence files). Everything of yours stays exactly where it is: your `userdata/` saves and DLC, your
`WWE 13/` game files, your `wwe13-enhanced.ini` settings, your `wwe13.toml` controls, your `music/`, your
`logs/` and your `backups/`. Existing shader-cache files are kept; only missing ones are added. Before
touching anything the launcher copies the current program files to `backups/update-<version>/`, so a failed
install is restored automatically. The download is checked against the release's SHA-256 before it is used,
and a damaged download changes nothing.

The check contacts `api.github.com` only and sends nothing about you or your PC. To turn it off, untick
**Check for updates when the launcher starts** in the launcher's Settings. You can also close the banner
with **Not now** (until the launcher restarts) or **Skip this version** (remembered). If the launcher
cannot reach GitHub, it says nothing and starts normally.

## Launcher settings

**Use Recommended for This PC** picks settings for your graphics card. You can also choose:

- **Resolution** – the sharpness the game renders at. 480p is the fastest (handhelds and integrated graphics); 720p is the original Xbox 360 sharpness; 1440p needs a strong graphics card.
- **Frame rate** – *Classic* (60 in matches, 30 in entrances and cutscenes, like the console), *60 Everywhere* (needs a strong PC), or *30 Locked* (steady, best for laptops and handhelds).
- **Display** – fullscreen or windowed; **Graphics card** – for PCs with two GPUs.
- **Stretch to fill wide screens** – fill a 21:9 or 16:10 screen instead of showing black bars (the 16:9 picture is stretched). **Sync frames to the monitor** – on by default; Windows only, turn it off if fullscreen stutters on a high refresh rate or FreeSync / G-SYNC monitor.
- **Language** – the language of the game's menus and text: English, German, French, Spanish or Italian. Commentary stays English. It is saved in `wwe13.toml` and takes effect the next time the game starts.
- **Start straight away next time** – skip the launcher on later starts. Hold **Shift** while it starts to come back to the settings.
- **Content** – everything you add to the game in one place: custom Superstars, Entrances, Arenas, Logos, your own entrance **Music**, and **Save Data** (Back Up Now, Restore, and imported packs).

## Controls

An Xbox-compatible controller is recommended. The keyboard also works as a controller: the default keys follow modern WWE 2K games on PC - **WASD** move, **J** strike (X), **L** grapple (A; also confirms in menus), **K** Irish whip / pin (B; back in menus), **Space** signature / finisher (Y), **1** reversal (RT), **Left Shift** run (LT), **U** pick up / in-out of the ring (LB), **Left Ctrl** limb targeting (RB), arrow keys taunts (D-pad), **Esc** pause. See and change every key on the launcher's **Controls** page. When the game's on-screen keyboard is open (for example, naming a story), you can type with your PC keyboard and paste with **Ctrl+V**. Names are upper case, like on the console.

While playing, **Alt+F4** quits the game; **F11** switches between fullscreen and windowed.

## Saves and DLC

The game keeps saves, DLC and settings in `userdata/` beside the launcher. It is local to this installation; use **Back Up Now** under **Content → Save Data** in the launcher (or copy the folder) before moving or replacing a release.

## Adding creations

Open **Content** in the launcher and pick a category (Superstars, Entrances, Arenas or Logos). **Add…** selects Xbox 360 creation packages (Superstar `.cas`, Entrance `.enc`, Arena `.car`, Paint Tool logo `.pt`); **Add a folder…** imports a whole folder of them. Each list shows the in-game name and slot and can be sorted by name, slot or date. The launcher backs up your saves before changing anything. You can also drag package files onto the page.

New creations only appear in game if your save lists them, so the Superstars, Entrances and Arenas pages show a short reminder while any installed item is not covered by an imported save.

Some creation packs include a matching `SaveData.dat` file that lists their custom slots. Use **Content → Save Data → Replace current save…** to import it; this replaces your current WWE '13 progress, so the launcher asks you to confirm and makes a backup first. Items imported together this way form a **pack**: remove them with **Remove pack** under **Save Data**, which also puts your save back the way it was before the import. Removing one item of a pack on its own would make the game report missing content, so the launcher does not allow it.

Some older entrance packages use title ID `54510890` rather than WWE '13's `545108B4`. The launcher stores these entrances under WWE '13's save title ID and tells you so; it does not modify the source package. Back up your saves before trying packages from an unfamiliar pack.

## Known issues

- **1080p** is hidden in the launcher for now: at that resolution the crowd can show glitches.
- Some shadow and lighting differences remain compared to the console.
- **480p**: the reversal button prompt that appears over a wrestler is drawn too far up and to the left. 720p and higher are not affected.
- **60 Everywhere**: entrances and cutscenes run in slow motion whenever your graphics card cannot keep 60 fps, because the game's timing follows the frame rate. Use **Classic** (the default) if that happens.
- Extract the release to a normal folder, not `C:\Program Files`: the launcher keeps your saves and settings next to itself (it warns you if the folder is read-only).
- Only the exact title update 2.0.1.0 is supported; other regions, game revisions or title updates are refused.
- In menus, the modern keyboard keys confirm with **L** and go back with **K** (they follow the controller's A and B buttons).

## Reporting bugs

Press **Save a Bug Report (logs + settings)** at the bottom of the launcher. It saves a `wwe13-bug-report-<date>.zip` next to the launcher with the latest game logs, your launcher settings and basic PC information (graphics card, system); no game files or saves. Attach it to a new issue on this repository's **Issues** page and describe what happened. If the game crashed, its log ends with a crash report that shows exactly where.

## Building from source

This is a developer build, not a one-command player install. Full guide: [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md).

1. `./tools/setup.sh` downloads the ReXGlue SDK next to this repository (`../tools/rexglue`), applies this project's
   SDK changes from `rexglue-patches/`, and builds it.
2. Copy your own `default.xex` and `default.xexp` (title update 2.0.1.0) into `game/`, then run `./tools/codegen.sh`.
3. Build with `./tools/build-linux.sh` or (cross-compiled from Linux) `./tools/build-windows.sh`.

`game/`, `generated/` and all retail files stay local: they are never committed or redistributed.

## Credits

- **ReXGlue SDK** — Xbox 360 PowerPC-to-x64 recompilation runtime and tooling; this project builds on the
  [rexglue-sdk-yukes](https://github.com/HollywoodAkeem/rexglue-sdk-yukes) fork. ReXGlue is based in part on work from **Xenia**, the Xbox 360 emulator project.
- **Xenia contributors** — foundational Xbox 360 system and GPU research/code acknowledged by the ReXGlue SDK.
- WWE '13 and all related game material are the property of their respective rights holders. This project is unofficial and is not endorsed by them.

## External libraries

FFmpeg can be combined with a number of external libraries, which sometimes
affect the licensing of binaries resulting from the combination.

### Compatible libraries

The following libraries are under GPL version 2:
- avisynth
- frei0r
- libcdio
- libdavs2
- librubberband
- libvidstab
- libx264
- libx265
- libxavs
- libxavs2
- libxvid

When combining them with FFmpeg, FFmpeg needs to be licensed as GPL as well by
passing `--enable-gpl` to configure.

The following libraries are under LGPL version 3:
- gmp
- libaribb24
- liblensfun

When combining them with FFmpeg, use the configure option `--enable-version3` to
upgrade FFmpeg to the LGPL v3.

The VMAF, mbedTLS, RK MPI, OpenCORE and VisualOn libraries are under the Apache License
2.0. That license is incompatible with the LGPL v2.1 and the GPL v2, but not with
version 3 of those licenses. So to combine these libraries with FFmpeg, the
license version needs to be upgraded by passing `--enable-version3` to configure.

The smbclient library is under the GPL v3, to combine it with FFmpeg,
the options `--enable-gpl` and `--enable-version3` have to be passed to
configure to upgrade FFmpeg to the GPL v3.

### Incompatible libraries

There are certain libraries you can combine with FFmpeg whose licenses are not
compatible with the GPL and/or the LGPL. If you wish to enable these
libraries, even in circumstances that their license may be incompatible, pass
`--enable-nonfree` to configure. This will cause the resulting binary to be
unredistributable.

The Fraunhofer FDK AAC and OpenSSL libraries are under licenses which are
incompatible with the GPLv2 and v3. To the best of our knowledge, they are
compatible with the LGPL.

route.title: Attach the native program with explicit existing paths
route.instruction: Select wwe13.exe and the complete WWE13-Recomp-x64 directory as working directory. Follow the upstream launch-plan coordinates: use the absolute path to your already prepared game folder as the first quoted argument, and --user_data_root= followed by the quoted absolute path to this installation’s existing userdata folder. Replace both paths with actual selections; do not use placeholders literally or select a new empty root. These are the source launcher’s game/user-root arguments, not another guessed cache or environment. Review the exact intent and request Play separately. The game entry validates the title update and owns the selected native process. Launcher-only display/performance environment choices do not automatically transfer to direct launch; finish or retain necessary settings upstream, and do not claim an identical presentation profile.

source_setup.title: Prepare the matching game and mandatory update
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Xbox 360 WWE ’13, title 545108B4, complete base data and mandatory title update 2.0.1.0 including default.xexp and data files. Source checks XEX2 structure/title, target update version and matching source/base version; these are not a cryptographic whole-original fingerprint or a promise every regional revision works. Finish upstream game import, update selection and launcher settings first. Optional DLC/creations are separate. No original, update, importer, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Preserve the whole installation and actual roots
persistence.instruction: Keep userdata/ with saves, DLC, profiles and settings, the selected WWE 13/ or external original folder, wwe13.toml controls, wwe13-enhanced.ini launcher settings, music/, logs/, backups/update-<version>/, custom creations and all configured external roots. Content imports can replace progress and require matching save-slot metadata; another WWE title’s package or shared save is not automatically compatible. Keep complete recovery copies before any upstream creation/save import or update. This guide performs no import, backup, restore, migration or deletion.

limitations: Keep the mandatory matching title update and actual existing user-data root. Direct launch uses explicit source-supported paths; launcher performance/display environment is not automatically reproduced.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Alpha boots field/sound/save/online, not Wii edition; exact ROM/revision and campaign breadth must follow primary requirements, no whole-game assumption.

packaged_documentation.FFCCEOT-Recomp-0.3.1-alpha-windows-x64/R:
Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: Echoes of Time, PC port (0.3.1-alpha, alpha)

1. Extract this folder somewhere you can write to (not Program Files) and run ffcc.exe.
2. Choose your own copy of the game. Two versions are supported (checked by SHA-1):
   - USA: Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles - Echoes of Time (USA) (En,Fr,Es).nds
     1df23d5a3a655bdd587c360b581202931d0f66e1
   - Europe: Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles - Echoes of Time (Europe) (En,Fr,De,Es).nds
     18f7004f74c83feba40f003641ec00571e52a301
   It is checked and built into a game for your PC (about a minute, once). Nothing else has to be installed.

This package contains no game data. It is an early alpha: report problems from the in-game menu (Report an issue).

The program is not signed: Windows SmartScreen or your antivirus may warn about it the first time
(choose More info, then Run anyway).

Your saves and settings are kept in %APPDATA%\FFCCEOT-Recomp\EchoesOfTime.
Put a file named portable.txt next to the program to keep them in a "data" folder beside it instead.

The licences of what the package contains are in the licenses folder and NOTICE.md.

route.title: Attach the prepared normal program
route.instruction: Select ffcc.exe, use its complete extracted package directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. The normal integrated start screen and game thread belong to this same native application; press its Play control when ready, or retain an existing Skip start screen preference. Review the exact intent and request Portcove Play separately. Complete missing/stale module preparation upstream before retrying. Do not attach clang/lld, add finite-frame/replay/test overrides or select an original NDS program as the host.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact Nintendo DS original
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own supported Nintendo DS Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles: Echoes of Time ROM. USA CFIE SHA1 is 1df23d5a3a655bdd587c360b581202931d0f66e1; Europe CFIP is 18f7004f74c83feba40f003641ec00571e52a301. Japanese and Wii editions are not these inputs. Finish upstream ROM selection, its retained copy, local module build and Welcome/settings flow outside Portcove; an update can rebuild from that retained copy. No ROM, converter, compiler, helper or game is obtained or executed by this guide.

persistence.title: Preserve the real data root and regional saves
persistence.instruction: Normally keep %APPDATA%/FFCCEOT-Recomp/EchoesOfTime with settings.ini, the retained ROM/module/build data, cfie.sav or cfip.sav, logs/ffcc.log and any reports/optional assets. An already existing portable.txt selects data/ beside the executable instead; an existing --data-dir or --save-file changes the actual roots. Preserve all actual and old roots plus independent originals. Upstream says a USA save can load in the European game, but that is not an observed migration or a permission to merge both copies. Cartridge saves, states and optional Wii-cutscene material remain separate. This guide performs no import, conversion, backup, restore or deletion.

limitations: Keep the exact supported DS ROM and region-specific data. First-use/rebuild work stays upstream; alpha reports, Wii cutscenes and community online services retain separate scope.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Review official player setup and data/persistence boundaries for the specific offered route; metadata alone does not qualify execution.

Luigi's Mansion Recompiled 1.1.5 - Windows x64
============================================

A native PC port of Luigi's Mansion (GameCube). No game data is included: the game is
built on your computer from your own disc image the first time you start it.


REQUIREMENTS
------------
- 64-bit Windows 10 or 11.
- A graphics card with Direct3D 12 support.
- About 2 GB of free disk space (the game module built at first start, shader caches).
- Your own Luigi's Mansion disc image (ISO, GCM, RVZ, WIA, GCZ, CISO, NFS, TGC):
    USA release (GLME01)  and/or  European release (GLMP01).
  Other games, other revisions and modified images are rejected.


FIRST RUN
---------
1. Unpack the archive anywhere you like.
2. Run LuigisMansionRecomp.exe.
3. Pick your USA and/or European disc image with "Browse...", then "Install". The game
   code is translated and compiled for your PC with the bundled compiler (llvm\ folder),
   which takes about 20 to 60 seconds, then the shaders are prepared once ("Preparing
   shaders"). Later starts go straight to the game.
With both discs you choose which release to play; the European disc also unlocks the
European Hidden Mansion. F1 > Game > "Add or change discs..." reopens setup later.
Updates: the game tells you when a new release is out; F1 > Game > Updates downloads,
verifies and installs it into this folder when you click (settings and saves stay).


KEYS
----
F1    options menu (Esc closes): Visuals, Sound, Controls, Enhancements (General /
      Gameplay / Unused content / Debug), Game
F3    info overlay (map / room / position)
F4    model viewer

Default keyboard: WASD move, arrows C-stick, E/Q/R/F = A/B/X/Y, Left Ctrl = Z,
Enter = START, Left Shift = L, Space = R, 1-4 = D-pad. Gamepads (including GameCube
controller adapters) are detected automatically; remap everything in F1 > Controls.


HIGHLIGHTS
----------
- Any resolution, widescreen and ultrawide (Hor+, HUD anchored to the screen edges).
- High frame rates: the game logic stays at its original 30 updates per second and every
  frame in between is interpolated (F1 > Visuals: frame-rate slider up to 320, "Match
  display refresh rate", "Original" for the console's 30). VRR / G-SYNC / FreeSync aware.
- Accurate GameCube rendering (EFB copies, depth textures, fog, indirect effects), with
  optional Enhanced lighting (per-pixel and colored lights, soft shadows, realistic
  flashlight, bloom) in F1 > Visuals.
- The European "Hidden Mansion" with its boss changes (needs the European disc; with
  both discs E. Gadd's lab offers the USA and the European Hidden Mansion).
- Restored unused and beta content in F1 > Enhancements > Unused content (all off by
  default): Game Boy Horror camera, beta ghost shading, early Bogmire, poison and other
  Luigi states, jukebox, gallery, 2-player mode and more.


WHERE FILES GO
--------------
    %APPDATA%\Luigi's Mansion Recompiled\            settings.ini (F1 menu), install.ini (discs)
    %APPDATA%\Luigi's Mansion Recompiled\game\       the game module built from your disc
    %APPDATA%\Luigi's Mansion Recompiled\USA\Card A  memory card saves (Dolphin-compatible .gci;
                                                     European: EUR\Card A)
Versions up to 1.0.1 used %APPDATA%\Luigi's Mansion PC; the first start of this version
renames it, so your settings and saves carry over.


PORTABLE MODE
-------------
To keep everything (settings, saves, the game module, shader caches) inside the game
folder instead of %APPDATA%, create an empty file named portable.txt (or a folder named
portable) next to LuigisMansionRecomp.exe before you start the game. Everything then goes
into the folder "portable" there: move the whole game folder to another drive or PC and
it keeps working; delete it and nothing is left behind. Keep your disc images inside the
game folder too, so they move along (a disc that is no longer at its old path is looked
for there by name). Another PC only prepares the shaders again.
An existing installation can be switched in F1 > Game > Data folder: "Make this
installation portable..." moves your data into the portable folder and restarts, "Move
data back to the system folder..." does the reverse. The data is copied and checked
before anything is removed, so a failed move changes nothing.
Portable mode needs a game folder you can write to: inside Program Files it stays off
(the setup screen and F1 > Game say so) and the data stays in %APPDATA%.
Updates keep a portable installation portable.


KNOWN LIMITS
------------
- 2-player mode (Unused content) is unfinished: Area 1, Chauncey and Boolossus work with
  two players; the rest of the game is not verified yet.
- A few very fast motions (Chauncey's quickest spin turns, the first frame of water spray
  drops) appear at the game's own 30 updates per second when interpolating.


WHAT IS IN THIS FOLDER
----------------------
    LuigisMansionRecomp.exe   the game program (runtime, recompiler, setup)
    *.dll                     runtime libraries (SDL3, Dawn/WebGPU, DirectX shader
                              compiler, nod, libpng, zlib)
    pipelines.bin             shader precache list
    llvm\bin\                 clang and lld-link, used once to build the game module from
                              your disc (LLVM, Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception,
                              llvm\LLVM-LICENSE.TXT)
    NOTICE.md                 third-party notices

route.title: Attach the already prepared normal player
route.instruction: Select LuigisMansionRecomp.exe, use the complete extracted LuigisMansionRecompiled-1.1.5-windows-x64 directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the exact intent and request Play separately. When configured discs/modules/overlays are current, the integrated setup is skipped and the module is loaded into this same native player. Missing/stale inputs can trigger local rebuilding; complete it upstream before retrying. Do not select a module DLL or compiler as the executable, and do not enable setup-auto, recovery-reset, finite-frame or test overrides.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact supported original upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own GameCube USA GLME01 or Europe GLMP01 revision 0 disc. Supported main.dol SHA1 values are 77d49225e7d28b9777916cdbe5809345c570ecbc (USA) and a1e2bd82813787cfe0b11afb5d138f08fdbd94f1 (PAL rev0). Upstream validates that DOL digest, not merely the image name; ISO/GCM, RVZ and other nod-readable containers are separate representations of that original. Supply both originals only if you want upstream’s cross-region Hidden Mansion overlays. Finish disc selection, local recompilation/link, shader preparation and chosen-version settings outside Portcove. No disc, compiler, converter, helper or game is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Preserve regional cards and destructive move recovery
persistence.instruction: Normally keep the actual %APPDATA%/Luigi's Mansion Recompiled root, including install.ini, settings.ini, game/GLME01 or GLMP01 modules/keys, hidden_mansion/ overlays, USA/Card A and other regional card folders, caches, logs and recovery state. Older Luigi's Mansion PC folders can be renamed on first 1.1+ start; failed rename can copy while retaining the old folder. Existing portable.txt or portable/ instead selects the package-local portable tree. An upstream requested data move copies/checks and switches, then can delete the previous system root; interrupted portable.lm-tmp/portable.lm-old leftovers can be deleted on next startup. Keep independent copies of both old/new roots and any pending move evidence before starting or changing layout. This guide creates no marker and performs no move, recovery, backup or deletion.

limitations: Preserve the actual regional cards and both sides of any system/portable data move before startup. First-use builds, automatic stale-module rebuilding and recovery remain upstream-owned.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Modern GIAN07 port distinct vintage binaries; README includes original outdated missing-source note below modern build guide. Latest release full replay validation remains bounded; Windows binary/LinuxFreeBSD build routes.

content_selection.unselected_members: full physical/logical index checks only; no full CRC or ABI claim

pe_prefix.scope: bounded header only; no execution, complete imports, ABI or dependency resolution

route.title: Attach the prepared modern game
route.instruction: After completing upstream resource/layout preparation, select the actual nonempty modern GIAN07.exe, use its complete prepared program/resource directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the exact intent and request Play separately. The modern SDL main enters the game in that process; do not select the legacy Win98 variant, original executable, ssg_cli.exe replay tool or a zero-byte placeholder. Keep the complete installation instead of moving only the EXE.

source_setup.title: Prepare the original resources upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete modern GIAN07 copy/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Shuusou Gyoku original graphics, audio, scripts and other required retail resources. The source release omits those resources. Keep a complete original installation and independent recovery; no original payload, extractor, compiler, helper or game is obtained or executed here. The exact retail data revision/full corpus fingerprints are not established by this bounded source/package inspection and remain Unknown.

persistence.title: Preserve the executable-side player data
persistence.instruction: The modern Windows data resolver uses the executable’s base folder. Keep the full prepared root, including the actual 秋霜CFG.DAT/other configuration, scores, replays, original data archives, bgm/ content and any established custom audio/resource paths. Preserve old installation roots before choosing another directory; source configuration formats and vintage/modern behavior do not prove cross-version score/replay compatibility. This guide performs no conversion, replay validation, backup, restore, migration or deletion.

limitations: Select the actual modern x86 GIAN07.exe and keep its executable-side resources/data. Vintage binaries, zero-byte placeholders and bounded replay checks have separate scope.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Review official player setup and data/persistence boundaries for the specific offered route; metadata alone does not qualify execution.

content_selection.unselected_members: full physical/logical index checks only; no full CRC or ABI claim

packaged_documentation.rac-rs-0.4.3/Cargo.toml:
# The build root of the game (cargo workspace). It sits here, above rac-rs\ and oracle\, so that every crate of the game,
# including the code that setup generates from your disc in oracle\rec and oracle\game, lies inside it. Cargo then names the
# compiled functions the same way on every PC, whatever folder the game is installed in, and the speed profile in pgo\ (made by
# the developers) fits your build. setup.ps1 builds with this file; rac-rs\Cargo.toml is the game itself.
[workspace]
members = ["rac-rs", "rac-rs/exe"]
default-members = ["rac-rs", "rac-rs/exe"]
resolver = "3"

# wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with one change (rac-rs/vendor/wgpu-hal/README_RAC_RS.txt): its DirectX 12 start-up does not create
# IDXGIFactoryMedia, which ReShade's DXGI hook crashes on. Cargo reads [patch] only here at the workspace root (the same line in
# rac-rs/Cargo.toml is ignored in this layout).
[patch.crates-io]
wgpu-hal = { path = "rac-rs/vendor/wgpu-hal" }

## Wrench

The Wrench modding tools and their documentation (the Ratchet & Clank modding community) describe the game's file formats. rac1-decomp's readers follow them, and so do ours.

## PCSX2

The sound (SPU2), graphics (GS/VU) and CPU behaviour in this project was written against the PCSX2 emulator as a hardware-behaviour reference. PCSX2 is licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later; rac-rs uses the same licence.

## Hardware documentation

psx-spx (Martin Korth / nocash) documents the SPU ADPCM and Gaussian interpolation tables. These are properties of the PlayStation hardware.

## Rust libraries

rac-rs uses crates from crates.io, including wgpu, winit, cpal, rayon, bytemuck, pollster and xxhash-rust, under the MIT, Apache-2.0, Zlib, BSD, ISC and BSL-1.0 licences. Cargo downloads them at build time. Their licence texts ship with each crate.

## OmniLoader mod loader (bundled/omniloader.dll) and Arsenal Mastery

bundled/omniloader.dll is OmniLoader, this project's own mod loader (MIT OR Apache-2.0), written from the MIT-licensed OpenRAC SDK documentation. Built into it: the Luau script engine (MIT; Roblox Corporation and Lua.org, PUC-Rio) through the mlua crate (MIT), and serde / serde_json (MIT OR Apache-2.0). bundled/mods/arsenal-mastery is a mod of this project with its own LICENSE file.

OmniLoader's mod format (the `omni-mod.json` manifest, which also accepts OpenRAC's `openrac-mod.json`), its Luau API and its sandbox rules follow the OpenRAC SDK 1.3 (https://github.com/OpenRAC/OpenRAC), written from its public documentation and data. ## Microsoft DirectX Shader Compiler (dxcompiler.dll)

On Windows the game can use Microsoft's DirectX Shader Compiler (DXC) to translate its shaders when you choose the DirectX 12 renderer
(Options -> Graphics -> Screen -> Renderer). It makes the first start about 7 s faster than the built-in fallback (FXC). The game works
without it.

rac-rs does not contain or ship DXC. The setup (setup.ps1) downloads Microsoft's own release archive onto your PC and copies only
`bin\x64\dxcompiler.dll` next to `rac-rs.exe`:

- Project: https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler
- Release: v1.9.2609 (2026-09-29), file `dxc_2026_09_29.zip`, SHA-256 `AD31B1FC8443175D204F77A611FDB3EF2EC42759BDC2F1167368DE24A4A7E7F1`
  (setup checks this; if the download fails or the checksum differs, the game simply uses FXC)
- `dxcompiler.dll` (x64) SHA-256 `0689E2FEE0A1C9DF8662A59680469F24E2A3AD7CE6BBBCC9284F7A83172BFC59`
