# rac-rs

An unofficial PC port of **Ratchet & Clank** (PlayStation 2, 2002), written in Rust. It runs the full game, start to credits, from **your own disc**.

> **No game data is included.** This repository contains no game code, graphics, sound, text or other game files.
> The setup reads your own copy of the disc and creates everything it needs on your PC. You need to own the game.

Project site: https://asobicodes.dev
Launcher (optional app to play, update, and manage texture packs and mods): https://github.com/AsobiCodes/rac-rs-launcher
Support the project (no pressure tho!): https://ko-fi.com/asobicodes

## Status

- The whole game is playable from power-on to the end credits, including New Game+.
- Gameplay follows the original PS2 game one to one. On top of that, the PC version has widescreen, keyboard and mouse controls, gamepad support, and an optional modern camera (mouse look and strafing).
- Optional modern graphics on the Graphics page (Pause > Options > Graphics): enhanced lighting with volumetric fog, 3D clouds and shining stars, global illumination, ambient occlusion, dynamic shadows, clear reflective water with waves and tides, vegetation, enhanced smoke, fire and explosions, sun rays, frame smoothing and a sharp HUD, each with quality levels, plus a Graphics Preset row (Low / Medium / High / Custom). The Classic settings keep the original PS2 look.
- Two renderers: Vulkan (the default) and DirectX 12 (Options > Graphics > Screen > Renderer). ReShade works with both.
- **RAC-RS Launcher** (since v0.4): a separate app to play, change every option, manage texture packs and mods, keep several game versions side by side, and update with a backup first. See [Launcher](#launcher).
- **Mods** (since v0.4): script mods through the bundled OmniLoader mod loader. **Arsenal Mastery** comes preinstalled and switched off. See [Mods and texture packs](#mods-and-texture-packs).
- **PCSX2 texture packs** (since v0.4): packs made for PCSX2 work as they are.
- Plays from the PAL / Europe disc and, since v0.2, from the USA disc.
- Windows 10 and 11, and since v0.4.1 Linux (x86-64). See [Linux](#linux).
- Known issues are listed under [Known issues](#known-issues) below.

## How it works

The game runs on its own original code. When you run setup, it translates the PS2 code from your disc into native Rust ("static recompilation"), and that code runs on a PS2 CPU core written in Rust. Because the game logic is the original code, gameplay behaves exactly like the PS2 version.

Everything around the game code is native PC code written for this port: graphics, sound, movies, input, saving, and the PC features. Where a fix, a PC feature or speed needs it, an original function is rewritten in readable Rust. Changes are tested against the original: test runs play the same frames on both versions and compare the game's memory.

## Goal

A faithful, fully playable PC version of Ratchet & Clank that you build from your own disc, with PC improvements on top. The game logic stays the original code. Rewriting the whole game from scratch is not a goal of this project.

## What you need

- **The game disc:** Ratchet & Clank, **PAL / Europe v1.00** (serial SCES-50916) or **USA v1.00** (serial SCUS-97199). Make an `.iso` image of **your own** disc. Other versions (Japan, Platinum and Greatest Hits re-releases) are not supported yet. Setup checks the image.
- **About the USA version:** it should play the same as the PAL version (at 60 frames per second, like the original US game), but it has had less testing so far. If something looks or behaves differently from the PAL version, please open an issue here on GitHub.
- **Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit**, with about **5 GB of free disk space** (the finished install takes about 3.5 GB) and an internet connection for the first setup.

That's all. Setup downloads anything else it needs into its own folder.

## Setup

1. Download **rac-rs-0.4.3.zip** from the [latest release](https://github.com/AsobiCodes/rac-rs/releases/latest) (or click the green **Code** button above and choose **Download ZIP**), and unzip it anywhere. Drives formatted as exFAT, USB sticks and SD cards work too.
2. Double-click **Setup.cmd**. A window opens (no black console window).
3. Click **Browse** and pick your `.iso` file. The window checks it and shows a green **Disc OK**. Two boxes below choose whether to also install the **RAC-RS Launcher** and whether to **add the game to Steam** (close Steam first). Then click **Install**.
4. Wait. The window shows the steps and a progress bar (about 15 minutes; you can keep using your PC). When it says **Ready to play**, click **Play**.

Next time, double-click the **Ratchet & Clank (rac-rs)** shortcut on your desktop (it opens the launcher if you installed it, otherwise the game), or open Setup.cmd and click **Play**. The same window also has **Repair / rebuild** if something breaks. If anything goes wrong the window says which step failed and has a **Copy details** button. For troubleshooting, `Setup.cmd -Console` runs setup in a console window instead.

Setup does the rest by itself:

- **Tools:** it downloads its own private copy of Rust, Python and the GNU assembler into the `toolchain` folder, using the official free packages (fixed versions, each download checked). Nothing is installed on your PC: no admin rights, no Windows prompts, no changes to your system, and any Rust or Python you already have is left alone. This download is about 220 MB and runs only once; the folder takes about 1.2 GB on disk.
- **Disc check:** it checks your disc image.
- **Build:** it generates the game code from your disc and builds the game. This takes about 12 minutes on a 24-thread CPU, or roughly half an hour on a 4-core CPU.
- **Shortcut:** it puts a shortcut on your desktop.

Your saves are kept in the `player` folder.

**Do not share or upload the generated files or the built game.** They contain code generated from the game disc. Everything setup creates stays inside this folder.

## Linux

Since v0.4.1, rac-rs also runs on Linux (x86-64). It is the same game code as on Windows, built from your own disc, and a recorded fight gives identical game memory on both. **Linux support is new**: it has been tested on Ubuntu 24.04 and Arch Linux (under WSL, with software Vulkan). Real graphics drivers and other distributions are not tested yet, so please report what you find. The double-click launcher folder, the keep-awake, Add to Steam and script mods on Linux are new in v0.4.2 and not yet tried on a real desktop or a real Steam Deck.

The Linux port was set up by **[DeSynkro](https://github.com/DeSynkro)** ([pull request #38](https://github.com/AsobiCodes/rac-rs/pull/38)): building and running the game on Linux, Linux gamepads, the Linux run and crash logs and the exact maths that give Linux the same game memory as Windows. Thank you!

Like on Windows, you do not install any programming tools. `setup.sh` downloads its own private copy of Rust 1.99, Python 3.14 and a C linker (zig) into the game folder (`toolchain`, about 250 MB to download and 1 GB on disk), plus the Rust libraries that `cargo` fetches from crates.io (about 200 MB). There is no compiler, `pkg-config`, development package or `sudo` involved. You need:

- A 64-bit Intel/AMD Linux with glibc 2.28 or newer (every mainstream distribution since 2019, SteamOS 3 included), about 7 GB of free space on a Linux drive (ext4, btrfs, ...; not an SD card formatted as FAT or exFAT, which cannot run programs or make links; `setup.sh` checks this) and an internet connection for the first setup.
- A Vulkan-capable graphics driver (Mesa for AMD/Intel, the NVIDIA driver for NVIDIA). On Linux the game uses Vulkan only; there is no Renderer row in the Options menu.
- Ordinary run-time libraries, which any desktop install already has (a minimal or server install may not): ALSA (sound), udev (it is what lets the game see gamepads), the Vulkan loader and the X11 window libraries (Xlib, Xcursor, Xi and the keyboard library xkbcommon-x11; on a pure Wayland desktop `libwayland-client` instead). `setup.sh` looks for them first and prints the install line for your distribution if one is missing. Without one of the window libraries the game stops at start with "Failed to load one of xlib's shared libraries". The packages:
  - Debian / Ubuntu: `sudo apt install libasound2t64 libudev1 libvulkan1 libxkbcommon-x11-0 libx11-6 libx11-xcb1 libxcursor1 libxi6` (`libasound2` instead of `libasound2t64` on Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 and older)
  - Arch: `sudo pacman -S alsa-lib systemd-libs vulkan-icd-loader libxkbcommon-x11 libx11 libxcursor libxi`
  - Fedora: `sudo dnf install alsa-lib systemd-libs vulkan-loader libxkbcommon-x11 libX11 libX11-xcb libXcursor libXi`
  - SteamOS normally has all of them. If the launcher says one is missing on a Steam Deck, start it in Desktop Mode and install the latest SteamOS update.
- Your Ratchet & Clank disc image: PAL/Europe v1.00 (SCES-50916) or USA v1.00 (SCUS-97199). Put it in the `rom` folder, or give its path.

The launcher for Linux is a `.tar.gz` download (`rac-rs-launcher-linux-x64.tar.gz`): extract it and double-click the launcher inside, no `chmod` needed. On a Steam Deck, `sh setup.sh --add-to-steam` (or Settings > Advanced > Steam in the launcher) adds the game to your Steam library as a non-Steam game; close Steam first. This is not yet tried on a real Steam Deck.

Build and play (in the unzipped game folder; the Launcher does the same with one click):

```
sh setup.sh                          # finds the .iso in rom/, downloads the tools, checks the disc, generates the game code, builds (takes a while)
sh setup.sh --iso "/path/to/disc.iso"
./play.sh                            # starts the game
```

`setup.sh` writes only inside the game folder (also its temporary files and caches; not with `--system-toolchain` below); it downloads only the tools above and the Rust libraries from crates.io, and checks every tool download against a fixed SHA-256. It ignores your `RUSTFLAGS`, compiler wrapper (for example sccache) and `~/.curlrc` / `~/.wgetrc`. It prints no compiler warnings, only errors. The first build takes 10 to 30 minutes and about 6 GB of memory (it uses fewer parallel jobs on a PC with little memory; `--cargo-jobs N` sets it). Run it again after an update (the Launcher's Update does that for you). `./clean.sh` removes the generated game code, the build files and the downloaded tools (several GB) once the game is built and keeps the game itself (and your `--system-toolchain` choice). `./install-desktop-entry.sh` adds "Ratchet & Clank (rac-rs)" to your application menu (one file in `~/.local/share/applications`).

Advanced: `sh setup.sh --system-toolchain` builds with your own Rust (1.90 or newer; 1.99 is best), `python3`, a C compiler, `pkg-config` and the ALSA and udev headers (`libasound2-dev`, `libudev-dev` / `alsa-lib`, `systemd-libs` / `alsa-lib-devel`, `systemd-devel`) instead of downloading anything; it is remembered until you pass `--pinned-toolchain`. `sudo docker compose up` is a third way: it builds the game in a Debian 12 container.

Gamepads: Xbox-style controllers, DualShock 4 and DualSense are read through the kernel's evdev interface (the SDL controller database that ships inside the `gilrs` library decides which button is which). A controller plugged in while the game runs is picked up. The first controller found is used.

Differences from Windows, for now:

- The Linux build has no profile-guided speed boost (PGO), so it can run slower than the Windows build on the same machine.
- There is no Update-now window and no Windows-only option (Renderer, RivaTuner, ReShade). The game shows a notice window when a newer version is out; to update, use the Launcher, or unpack the new release over the game folder and run `sh setup.sh` again (it notices the new version and rebuilds what changed).
- The game writes `player/log.txt` (the run log when started from a menu or file manager) and `player/crash.log` (panics) next to the saves.

## Launcher

The **RAC-RS Launcher** ([AsobiCodes/rac-rs-launcher](https://github.com/AsobiCodes/rac-rs-launcher)) is an optional app next to the game. Setup offers to install it; you can also download it from its own release page. From the launcher you can:

- start the game, and change every option (graphics, camera, controls, Skip intro) before you play,
- add, import and switch PCSX2 texture packs, and turn mods on or off with their own settings,
- keep several game versions side by side and use profiles,
- update the game: it backs up your current version first.

The game works the same without the launcher; everything it changes can also be set in the game's own menus.

## Mods and texture packs

- **Script mods** run through **OmniLoader**, this project's own mod loader, which comes with the game (`bundled\omniloader.dll` on Windows, `bundled/libomniloader.so` on Linux). Turn mods on or off in the launcher's Mods page or on the title screen under Options > Mods. With no mod switched on, the game plays exactly as before.
- **The mod format comes from OpenRAC.** OmniLoader is this project's own code, written from the public, MIT-licensed mod SDK of [OpenRAC](https://github.com/OpenRAC/OpenRAC) (another Ratchet & Clank PC project). It follows OpenRAC's script-mod format and Luau API, so a mod folder with OpenRAC's `openrac-mod.json` is read too. No code of OpenRAC's game port is used. Credit and the SDK licence are in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).
- **Arsenal Mastery** is preinstalled and switched off: a fan-remaster style mod where weapons level up like in Ratchet & Clank 3, Nanotech levels raise Ratchet's health and enemies are rebalanced to match. Switch it on in the launcher when you want it.
- **PCSX2 texture packs:** add a pack made for PCSX2 (a folder or a .zip) in the launcher, or import it from your PCSX2 texture folder. Packs cover world textures, water, sky, chrome and glass, the ship, particles, grass, and the HUD and menus. A pack made for the other disc region mostly works too. Turn packs on or off on the title screen under Options > Mods; while one is on, Pause > Options > Mods has the switches in game too.

## Making mods

- **Script mods** (Luau, run by OmniLoader): [docs/MODDING.md](docs/MODDING.md) is a step-by-step guide with a 5-minute first mod, hooks, fields, drawing and per-save data. The preinstalled [Arsenal Mastery](bundled/mods/arsenal-mastery) is a full worked example.
- **Reference**: [docs/MODDING_REFERENCE.md](docs/MODDING_REFERENCE.md) lists every hook id, game function and field.
- **Texture packs** (PCSX2 format): [docs/TEXTURE_PACKS.md](docs/TEXTURE_PACKS.md) shows how players add and switch packs and how to make one.

## Updating

When you start the game, it checks online whether a newer version is out. If there is one, a window shows what is new. Click **Update now** to update, or **Not now** to just play. With the launcher, updates also show up there, and the launcher backs up your current version first. Your saves, your settings, your disc setting and the downloaded tools are kept, and only the parts that changed are rebuilt. Most updates take a few minutes; a few take about as long as the first build (about 15 minutes). You can also check by hand: open Setup.cmd and click **Check for updates**. The check only downloads a small version file from GitHub; nothing about you or your game is sent. On Linux the window is a notice only: update with the launcher.

If you downloaded v0.1.0, it has no automatic updates. Download the new ZIP, unzip it over your old folder (replace the files) and double-click **Setup.cmd**. If the window says "Finish the update", click **Update**; otherwise click **Repair / rebuild**. Either way the game is rebuilt once, completely, and your saves and disc settings are kept.

What changed in each version is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).

## Controls

The game's own button prompts show the keyboard and mouse keys. You can change the camera style, the language and every button in the game's Options menu (Pause > Options > Controls for the buttons; Camera speed and Mouse speed are separate rows). Controllers work too: Xbox-style controllers (XInput) and PlayStation controllers (PS4 DualShock 4 and PS5 DualSense, over USB or Bluetooth), also when you switch one on or plug it in after the game has started. With the modern camera on, hold R2 to strafe (Options > Camera > Strafe aiming: Raised, Shoulder or Off). Tutorial pop-ups show your keyboard keys when you play on keyboard. Pause > Options > Graphics, page System, has Quick Select mouse (off by default: hold Triangle, T or the middle mouse button and point at a weapon), Stick dead zone and Button glyphs.

## Known issues

- The faint afterimage trail behind Ratchet during Thruster-Pack flight is not drawn yet.
- Some glass surfaces can flicker.
- On AMD and Intel graphics, HUD Sharp only sharpens the title screen and main menu for now. In game, the on-screen text, icons, menus and shop keep the Original look.

## Reporting a problem

If the game freezes, crashes or looks wrong, please [open an issue](https://github.com/AsobiCodes/rac-rs/issues) and attach the file `player\log.txt` from your rac-rs folder. The game writes it every time it runs. It lists your Windows version, processor and graphics card, and what the game did up to the problem. If the game froze, wait about 15 seconds before you close it: the log then also says where it got stuck. The previous run is kept as `player\log.prev.txt`, so if you already restarted the game, attach that file instead. If you use mods or a texture pack, say which ones, and try once with them switched off. The log stays on your PC; the game sends it nowhere. On Linux the file is `player/log.txt` in the game folder; the launcher's Open log folder opens it.

## Contributors

- **[DeSynkro](https://github.com/DeSynkro)**: the Linux port ([pull request #38](https://github.com/AsobiCodes/rac-rs/pull/38), v0.4.1).

## Legal

This is a fan project for preservation and education. It is **not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Insomniac Games**. "Ratchet & Clank" is a trademark of Sony Interactive Entertainment LLC. All game content belongs to its owners.

The repository contains only original source code and tools. It contains no copyrighted game data, and it does not tell you how to get the game other than from a disc you own.

## License

GPL-3.0-or-later, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Credits for third-party work (including OmniLoader's Luau script engine) are in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

# Arsenal Mastery

Ratchet & Clank 3 style weapon levels for Ratchet & Clank 1. Every weapon, and the wrench, earns XP from the damage it deals and grows through levels V1 to V5. The enemies are rebalanced so the game stays a fight. XP is saved per save slot (a new game starts at zero, New Game+ keeps what you had). It needs a game with the OmniLoader extension: on another loader the mod logs one line and does nothing. The mod reads the game only through the named fields of the port's binding; a perk whose fields a port does not name yet is switched off with one log line, the rest of the mod keeps working.

## XP and levels
- A weapon earns 10 XP for every point of health it takes off an enemy (overkill does not count), plus a bonus for the last hit. A 3-health enemy killed by one weapon gives 45 XP. Crates do not count.
- Levels (XP, before the XP rate): V2 750, V3 2,250, V4 5,000, V5 10,000. Weapons you get late in the game need less (three quarters, or half for the last ones), so they can catch up. Levelling is slow on purpose: expect to reach V5 with your favourite weapons, not with all of them, in one playthrough.
- Each level makes the weapon hit harder: about x1.2 at V2, x1.5 at V3, x1.9 at V4 and x2.5 at V5.
- The Weapons page of the pause menu shows every weapon's level and XP bar, and the wrench's in the header. When a weapon levels up, its icon and the new level pop up on screen for a moment.

## New Game+ and Endless
- In New Game+ weapons can go on to V6 Mega, V7 Giga and V8 Omega (Mega is bought, see below; the five weapons without a gold version earn it with XP).
- With the Endless level cap, levels go up to V99, each one a little stronger and a little slower to earn.
- Enemies are tougher in New Game+ (they take 2.5x less damage than in the first playthrough), so Mega to Omega weapons still have a fight; with Nanotech levels on, their hits also take twice as much health.

## Nanotech levels
Health works as in Ratchet & Clank 3. You start with 10 health, and every hit you score with any weapon or the wrench earns nanotech XP, a third of what the weapon gets (10/3 per point of enemy health). Each level adds 1 health and fills it at once, as in Ratchet & Clank 3. Levels come often early and slower later: 20 health at 2,000 XP, 30 at 5,000, 50 at 14,500, 70 at 30,000 and the most, 100 health, at 72,500. In New Game+ it goes on to 200 health, 1,100 XP a level. The Premium and Ultra Nanotech upgrades you buy on Orxon still count: x1.25 and x2 health.
- Enemy hits take more health the further you are in the game: 3 on Veldin, about 10 on Eudora, 20 on the last planets (x2 in New Game+, x1.3 with Hard rebalance). A falling or crushing death is still a death.
- The orbs are replaced by the number: the nanotech icon and your health, with a bar of what is left, where the orbs were. It turns red under a quarter. A nanotech pickup gives back the share of one orb, a death refills it all.
- Your nanotech XP is saved per save slot (a new game starts again at 10 health, New Game+ keeps it).

## Enemy rebalance
Enemies take less damage the further you are in the game, to match your levelled weapons: Off, Standard, or Hard (stronger enemies, and every second hit on Ratchet costs one more health orb, or, with Nanotech levels, enemy hits take 30% more health).

## Settings
XP rate (0.5x to 3x), Level cap, Enemy rebalance, Weapon power from levels, Gold version at V5, Extra projectiles and perks, Ammo, XP bars and level-up icons, Nanotech levels, and "Start every weapon at" (a sandbox option for trying high levels).

Advanced (in the launcher's Mod settings, under "Advanced"), each x0.25 to x4, x1.0 = as designed:
- **Nanotech XP rate**: how fast nanotech levels come (weapon XP keeps its own XP rate).
- **Weapon damage**: the damage your weapons and the wrench deal, on top of weapon levels and the rebalance.
- **Damage you take**: the damage enemy hits do to Ratchet. With Nanotech levels it scales the health a hit takes; with the orbs, the part of an orb carries over (x0.5 = every second hit is free, x1.5 = 1, 2, 1, 2 orbs, x2 = two orbs a hit).

The settings are saved in the game's `mods\settings.json` under `"arsenal-mastery"` (the launcher writes it; you can also edit it by hand while the game is closed), for example:
```json
{"format":1,"mods":{"arsenal-mastery":{"xp_rate":1.5,"nanotech_xp_rate":2.0,"weapon_damage":1.25,"enemy_damage":0.75}}}
```
A setting you leave out, or a value of the wrong kind or outside its range, uses its default.

Presets: **Default** (the defaults), **Just the XP** (bars and XP only, nothing in the game changes, the game's own orbs), **Survival** (Hard enemies and Survival ammo), **Endless** (V99 cap).

## Gold weapons (V5)
With "Gold version at V5" on, an owned weapon that has a gold version in the game turns gold when it reaches V5: gold icon, gold name, gold glow and the game's own gold stats, all together. A gold version earned this way costs no gold bolts, so every gold bolt you found stays free for Mega. Gold weapons you bought in the game yourself are never touched. Turn the setting off and the gold the mod gave is taken back (the ones you bought stay).

## Mega at the Gold Weapon Cases (New Game+)
In New Game+, the gold weapon case of a weapon that is at V5 offers Mega, bought the same way you buy a gold weapon in the original game: you need the bolts and 4 spare gold bolts. The case, the talk prompt and the fanfare are the game's own, so the offer text is the game's gold text. The price in bolts is the weapon's normal gold price (10,000 to 60,000), and every Mega uses up 4 of your gold bolts: the 40 gold bolts in the game pay for all ten. The Gold Bolts page of the pause menu shows what is left. A case that was already empty when you walked in (for example after you bought the gold weapon the normal way in this room) opens again after you leave the room and come back. The five weapons with no case (Taunter, Walloper, Visibomb, Drone Device, R.Y.N.O.) reach Mega by XP instead. Mega needs "Weapon power from levels", "Gold version at V5" or "Extra projectiles (perks)" to be on.

## Ammo capacity and Survival
With "Weapon power from levels" on, a weapon holds more ammo as it levels: 125 percent from V3, 150 percent from V5, 175 percent from V6. With "Ammo: Survival", ammo crates give half of their ammo (at least 1), every kill gives 1 shot back to the weapon you used (not the Glove of Doom: its agents kill by themselves), and vendors sell the full amount as always. With "Normal" crates and kills work as in the original game.

packaged_documentation.rac-rs-0.4.3/rac-rs/Cargo.toml:
[package]
name = "rac-rs"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"
# The game as a library (src/lib.rs, crate rac_game) without the generated game code; the exe `rac-rs` is built by the package in
# exe/ (rac-rs-exe), which adds ee-game. Kept apart so this crate compiles in parallel with the generated crates.
autobins = false

[lib]
name = "rac_game"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[dependencies]
bytemuck = { version = "1.25.2", features = ["derive", "extern_crate_alloc"] }
cpal = "0.18.2"
pollster = "1.0.1"
rayon = "1.12.0"
wgpu = "30.0.1"
winit = "0.30.13"
libloading = "0.8.9"
ee-oracle = { path = "../oracle" }
# Pure-Rust maths for the PC code that writes game memory (src/fmath.rs): the same bits on Windows and Linux. Pinned: a new
# version can change bits (re-take the fmath GOLDEN and the fullcheck replay hashes first).
libm = "=0.2.16"
# PCSX2 texture pack names (src/texpack): XXH3_64 of the texture bytes.
xxhash-rust = { version = "0.8.18", default-features = false, features = ["xxh3"] }

# Same version as wgpu-hal's (Cargo.lock): the D3D12 descriptor types for the ReShade add-on (viewer/gpu/reshade/native.rs).
[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]
windows = { version = "0.62", default-features = false, features = ["Win32_Graphics_Direct3D12", "Win32_Graphics_Dxgi_Common"] }

# Linux: the gamepads (an Xbox controller, a DualSense, ...) as evdev devices, read with gilrs (retail/lxpad.rs); libc for the run log
# (runlog_linux.rs). The Windows build has its own paths (xinput for an Xbox controller, pspad for a PlayStation one) and does not need these.
# The default features of gilrs (`wgi`) are kept: gilrs-core insists on one of `wgi` / `xinput` being enabled on every platform, and
# the `windows` crate behind `wgi` is an empty stub outside Windows, so it costs nothing here.
[target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies]
gilrs = { version = "0.11.2" }
libc = "0.2.190"

[features]
# Public build: the exe uses the Windows GUI subsystem (no console window) and logs panics to <player dir>/crash.log. Off for dev builds and test tools.
windows_gui = []

[dev-dependencies]
naga = { version = "30.0.1", features = ["wgsl-in"] }
ee_game_for_tests = { package = "ee-game", path = "../oracle/game" }

# wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with one change (vendor/wgpu-hal/README_RAC_RS.txt): its DirectX 12 start-up does not create IDXGIFactoryMedia,
# which ReShade's DXGI hook crashes on. A cargo workspace root in a release tree needs the same line (path rac-rs/vendor/wgpu-hal).
[patch.crates-io]
wgpu-hal = { path = "vendor/wgpu-hal" }

packaged_documentation.rac-rs-0.4.3/rac-rs/vendor/wgpu-hal/READ:
wgpu-hal 30.0.1 as shipped on crates.io, with ONE change for rac-rs (MIT OR Apache-2.0, see LICENSE.MIT / LICENSE.APACHE).

What changed
  src/dx12/instance.rs, in `Instance::init`: `let factory_media = lib_dxgi.create_factory_media().ok();` became
  `let factory_media = None;` (plus comment lines), and `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `create_factory_media` in src/dx12/mod.rs
  (the function is no longer called). Nothing else differs from the published crate (compare with
  `diff -r` against ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/wgpu-hal-30.0.1; only the .cargo-ok marker file is missing here).

Why
  wgpu-hal's DirectX 12 start-up always calls CreateDXGIFactory1(IID_IDXGIFactoryMedia). That factory is used only for
  SurfaceTarget::SurfaceHandle (composition surface handles), never for window (HWND) surfaces, which is all rac-rs uses.
  ReShade 6.8.0 hooks CreateDXGIFactory1 in its dxgi.dll proxy and its hook crashes (access violation) on that interface id,
  so the game could not start on DirectX 12 with ReShade installed. A SurfaceHandle surface now fails with wgpu's own error
  "IDXGIFactoryMedia not found"; rac-rs does not use one. wgpu has no option that avoids the call (checked in 30.0.1).

How it is used
  rac-rs/Cargo.toml: [patch.crates-io] wgpu-hal = { path = "vendor/wgpu-hal" }. In a release tree whose cargo workspace root
  is the tree root (relayout.py), the same [patch.crates-io] line with path = "rac-rs/vendor/wgpu-hal" must be in the ROOT
  Cargo.toml: cargo ignores [patch] in a member manifest.

How to re-apply on a wgpu upgrade
  1. Copy the new wgpu-hal-X.Y.Z from the cargo registry over this folder (leave out .cargo-ok).
  2. In src/dx12/instance.rs find `create_factory_media()` in `Instance::init` and replace the call with `None`.
  3. If a wgpu release stops creating the factory unconditionally (or ReShade's hook survives it), delete this folder and the
     [patch] lines instead.
packaged_documentation.rac-rs-0.4.3/rom/README.md:
# Put your Ratchet & Clank disc image in this folder.

Any name ending in `.iso` works. The setup finds it on its own:

    ./setup.sh

or, with Docker:

    sudo docker compose up

If you have more than one image here, the setup asks which one to use.

The supported discs are **PAL / Europe v1.00** (serial SCES-50916) and
**USA v1.00** (serial SCUS-97199). Other versions (Japan, the Platinum and
Greatest Hits re-releases) are not supported yet.

Your disc image is never committed to git, and it is only ever read.

route.title: Attach the generated native game directly
route.instruction: Select the existing build/release/rac-rs.exe from that prepared installation, use its full installation root as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the intent and request Play separately. The native no-argument entry finds generated/play.cfg up the executable’s parent chain, reads its original ISO setting, derives required support/player paths and starts the normal retail-cold game in process. It does not require invented launcher environment. Do not attach Setup.cmd, Play.cmd, a compiler or the developer oracle. Complete an update prompt or rebuild outside the attached attempt first.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact disc upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete rac-rs copy/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own PS2 Ratchet & Clank PAL/Europe v1.00 SCES-50916 ISO (4,213,997,568 bytes, SHA1 B0DFBD8EAC0D84F173B6FC25D8A02A5FF22C652F) or USA v1.00 SCUS-97199 (4,214,095,872 bytes, SHA1 AEE9275384F739C9B24CD5DE6F7E200292DB7B01). Japan, Platinum and Greatest Hits are not accepted by those fingerprints. Finish Setup.cmd disc validation, local translation/build and settings upstream. Keep the original ISO at its configured location. No original, toolchain, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Preserve player files and generated configuration
persistence.instruction: Keep the complete player/ folder, especially card.bin and card.start1.bin/card.start2.bin safety copies, settings, mod data, logs and crash logs, plus generated/play.cfg, all configured original/source paths and any established external player root. PAL/USA compatibility and modified rosters/scripts are not established by a shared title. Script mods use the separate OmniLoader/Luau contract; keep active mods and texture packs independently. This guide performs no import, conversion, restore, backup or deletion.

limitations: This release is a setup/source kit. Attach only the already generated native game with its complete installation and play.cfg; upstream retains compilation/update ownership.

packaged_documentation.RidgeRacer6-PC-TestBuild-09/README.txt:
RIDGE RACER 6 - PC TEST BUILD 09
================================

An unofficial test build of Ridge Racer 6 (Xbox 360) running natively on
Windows. It contains NO game data: you supply your own disc image of the game.
Please do not pass this build on to anyone who does not own the game.


WHAT YOU NEED
-------------
- Your own Ridge Racer 6 disc image (.iso), USA version. Other regional
  versions are refused: this build only matches the USA executable.
- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
- A graphics card with DirectX 12 support.
- About 6.5 GB of free disk space for the extracted game files.
- An Xbox or PlayStation controller, or a keyboard.
- The Microsoft Visual C++ 2015-2022 runtime (x64). Most gaming PCs already
  have it; the launcher tells you if it is missing.


HOW TO START
------------
1. Extract this whole zip to a normal folder (for example C:\Games\RR6).
   Do not run it from inside the zip.
2. Double-click   RR6 Launcher.exe
3. Press "Choose disc image..." and pick your Ridge Racer 6 .iso, wherever it
   is on your PC. The launcher copies the game files out of it into a "game"
   folder here. That takes a few minutes and happens only once. Your .iso is
   not changed and is not needed again afterwards.
4. Choose your settings (the defaults suit most PCs) and press Play.

You can press Stop while the files are being copied; choosing the .iso again
later carries on from where it stopped.

If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", choose More info > Run anyway.
The build is not code-signed. (To avoid being asked for each program, unblock
the zip before extracting it: right-click the zip, Properties, tick "Unblock",
OK.) If the launcher will not open at all, copy your .iso into the
PUT-ISO-HERE folder and use "Play without the launcher.bat" instead.

Some antivirus programs flag bin\rexruntime.dll under a general name such
as "Yogi" or "Generic". That file is the runtime of the ReXGlue SDK, the
toolkit this port is made with. From test build 07 on it is built from our
own copy of the SDK's source (github.com/Sirhalo23/rexglue-sdk), which fewer
scanners flag than the SDK's own download. The project's page on GitHub has
the current results and says how to check the file ("If your antivirus flags
rexruntime.dll"). If the game does not start and the file is gone from the
bin folder, your antivirus has removed it.


THE LAUNCHER
------------
The picture at the top of the launcher is not part of this package. On the
first start it is a plain drawn banner; once your game files have been copied
out of your .iso, the launcher shows a still from the game's own opening movie
instead (read from your files, on your PC). To use a picture of your own, put
it next to RR6 Launcher.exe as launcher-art.png, launcher-art.jpg or
launcher-art.bmp.


SETTINGS
--------
The launcher's Display tab:
- Screen: full screen or a window.
- Picture shape: on a screen wider than 16:9 (ultrawide), "Fill my screen"
  widens the 3D view to use all of it. "Original 16:9" keeps bars at the sides.
- HUD position on wide screens: at the screen edges, or where 16:9 put it.
- Sharpness: how large the game is drawn internally. Automatic matches your
  screen. Lower it if the game runs slowly.
- Edge smoothing, Texture detail: optional image-quality extras.
- Language: English, Japanese, German, French, Spanish or Italian. The disc
  has all six; the game's text and menus follow this choice.

The game always runs at 60 frames per second, as it did on Xbox 360.
While playing: F4 opens more settings; press "Save to config" there to keep a
change for the next start. F3 shows the frame rate. Settings changed in F4
or in the file by hand are kept when you press Save or Play in the launcher.
The launcher stores its choices in bin\rr6_recomp.toml.

To leave the game, press Esc: it asks "Quit Ridge Racer 6?". Enter quits,
Esc again goes back to the game. On a controller, hold Back + Start for a
second (Create/Share + Options on a PlayStation pad), then A quits and B goes
back. Alt+F4 still closes the game at once.


CONTROLS
--------
Controllers: Xbox and PlayStation controllers work as soon as they are
plugged in or paired. The game shows Xbox button names. On a PlayStation pad:
Cross = A, Circle = B, Square = X, Triangle = Y, L1/R1 = LB/RB, L2/R2 = LT/RT,
Options = Start, Create/Share = Back.

Keyboard (can be changed on the launcher's Controls tab):
  Arrow keys or W A S D   steer / move in menus; Up or W also accelerates,
                          Down or S also brakes
  Space                   A  (confirm)
  Backspace or B          B  (cancel)
  X, Y                    X, Y
  Q, E                    LB, RB
  Enter or P              Start (pause)
  Tab                     Back
  Numpad 8 2 4 6          D-pad
  I K J L                 right stick
Keys do not respond while Shift, Ctrl or Alt is held down.
The keyboard is on/off: steering is all-or-nothing, so a controller is the
better way to play.


ACHIEVEMENTS
------------
The game's 36 achievements work as they did on the Xbox 360: when you earn
one, a pop-up appears with a sound, and it is remembered.

- The list while playing: press F7. Or press Esc and then Y; on a controller,
  hold Back + Start for a second and then press Y. The arrow keys, the D-pad
  or the stick scroll it; Esc or B closes it.
- The list without starting the game: the launcher's Achievements page.
- 15 of the 36 need Xbox Live play, which this version does not have. The
  lists show them apart, and count your progress against the 21 you can earn
  (565 of the 1000 gamerscore).
- Your own sound: put a file named achievement.wav next to RR6 Launcher.exe
  and the game plays it instead of its own chime. The launcher's Achievements
  page has a button to hear it.
- Progress is kept with your save data (Documents\rr6_recomp).


DOWNLOADABLE CONTENT
--------------------
If you own downloadable content for Ridge Racer 6, you can add it to the
game: put the files in the DLC folder (next to RR6 Launcher.exe), or use the
launcher's DLC page.

- You need the content files from your own Xbox 360's storage. They are in
  the folder Content\0000000000000000\4E4D07D3\00000002 and have long names
  without an extension; keep those names. A PC cannot read an Xbox 360 drive directly; a reader
  program for the console's disk format is needed to copy them off.
- The DLC folder: copy the files into it (folders inside it are searched
  too). Each time the game starts, it adds the files that are new or have
  changed; that takes a few seconds the first time.
- Or, on the DLC page, press "Add content files..." and choose them, or
  "Add a folder..." for a folder that holds them. The folders inside it are
  searched too, so the copied Content folder itself will do. A game window
  opens for a moment and closes again; the launcher then says what was added.
- Only content for Ridge Racer 6 is accepted. A save or another game's file
  chosen by itself is refused with a reason; in a folder, anything that is
  not Ridge Racer 6 content is passed over.
- The game looks for added content each time it starts. To remove content,
  delete its folder ("Open content folder" on the DLC page), and take its
  file out of the DLC folder if it is there.
- Added music appears under "Change BGM" on the screen before a race, as
  "Player Disc".
- This is new. Five of the downloadable music tracks have been added and
  played this way; the downloadable car designs have not been tried. If your
  content does not show up in the game, please report it.


WHAT TO TEST
------------
This build has only been played for short sessions on ONE PC (NVIDIA
RTX 3060 Ti, 3440x1440). Everything else is unknown, so all of this is useful:

- Does it start and reach the menus on your PC? (AMD and Intel graphics are
  completely untested.)
- Other tracks, cars and game modes.
- The intro and ending videos.
- Whether your progress is still there after closing and restarting.
- Longer sessions: stutter, slowdowns, crashes, sound problems.
- Ultrawide screens: anything stretched, cut off or in the wrong place.
- PlayStation controllers and keyboard play.
- Anything that looks wrong on screen. Screenshots help a lot.
- Achievements: does the pop-up appear, with its sound, when you earn one?
  The quickest is "360!": spin the car a full turn in a drift during a race.

Known: online play and Xbox Live features do not work.


REPORTING A PROBLEM
-------------------
1. In the launcher, open the Troubleshooting tab, tick "Record a detailed log
   the next time I play", and press Play.
2. Play until the problem happens, then close the game (or let it crash).
3. The launcher saves   bug-report.zip   in this folder and shows it to you.
   Send that file with:
   - what you were doing (track, car, mode),
   - what went wrong,
   - a screenshot if it is a visual problem.

If the game crashes without the box ticked, a smaller bug-report.zip is still
made. bug-report.zip contains the game's log, the exit code, your settings,
Windows' crash record for this game, and your PC's Windows version, CPU,
memory and graphics card and driver. Nothing else is collected and nothing is
sent automatically. Your Windows user name is taken out of the file paths in
it, so it can be attached to a public bug report.


A NOTE ON SAFETY
----------------
- Get this build only from the place you were pointed to. If a SHA-256 value
  was published with the download, you can compare it: in PowerShell,
  Get-FileHash followed by the path of the zip.
- Use your own disc image and your own save data. The launcher checks that the
  image is the right game, but the game trusts everything else in it and in
  save files, just as it did on the console.
- The programs are not code-signed, so Windows and antivirus tools may warn
  about them.
- The launcher has no network features, and nothing is sent anywhere. The
  game's online modes do not work on PC, and what they attempt has not been
  tested: leave "Online Battle" alone.


WHERE THINGS ARE
----------------
RR6 Launcher.exe     start here
game\                game files copied out of your .iso (created by the launcher)
PUT-ISO-HERE\        only for "Play without the launcher.bat": your .iso goes here
bin\                 the game program and its settings file (rr6_recomp.toml)
logs\                log files
gamecontrollerdb.txt extra controller definitions (community database)
Documents\rr6_recomp (in your user folder)   save data and shader cache

To remove everything: delete this folder and Documents\rr6_recomp.

# Ridge Racer 6 PC - settings (copied next to the exe as rr6_recomp.toml).
# "RR6 Launcher.exe" edits this file for you; F4 in the game changes settings
# while playing ("Save to config" keeps a change) and F3 shows the frame rate.
# Options marked [restart] in that menu take effect the next time the game starts.
# The game runs at its native 60 fps; these settings only change image quality.

# Stops foliage flicker on NVIDIA cards.
use_fuzzy_alpha_epsilon = true

# Texture sharpness at shallow angles (the road surface stretching into the
# distance). 3 = 4x (runtime default), 4 = 8x, 5 = 16x.
anisotropic_override = 5

# ---- 16:9 picture (bars at the sides on an ultrawide monitor) ----
# Internal render scale. 1 = 1280x720 (what the Xbox 360 drew),
# 2 = 2560x1440, 3 = 3840x2160. Higher is sharper and costs more GPU.
resolution_scale = 2

# Other options you can set here:
# swap_post_effect = "fxaa"         # extra edge smoothing: none, fxaa, fxaa_extreme
# fullscreen = true                 # false = run in a window
# vsync = true                      # the game's speed is tied to 60 Hz; leave on

# ---- Keyboard (works alongside a controller) ----
# "RR6 Launcher.exe" has a Controls tab that edits these. Several keys can be
# given for one button, separated by commas. Keys do not respond while Shift,
# Ctrl or Alt is held. Xbox and PlayStation controllers need no settings.
mnk_mode = true                     # false = ignore the keyboard
mnk_mouse = false                   # leave the mouse pointer alone
keybind_lstick_left = "Left,A"      # steer left
keybind_lstick_right = "Right,D"    # steer right
keybind_lstick_up = "Up,W"          # menu up
keybind_lstick_down = "Down,S"      # menu down
keybind_right_trigger = "Up,W"      # RT / R2: accelerate
keybind_left_trigger = "Down,S"     # LT / L2: brake
keybind_a = "Space"                 # A / Cross: confirm
keybind_b = "Backspace,B"           # B / Circle: cancel
keybind_x = "X"                     # X / Square
keybind_y = "Y"                     # Y / Triangle
keybind_right_shoulder = "E"        # RB / R1
keybind_left_shoulder = "Q"         # LB / L1
keybind_start = "Return,P"          # Start / Options: pause
keybind_back = "Tab"                # Back / Create
keybind_dpad_up = "Numpad8"
keybind_dpad_down = "Numpad2"
keybind_dpad_left = "Numpad4"
keybind_dpad_right = "Numpad6"
keybind_rstick_up = "I"
keybind_rstick_down = "K"
keybind_rstick_left = "J"
keybind_rstick_right = "L"
keybind_lstick_press = "N"          # left stick click / L3
keybind_rstick_press = "M"          # right stick click / R3

route.title: Attach the native fallback command after preparation
route.instruction: Select bin/rr6_recomp.exe, use the complete extracted package root as working directory, and supply --game_data_root with the quoted absolute path to its already prepared game folder, plus --gpu_plugin=xenos and --log_file with the quoted absolute path to this installation’s existing logs/run.log. Use your actual paths, not literal placeholders. This is the selected source’s normal native command and documented no-launcher fallback, with preparation already finished; do not attach the BAT, which starts a child and exits. Review the intent and request Play separately. Diagnostics, DLC import and missing-game repair are separate upstream operations.

source_setup.title: Prepare the precise supported original upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Xbox 360 Ridge Racer 6 USA original, title 4E4D07D3. The selected source pins default.xex SHA256 39D3C0004EC62AEB0FE3E7E1889CF25D98FBD27987B6BC6B5FF30A56FFBA6C00. Finish the upstream launcher’s ISO/extracted-game preparation and settings before attachment, keeping the independent original and complete game/ data. A matching title ID alone does not qualify another revision, region or update. No ISO, extractor, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Preserve the actual Documents root
persistence.instruction: Keep the real Windows Documents/rr6_recomp directory, including profile/content trees, saves, achievements and caches, plus bin/rr6_recomp.toml, launcher preferences, logs, game/ and original images. Documents can be redirected. The selected launcher source says a TOML user_data_root line does not change this runtime default; an existing explicit CLI user-data override does, so preserve whichever root the player actually used. Do not assume bin/ or the program root holds saves, merge other revisions, or follow cleanup instructions on another install’s thumbnails/caches. This guide performs no import, backup, restore, migration or deletion.

limitations: Use the actual 0.1.5 package layout and already prepared game paths. Preserve redirected Documents data; the no-launcher BAT is not a wait-through-game executable.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

# =============================================================================
# Fukami settings.
#
# The in-game menu (Esc or F1) changes these and saves them here. You can
# also edit this file while the game is closed. Settings marked "restart"
# in the menu apply the next time the game starts.
#
# Format: `key = value`, one per line. Lines starting with # or ; are comments.
# Booleans accept: true/false, yes/no, on/off, 1/0.
# A setting that is missing from this file (deleted, commented out, or added
# by a newer version of the app) uses the app's default.
# =============================================================================


[display]
# --- ratio ------------------------------------------------------------------
# REAL widescreen. The game's camera renders a wider view (shows more of the
# scene at the sides) and the window shows it at that shape. The intro
# (attract cinematic) is already a wide, letterboxed picture: it keeps its
# width and fills the screen without the black bars instead.
# This changes guest data (an RR5 enhancement). 4:3 is the stock game.
#   4:3 | 16:9 | 16:10 | 21:9
# default: 16:9
ratio = 16:9

# --- hud --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Only matters when ratio is not 4:3. How the 2D parts (HUD, menus, text)
# behave on a wide picture.
#   stretch : never fixed; 2D is stretched wide (what the No.47 hack shows)
#   fixed   : 2D keeps 4:3 proportions, pinned to the screen edges, everywhere
#   race    : fixed during races only; menus stay stretched
#   (no47 is accepted as an alias for stretch)
# default: race
hud = race

# --- aspect -----------------------------------------------------------------
# How the finished picture fits the window. Presentation only, the guest does
# not change. Leave EMPTY to follow `ratio` (recommended).
#   (empty) | auto | 4:3 | 16:9 | 16:10 | 21:9 | stretch
#   auto    : 4:3 with black bars
#   stretch : fill the whole window (distorts if the window shape differs)
# default: empty
aspect =

# --- window -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Starting window size in pixels, WIDTHxHEIGHT (for example 1920x1080).
# Leave EMPTY for automatic: 80% of the screen height, at the picture's shape.
# default: empty
window =

# --- fullscreen -------------------------------------------------------------
# Start in fullscreen. F11 toggles it while the game runs.
#   true | false
# default: false
fullscreen = true

# --- integer_scaling --------------------------------------------------------
# Snap the picture to whole-number multiples of its size (sharper, but bars
# around it if the window is not an exact multiple).
#   true | false
# default: false
integer_scaling = false

# --- present_pacing ---------------------------------------------------------
# Even frame pacing: every frame is shown for the same time, so motion is
# smooth (without it, frames can stay up 8 or 25 ms instead of 16.7 ms on a
# 120 Hz Mac screen: judder). Costs about 6-9 ms of extra display delay.
# On Linux / Steam Deck it instead takes the wait for the next screen image off
# the render thread, so a heavy frame at a high internal resolution does not
# hold up the next one; it adds no display delay there.
# Presentation only, the guest does not change. Takes effect on restart.
#   true | false
# default: true
present_pacing = true

# --- refresh_rate -----------------------------------------------------------
# Windows only. The game makes 59.94 pictures a second; a display at a
# multiple of 60 Hz can show each for the same time, another rate cannot (at
# 165 Hz every fourth picture is 6 ms short). In fullscreen the display is
# switched to a multiple of 60 Hz it supports, and back on leaving fullscreen.
# Presentation only, the guest does not change. Takes effect on restart.
#   auto : a display already at 60, 120, 180 or 240 Hz stays; another goes to
#          the highest of those below its rate (165 -> 120, 144 -> 120, 75 -> 60)
#   60 | 120 | 180 | 240 : that rate (as auto when the display lacks it)
#   off  : leave the display as it is
# With vrr = on (below) the display is left as it is too.
# default: auto
refresh_rate = auto

# --- vrr --------------------------------------------------------------------
# Windows with Direct3D 11 only. On a variable-refresh display (FreeSync,
# G-Sync) each picture is shown at its own time instead of at the display's
# next refresh, so every picture stays up 16.7 ms whatever the display's rate.
#   auto : used once the display is seen following the game (it does when
#          variable refresh is on in the graphics driver)
#   on   : always. On a display without variable refresh the picture tears.
#   off  : never
# Presentation only, the guest does not change. Takes effect on restart.
# default: auto
vrr = auto

# --- sync_to_display --------------------------------------------------------
# Windows with Direct3D 11 only (other systems ignore it). The game makes
# 59.94 pictures a second and a display shows 60.00, so about every 17 seconds
# one picture has to stay up longer, with uneven pictures around it. With this
# on the display is the game's clock: on a 60, 120, 180 or 240 Hz display the
# game runs at 60.00 pictures a second (0.1 % faster; the sound is resampled
# to follow, 2 cents of pitch) and every picture stays up exactly as long as
# the others. The game itself computes the same pictures; only the pace at
# which they are released changes. It adds one picture of delay (16.7 ms) and
# 21 ms of sound delay.
# A FreeSync / G-Sync display is paced by variable refresh (vrr above) either
# way, and a display that is not at a multiple of 60 Hz by the even frame
# pacing; the game keeps its 59.94 there.
#   true  : the display paces the game
#   false : the game's exact 59.94 pictures a second, least delay
# Takes effect on restart.
# default: true
sync_to_display = true


[rendering]
# --- render_mode ------------------------------------------------------------
#   full  : full-frame rendering at 448+ real rows, progressive ~59.94 Hz.
#           Needs a full-capable runtime (the default runtime is one).
#   field : the older half-height field output (Gate-4 style).
# default: full
render_mode = full

# --- scale ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Internal resolution multiplier, full mode only. Higher = sharper, slower GPU.
# On a Steam Deck an odd value above 1 is lowered to the even one below it (3
# runs as 2): its GPU does not reproduce its own depth at 3x and car panels
# come out hatched.
#   1 to 8 (2 | 4 recommended)
# default: 4
scale = 4

# --- aa1 --------------------------------------------------------------------
# PCSX2's AA1 edge anti-aliasing emulation (full mode).
#   true | false
# default: true
aa1 = true

# --- fxaa -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fast anti-aliasing: smooths jagged edges on the finished picture. Cheap.
# Slightly softens fine detail. Presentation only, the guest does not change.
# Only in a window (ignored when headless, so captures stay unchanged).
#   true | false
# default: false
fxaa = false

# --- cas --------------------------------------------------------------------
# CAS sharpening (AMD FidelityFX CAS) on the finished picture, in percent.
# Pairs well with fxaa or a low scale. Presentation only, window only.
#   0 (off) to 100
# default: 0
cas = 0

# --- aniso ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Anisotropic filtering: keeps textures seen at a steep angle (the road going
# into the distance) sharp instead of blurry. Costs a little GPU.
# This changes rendered pixels (a host enhancement, not the stock look).
#   0 (off) | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16
# default: 0
aniso = 0

# --- texture_filter ---------------------------------------------------------
# How textures are sampled when they are drawn larger than their own pixels.
#   ps2      : as the game asks. Ridge Racer V asks for point sampling on its
#              car textures (and only there), so on a car seen up close the
#              texture's pixels show as blocks: logos, lights, number plates.
#   bilinear : every 3D texture is smoothed (PCSX2's "Bilinear (Forced
#              excluding sprites)"). In this game that changes the cars; the
#              2D parts (HUD, menus, text) keep what the game asks.
# This changes rendered pixels (a host enhancement, not the stock look). The
# game itself does not change.
# Needs a runtime that has the setting (newer than v157): the line below is
# commented out until that runtime is the ./run.sh default, because an older
# runtime refuses a key it does not know.
# default: ps2
# texture_filter = ps2

# --- sprite_filter ----------------------------------------------------------
# How the 2D parts (HUD, menus, text, logos) are sampled. The game draws them
# as textures with point sampling: one texture pixel per screen pixel.
#   even : every screen pixel shows the texture pixels under it by share, so
#          letters and digits keep even strokes at every `scale`, and the 4:3
#          HUD on a wide picture (hud = fixed or race) has no stray columns.
#          Where a texture pixel covers a whole number of screen pixels the
#          picture is the same as ps2.
#   ps2  : as the game asks. Even only when a texture pixel covers a whole
#          number of screen pixels: at scale 1 every other row of the text is
#          missing, at 3 strokes are 1 and 2 rows thick, and with hud = fixed
#          or race pieces of the neighbouring letter show at the edge of some
#          letters and digits.
# This changes rendered pixels (a host enhancement, not the stock look). The
# game itself does not change. Full mode only.
# Needs a runtime that has the setting (newer than v174; the ./run.sh default
# has it): an older runtime refuses a key it does not know.
# default: even
sprite_filter = even

# --- mipmap -----------------------------------------------------------------
# PCSX2's emulation of the PS2's mipmaps (smaller texture copies used far
# away). On is what the real hardware does; at the internal resolutions this
# is played at the smaller copies mostly blur distant textures, so it is off
# unless you turn it on. Off can shimmer on some surfaces.
# Full mode only.
#   true | false
# default: false
mipmap = false

# --- backend ----------------------------------------------------------------
# The graphics API the picture is drawn with. Windows only: macOS always uses
# Metal and Linux always uses Vulkan, whatever this says.
#   auto   : Direct3D 11. It is the one that keeps every picture on screen
#            for the same time (even frame pacing, refresh_rate, vrr above).
#   d3d11  : Direct3D 11.
#   vulkan : Vulkan. Try it when Direct3D 11 does not start or misbehaves
#            with your graphics driver.
# default: auto
backend = auto



[input]
# --- analog -----------------------------------------------------------------
# true  : the controller is a DualShock 2: sticks steer, triggers have
#         pressure (the game's analog mode).
# false : a digital-only pad. The game ignores the sticks and trigger
#         pressure; steer with the d-pad.
# default: true
analog = true

# --- rumble -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Controller vibration, driven by the game like a DualShock 2. Only works with
# a controller that can rumble.
#   true | false
# default: true
rumble = true


[game]
# --- car_lod ----------------------------------------------------------------
# RR5 enhancement. Multiplies the game's car level-of-detail distances, so cars
# stay detailed farther away. Capped at the game's own cull distance.
# This changes guest data.
#   1        : stock game
#   a number : for example 2, 4, 6.5   (a decimal point is allowed)
# Above 1, races get the game's larger display-list buffers (4 MB, as its own
# menus use), and a car that would not fit in them is drawn at stock detail
# for that field, so no value can overflow the list (it used to crash the
# start of the second race at 4).
# default: 4
car_lod = 4

# --- draw_distance ----------------------------------------------------------
# RR5 enhancement. The game draws the track's scenery from a baked list per
# course section, so far buildings pop in. This also draws the lists of the
# next N sections ahead, so they appear sooner. Costs speed: measured 107
# (stock) -> 89 (+2) -> 82 (+4) -> 68 (+8) frames/s unpaced at 4x; 2 is
# the sweet spot.
# This changes what the guest draws.
#   0        : stock game
#   1 to 16  : sections ahead
# default: 0
draw_distance = 0

# --- fast_unpack ------------------------------------------------------------
# RR5 enhancement. The game unpacks the data it loads from the disc on its
# main thread and draws nothing meanwhile, so the picture freezes (twice for
# about 1/3 s during the boot Namco logo). This runs the game's unpacker
# natively and nearly instantly: same data, no freeze, faster loading.
# This changes guest timing (not what is drawn).
#   true | false
# default: true
fast_unpack = true

# --- car_depth_fix ----------------------------------------------------------
# EXPERIMENTAL (menu page "Experimental"). Known fault: part of the hood of the
# car sliding into the car selection screen turns black.
# RR5 fix. The game draws a near car's body twice from the same vertices (the
# paint, then a second texture layer) and the second pass only lands where its
# depth equals the first exactly. A GPU at a scale that is not a power of two
# may not reproduce its own depth (Steam Deck at scale 3: hatched bumpers,
# reflections that come and go). This draws the second layer and the reflection
# from a copy of the vertices a hair in front (16 depth units per million), so
# nothing depends on a tie.
# This changes what the guest sends to the GS (display list size), not the
# picture on an exact GS.
#   true | false
# default: false
car_depth_fix = false

# --- native_code ------------------------------------------------------------
# Host speed-up. The game's busiest code runs as native versions of itself:
# about 30 of its functions (the 3D geometry builders and their helpers) as
# native versions of their own recompiled code, and the graphics-unit (VU1)
# microprograms that draw the course as whole native programs. The game clock
# is kept exactly and the guest sees the same state at every step, so the
# result is bit-for-bit the same, with less CPU used.
# Off runs all game code as plain recompiled code.
#   true | false
# default: true
native_code = true

# --- logging ----------------------------------------------------------------
# The Fukami app only. Writes a session folder (stdout.log, stderr.log, the pad
# record, per-start timing files, a copy of the memory card) under
# sessions/ in the app's support folder. Off (the default) creates no folder
# and writes no file. Takes effect on restart. ./run.sh always writes its
# session under local/product/sessions and ignores this.
#   true | false
# default: false
logging = false


[timing]
# --- unpaced ----------------------------------------------------------------
# false : real-time. Locks the game to 60000/1001 VBlanks per second
#         (about 59.94 Hz) and vsyncs the window (no tearing).
# true  : run as fast as the host can. For speed tests. No vsync.
# default: false
unpaced = false

# --- inline -----------------------------------------------------------------
# Where VIF1, VU1 and GS run.
#   false : on their own owner thread (faster; the default)
#   true  : on the EE thread, as before (for comparison and debugging)
# default: false
inline = false

# --- split_gs ---------------------------------------------------------------
# With inline = false: run VU1 and GS on two threads (rrv-vu1 and rrv-gs-owner)
# instead of one owner thread. Faster on slower CPUs (Steam Deck).
#   true  : two threads (the default)
#   false : one owner thread
# default: true. In the in-game menu under Performance (restart).
split_gs = true

# --- pacer_spin -------------------------------------------------------------
# With unpaced = false: how the game waits for the next field. Sleeping lets a
# Steam Deck clock its CPU down (3.5 -> 2.4 GHz), and the same game work then
# costs 30-45% more CPU time, so scenes with headroom can miss 60 fps there.
# Busy-waiting the last N ms of each wait keeps the clock up. It costs power
# (one CPU core stays busy); it does not change the game.
#   0        : sleep (the default)
#   1 to 17  : busy-wait the last N ms (17 = the whole wait; worth trying on a
#              Steam Deck if you see stutter)
# default: 0. In the in-game menu under Performance (restart).
pacer_spin = 0

# --- headless ---------------------------------------------------------------
# No window. For automated runs.
#   true | false
# default: false
headless = false

# --- from -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Replay debugging (with `replay` below). Run the first N VBlank starts as
# fast as the host can (sound muted), then switch to real time with vsync, so
# you land on a scene quickly and then watch it live. 60 starts = 1 second.
# Leave EMPTY for a normal launch. Needs unpaced = false.
# default: empty
from =



[developer]
# Developer mode lifts the [env] allowlist below. Leave it off unless you are
# debugging or qualifying the runtime: the other RRV_* variables switch on
# diagnostics, change what the game computes or write files to disk.
# (./run.sh also accepts RRV_DEVELOPER=1 in the environment of the command.)
#   true | false
# default: false
enabled = false


[env]
# Advanced. A line here is passed to the game as an environment variable, and
# is applied LAST, so it overrides what the settings above produce.
# One per line, NAME = value, names are RRV_ plus capitals, digits and _.
# Without developer mode (above) only these names are accepted, the ones the
# settings above map to:
#   RRV_GS_RENDER_MODE RRV_PCSX2_GS_FULL_SCALE RRV_PCSX2_GS_FULL_HWAA1
#   RRV_PCSX2_GS_FXAA RRV_PCSX2_GS_CAS RRV_PCSX2_GS_ANISO
#   RRV_PCSX2_GS_TEXTURE_FILTER RRV_PCSX2_GS_SPRITE_FILTER
#   RRV_PCSX2_GS_FULL_HWMIPMAP RRV_PCSX2_GS_VSYNC RRV_PCSX2_GS_PRESENT_PACING
#   RRV_PCSX2_GS_ASPECT RRV_PCSX2_GS_HUD_SCALE RRV_PCSX2_GS_HUD_MODE
#   RRV_PCSX2_GS_INTEGER_SCALING RRV_WINDOW_SIZE RRV_WINDOW_FULLSCREEN
#   RRV_PAD_ANALOG RRV_PAD_RUMBLE RRV_RR5_CAR_LOD RRV_RR5_DRAW_DISTANCE
#   RRV_RR5_FAST_UNPACK RRV_RR5_NATIVE_HOT RRV_RR5_WIDESCREEN RRV_RR5_CAR_ZTIE

route.title: Attach the prepared waiting application
route.instruction: Select Fukami.exe, use its complete extracted Fukami folder as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the exact intent and request Play separately. Source creates a same-image child with the configured environment and original ELF, waits without a play-session timer and returns its exit status; it can restart that child after an upstream settings restart. Keep that supported parent rather than inventing environment/child flags or attaching a resource DLL. Finish missing-disc preparation outside the attached attempt. The source attempts a kill-on-close job on a best-effort basis; this is not an observed universal descendant-cleanup or save-flush guarantee.

source_setup.title: Prepare the supported PS2 original upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Ridge Racer V USA SLUS-20002 as CHD or a complete CUE/BIN pair. The selected extractor verifies nine original files, including SLUS_200.02 at 1,295,332 bytes / SHA256 fb5b4d3f6d74384cee9da4c8b954b40a0205da0a9ae7db9e68d670156f5e706f. This is a per-file source contract, not a hash of every disc representation. Complete upstream disc selection/extraction and settings first; keep the original independently. No original, converter, extractor, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Preserve actual cards and resource/data roots
persistence.instruction: Normally keep %LOCALAPPDATA%/Fukami with fukami.ini, mc/ memory cards, disc/ extracted originals, sessions/ when logging is enabled and all other player data. The real Windows known folder can be relocated; an established FUKAMI_DATA_DIR selects another per-run root. Keep the source CHD or complete CUE/BIN and any external texture/settings/card paths, plus the matching immutable resource package. Card persistence, state files and session logs are distinct. This guide changes no environment and performs no extraction, migration, backup, restore or deletion.

limitations: Keep the complete Fukami app and actual memory-card/data roots. Its source waits for the same-image game child; job cleanup, real saves and gameplay were not observed here.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Which disc container formats and exact clean RL8E54 revision/hash does selected Setup accept?

Non-Windows builds use libco's symmetric stackful coroutines in place of Win32 Fibers for guest
OSThread scheduling (`runtime/src/fiber_manager.cpp`). Vendored in full (all non-Windows
CPU-architecture backends - amd64, x86, arm, aarch64, ppc, ppc64v2, plus the portable sjlj
fallback - though this project's x86_64-only target only ever compiles amd64.c) in
`runtime/third_party/libco` from commit `e18e09d634d612a01781168ad4d76be10a7e3bad`.

`runtime/third_party/libco/LICENSE`.

route.title: Attach the already configured normal game
route.instruction: After completing upstream setup and restart-required graphics choices, turn Show launcher at startup off upstream if you want direct play. Select the generated Game/MLBPowerPros2008.exe, use that complete Game directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the intent and request Play separately. The integrated pre-boot launcher normally continues into the linked runtime in process, but settings requiring a fresh renderer can spawn a replacement; finish them outside the attached attempt. Do not assume successor tracking across a settings restart.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact clean Wii source upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own MLB Power Pros 2008 Wii USA RL8E54 original. Setup accepts ISO, NKit, RVZ, WBFS, WIA, GCZ or CISO through its documented reader, then checks extracted main.dol SHA256 789c208f1611c4b150d272eb32cbd461d24aebbc5d7c11a420102d868ff1c5f7 and ovl_main.rel SHA256 dcc37a1a4824702feff5bcaa6aae7cefdedfc3b5d832fbf3de92b982a59b4edc. These identify the clean code inputs across disc representations, not every container’s hash. Finish upstream Setup installation, translation/compilation and settings outside Portcove, keeping independent originals. No original, converter, toolchain, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Preserve portable and mod-specific persistence
persistence.instruction: Keep Game/portable.txt, Game/UserData/Config.toml, all Wii save/NAND content, the selected Data/ tree, configured dvd_root, mods/, texture/roster/stadium content and external originals. Roster-changing mod combinations have separate UserData/ModSaves/ sets; changing the active roster does not merge those saves or make a clean save interchangeable. Keep independent copies before repair/reinstall or mod/roster imports: upstream preparation can re-extract its managed Data tree. Preserve any older installations and explicitly configured paths. This guide performs no import, migration, backup, restore or deletion.

limitations: This is a preparation-kit route: attach only the completed Game/MLBPowerPros2008.exe. Keep Data, portable UserData and separate roster-mod save sets; finish settings restarts upstream.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

# PuyoPuyoBox Recompiled [![GitHub downloads (all assets, all releases)](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/kirbyguy1237/PuyoPuyoBoxRecomp/total)](https://github.com/kirbyguy1237/PuyoPuyoBoxRecomp/releases) [![GitHub downloads (latest release)](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/kirbyguy1237/PuyoPuyoBoxRecomp/latest/total)](https://github.com/kirbyguy1237/PuyoPuyoBoxRecomp/releases/latest) [![GitHub release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/kirbyguy1237/PuyoPuyoBoxRecomp)](https://github.com/kirbyguy1237/PuyoPuyoBoxRecomp/releases/latest)

Static recompilation of **PuyoPuyoBox** built on [psxrecomp](https://github.com/mstan/psxrecomp) and [recomp-ui](https://github.com/mstan/recomp-ui). _Add a short pitch in catalog_identity.json / README._ | | | |---|---| | Players | 4 | | Region | Japan | | Publisher | Compile, Sega | | Year | 2001 | Scaffolded with the New Project Layout. See `psxrecomp/docs/GAME_PROJECT_SETUP.md` for the full flow. ## RetComM Launcher You can run this title **standalone** (release zip + the built-in recomp-ui Generate & Build flow), or manage installs, updates, ROM/BIOS wiring, and queued builds more intuitively with **[RetComM Launcher](https://github.com/TechnicallyComputers/RetComM-Launcher)** — the Retro Compilation Manager hub for self-compiling recomps. [Downloads](https://github.com/TechnicallyComputers/RetComM-Launcher/releases) · [Full README & features](https://github.com/TechnicallyComputers/RetComM-Launcher#readme)

RetComM checks for updates, rebuilds with existing build data when possible, shares the portable toolchain used by per-title launchers, and automates BIOS/ROM/save plumbing so you are not stuck repeating each game’s wizard by hand. ## Legal You must own the original game. Disc images under `disc/` are gitignored and must never be committed. Retail BIOS dumps are not redistributed; OpenBIOS is used for Generate unless you supply your own SCPH locally. Default app icon: `assets/psxrecomp.ico` (and `.png` / `.svg`) — RetComM-themed controller mark from `psxrecomp/assets/`. Windows builds embed it via `APP_ICON`. Optional box art under `launcher_assets/img/` may come from [libretro-thumbnails](https://github.com/libretro-thumbnails/libretro-thumbnails) (`Named_Boxarts`); see `BOXART_SOURCE.txt` when present. ## Quick start (dev) ```bash git submodule update --init --recursive ./psxrecomp/tools/ci/build_emitters.sh python3 psxrecomp/psxrecomp_cli.py generate \ --config game.toml --project-root . --disc disc/.cue cmake -S . -B build-release -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build-release --target psx-runtime ``` Zip prefix for CI artifacts: `ppb`. ## Symbols Progressive map: `symbols.toml` → `python3 tools/sync_symbols.py` → `psx_symbols.h` (`PSX_FN_*`). See `psxrecomp/docs/SYMBOLS.md`. ## Framework pins Submodule gitlinks (`psxrecomp`, optional `recomp-ui`, nested `recomp-net`) are authoritative. `framework_pins.txt` is an optional scaffold snapshot; release CI logs SHAs with `record_pins.sh` but builds whatever the gitlinks resolve to. Bump submodules deliberately — do not float on `main`/`master` in release CI. ---

R.A.I.D. — Retro AI Development · a Discord for AI-assisted retro reverse-engineering, decomp & recomp

packaged_documentation.mods/preloaded/README.md:
# Preloaded mods

Ship reviewed, default-disabled packages here:

```text
packages/<package-id>/<version>/
  manifest.toml
  …
```

Build wiring copies `mods/preloaded/packages` next to the game executable as
`mods/bundled/`. That tree is build output: every build wipes and re-stages it,
so nothing you place there by hand survives.

Player-installed `.psxmod` archives live in `mods/installed/`, which the
launcher owns and no build ever touches. Install them through the launcher Mods
manager rather than committing them here.

See `psxrecomp/docs/MOD_PACKAGES.md`.
