packaged_documentation.recomp-ui/README.md:
# recomp-ui

A shared, **console-agnostic launcher and in-game settings UI** for static-
recompilation game ports. One Dear ImGui launcher core serves every recomp
ecosystem — SNES, PSX, N64, Nintendo DS, Genesis, NES, and beyond — while a small runtime
overlay API lets the same hosts expose live settings after boot.

It is the reusable extraction of the SNES-recomp "launcher_ng" launcher,
generalized behind a small C ABI. Consume it as a git submodule, hand it your
game's facts through a plain-C struct, and it renders the right UI for that
console.

Proven in production driving two very different consoles from the **same
binary core**:

- **Mega Man X** (Super Nintendo) — CRT theme, SNES pad, ROM verification.
- **Ape Escape** (PlayStation) — blue theme, DualShock + pad-modes, real disc
  verification, memory cards, deep PSX video settings.

---

## Architecture: composition + inheritance

recomp-ui is **one** launcher composed differently per console — never a
per-console fork, never a mega-`if`. See [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

- **Composition** decides *which* cards appear. A `SystemProfile` lists the
  panels each view (dashboard / settings / controller) gets. "PSX has memory
  cards, SNES has SRAM, this game has neither" = include/omit the panel.
- **Inheritance** decides *how* a card behaves. Each module — Controller, Save,
  Video, Verify, Hotkeys — has one base implementation specialized per console
  by a small data **spec**. "Every game has a controller; its art/buttons/count
  differ" = one base card, per-system data.

Adding a console is (ideally) **one `SystemProfile` row** in
[`src/launcher_system.h`](src/launcher_system.h). The console difference is pure
data passed through the C ABI — theme, platform label, box art, pad image,
which panels — so there is no `../snes` / `../psx` source fork.

The DRY heart is [`src/launcher_model.h`](src/launcher_model.h): all launcher
STATE + BEHAVIOR, free of any UI toolkit, built purely from the C ABI structs —
so behavior is identical across every game.

---

## Consuming it

### 1. Vendor the repo (git submodule)

```sh
git submodule add https://github.com/mstan/recomp-ui.git recomp-ui
```

### 2. Wire it into your CMake target

```cmake
include(${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/recomp-ui/recomp_ui.cmake)
recomp_target_launcher_ui(my-game-runtime
    CONSOLE psx                                  # required: psx/snes/nds/n64/nes/...
    BOXART ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/art/boxart.tga   # optional: game box art
    PAD    ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/art/pad.tga       # optional: per-console controller image
    BRAND  ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/art/brand.tga)    # optional: per-console top-left mark
```

`recomp_ui.cmake` is fully self-contained: it bundles Dear ImGui, crc32/sha256/
keybinds, tinyfiledialogs, an IPS applier, and a PS1 memcard formatter, and
stages its fonts/images next to your exe. No network / FetchContent — builds
offline. It defines `RECOMP_LAUNCHER` on the target and links OpenGL. The
standalone recomp-ui project defaults to SDL3; a generic project that directly
includes `recomp_ui.cmake` defaults to the SDL2 compatibility backend unless it
sets `RECOMP_UI_SDL3=ON` or supplies the ecosystem-level
`SNESRECOMP_SDL_BACKEND=SDL3` selection. See
[Build configuration reference](#build-configuration-reference) for precedence
and the definitions produced on the target.

`CONSOLE` is required and selects the runtime asset manifest for that target:
`psx`, `snes`, `n64`, `nes`, `gba`, `genesis`, `gb`, or `gbc`. Common fonts
and launcher chrome are always included; controller, brand, memory-card, and
cartridge art comes only from the selected console family. `CONSOLE all` is
reserved for targets that intentionally switch between multiple console
profiles, such as recomp-ui's standalone preview.

The schema-driven Mods view is developer opt-in. Configure the consuming build
with `-DRECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS=ON`, then provide a non-null
`RecompLauncherCGameInfo.mods` provider. These are separate gates: the CMake
option enables the frontend, while the provider supplies the actual catalog and
behavior. See [Mods frontend](#mods-frontend) for the complete integration.

Multi-display systems can provide `GameInfo.display_layout_labels`; recomp-ui
then exposes a dedicated Display → Screen layout cycle backed by
`Settings.display_layout`. This remains independent of aspect or widescreen
features. The Nintendo DS profile uses it for stacked versus separate windows,
keeps Player 1's ordinary buttons controller-configurable, and leaves the
bottom-screen pointer/touch mapping to the host.

### 3. Call it from your `main()`

```c
#if defined(RECOMP_LAUNCHER)
#include "recomp_launcher.h"
#include "launcher_profile.h"

RecompLauncherCSettings io = { /* seed from your config */ };
RecompLauncherCGameInfo gi = {0};
launcher_profile_apply("snes", &gi);   // "psx", "n64", ... — one call sets the console identity
gi.name = "My Game";
gi.expected_crc = 0x1B4B2E9C; gi.has_expected_crc = 1;
RecompLauncherCSettings defaults = { /* authoritative first-run values */ };
gi.default_settings = &defaults;       // optional Restore Defaults action
gi.has_assist_tools = 1;               // optional host-defined opt-in page
gi.assist_tools_note = "Enables host convenience features.";
gi.credits_text = "Original game and port credits."; // optional read-only page
/* ...per-game overrides... */

char out_rom[512];
int rc = recomp_launcher_run_window("My Game — Launcher", &io, &gi,
                                    ".", initial_rom, out_rom, sizeof(out_rom));
// rc: 0 = LAUNCH (boot out_rom with the edited io), 1 = QUIT, 2 = UNAVAILABLE
#endif
```

The whole contract is [`src/recomp_launcher.h`](src/recomp_launcher.h): a plain-C
settings struct in/out, a game-facts struct, and (optionally) **host callbacks**
for console-specific verification the launcher re-runs on change — e.g. PSX disc
identification (`disc_verify`) and memory-card inspection (`memcard_inspect`).

## Mods frontend

recomp-ui provides a generic, schema-driven **frontend** for mods. It displays
features and their boolean/choice/integer options, installs local archives,
manages installed versions, shows structured diagnostics, and asks the host to
commit the staged selection before launch.

It deliberately does **not** define a mod file format, parse packages, resolve
dependencies, patch a ROM/disc, execute package code, or decide which mods a
game supports. Those jobs remain with the host's mod manager. A PSX host may use
`.psxmod`; another ecosystem can advertise `.gbamod` or another archive type
through the same UI ABI.

### The three gates

A Mods button appears only when all three integration layers are present:

1. The target calls `recomp_target_launcher_ui(...)`, which compiles the
   launcher into that target and defines `RECOMP_LAUNCHER`.
2. The build is configured with `RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS=ON`. The helper turns
   this CMake cache value into the private target definition
   `RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS=1`.
3. The host sets `RecompLauncherCGameInfo.mods` to a live
   `RecompLauncherCModProvider` before calling
   `recomp_launcher_run_window()`.

If the CMake option is off, recomp-ui deliberately discards the provider while
initializing its model. If the option is on but `game.mods` is `NULL`, the
launcher has no catalog to show and omits the Mods button. This is why enabling
the flag in recomp-ui's standalone harness does not produce a sample catalog:
the harness does not fabricate a package manager.

Enable the frontend during the **configure** step:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DRECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS:BOOL=ON
cmake --build build
```

For a consuming game, those commands point at the game's source and build
directories, not necessarily the recomp-ui submodule itself:

```sh
cmake -S path/to/game -B path/to/build \
  -DRECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS:BOOL=ON
cmake --build path/to/build
```

`-D...=ON` belongs on `cmake -S/-B`, not on `cmake --build`. Reconfiguring an
existing build directory with the explicit value updates its cache and causes
CMake to rebuild affected launcher sources; a clean rebuild is not normally
required. Inspect the stored value with:

```sh
cmake -LA -N build | grep RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS
```

PowerShell equivalent:

```powershell
cmake -LA -N build | Select-String RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS
```

If a host wants Mods enabled by default without overriding an explicit user
choice, set the cache default **before** including `recomp_ui.cmake`:

```cmake
if(NOT DEFINED RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS)
    set(RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS ON CACHE BOOL
        "Enable this game's Mods launcher view")
endif()

include("${RECOMP_UI_ROOT}/recomp_ui.cmake")
recomp_target_launcher_ui(my-game-runtime CONSOLE psx)
```

The option is build-tree-wide: every target passed to
`recomp_target_launcher_ui()` in that CMake build receives the same value. Use
separate build directories if one produced executable must expose Mods and
another must compile with the frontend disabled.

### Supplying the provider

Zero-initialize a `RecompLauncherCModProvider`, populate its callbacks, keep it
alive for the entire launcher call, and assign it to the game info:

```c
RecompLauncherCModProvider mods = {0};
mods.ctx = &my_mod_manager;
mods.package_count = my_package_count;
mods.package_get = my_package_get;
mods.feature_count = my_feature_count;
mods.feature_get = my_feature_get;
mods.feature_option_get = my_feature_option_get;
mods.feature_choice_get = my_feature_choice_get;
mods.feature_enable = my_feature_enable;
mods.feature_set_option = my_feature_set_option;
mods.commit = my_mod_commit;
mods.last_error = my_mod_last_error;

RecompLauncherCGameInfo game = {0};
launcher_profile_apply("psx", &game);
game.mods = &mods;
```

The complete append-only ABI is
[`RecompLauncherCModProvider`](src/recomp_launcher.h). New integrations should
implement its feature-oriented callback group as the primary player-facing
surface and the package callbacks as the secondary installation/version/removal
surface:

- `feature_count` / `feature_get` enumerate independently toggleable features.
- `feature_option_get` and `feature_choice_get` describe validated typed
  controls; `feature_enable` and `feature_set_option` stage mutations.
- `package_count` / `package_get`, version callbacks, `select_version`,
  `install_archive`, and `remove_package` drive package maintenance.
- `option_get`, `choice_get`, `set_enabled`, and `set_option` retain the legacy
  package-only surface for providers that have not adopted independent
  features.
- `diagnostic_count` / `diagnostic_get` attach information, warnings, and
  errors to a package or feature.
- `archive_extension` and `archive_description` replace the default
  `.psxmod` file-picker vocabulary for other ecosystems.
- `last_error` supplies the visible reason after any callback returns failure.

The launcher selects the feature-first view only when the complete core feature
group (`feature_count`, `feature_get`, `feature_option_get`, `feature_enable`,
and `feature_set_option`) is present. A package-only provider remains supported;
an accidentally partial feature implementation falls back to that package
view, so implement the core group together.

All query structs contain fixed-size character buffers. recomp-ui copies their
contents and does not retain provider-owned string pointers, so a successful
mutation may safely rebuild or rescan the host catalog before the next query.
Mutation callbacks return `1` on success and `0` on failure.

### Commit and netplay behavior

Normal edits are staged through the provider. When the player presses **PLAY**,
recomp-ui calls `commit(ctx, selected_image_path)` before returning launch
success. A failed commit keeps the launcher open and displays `last_error`; the
host can perform final target verification, dependency resolution, collision
checks, persistence, and plan construction there.

Hosted-lobby, LAN, and direct netplay launches never call the normal `commit()`.
If supplied, `commit_netplay()` should clear any in-session mod plan without
changing the user's persisted offline selection. If it is `NULL`, recomp-ui
skips mod commit entirely. This keeps network matches vanilla unless a host
later defines and implements a synchronized mod contract.

The provider ABI stays present in `recomp_launcher.h` even when
`RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS=OFF`, so the option does not change
`RecompLauncherCGameInfo` layout. The generated macro is private to the target
passed to `recomp_target_launcher_ui()`; it is a frontend exposure switch, not
a build flag for a separately compiled package-manager library.

### PSXRecomp integration

PSXRecomp supplies the provider through
`mod_runtime_launcher_provider()` and sets `game.mods` for its launcher. Its
`PSX_RECOMP_UI` option controls whether the entire recomp-ui launcher is built;
`RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS` controls the Mods surface inside that launcher:

```sh
cmake -S path/to/psx-game -B build \
  -DPSX_RECOMP_UI:BOOL=ON \
  -DRECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS:BOOL=ON
cmake --build build
```

Current PSXRecomp versions default `RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS` to `ON` for a fresh
game build cache while still honoring an explicit `OFF`. An older build
directory may retain the former recomp-ui default (`OFF`); reconfigure it with
the explicit `-DRECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS:BOOL=ON` command above. PSXRecomp emits a
CMake warning when it detects this Mods-less cached state.

### In-game settings overlay

[`src/recomp_runtime_ui.h`](src/recomp_runtime_ui.h) is the separate runtime
contract. A game supplies sectioned item descriptors plus callbacks to read,
apply, persist, and enable its own settings. `recomp-ui` owns hierarchical
navigation, selection state, help/status text, and drawing.

The runtime model is renderer-independent. For a modern/GPU host, call
`recomp_runtime_ui_render_imgui()` inside the host's active Dear ImGui frame;
it uses the same responsive layout and console theme tokens as the launcher,
without exposing ImGui types through the C ABI. This is the preferred path for
RT64/N64 and other high-resolution renderers.

SDL2 hosts that retain an `SDL_Renderer` can add the matching official
SDL_Renderer2 backend to one runtime target with
`recomp_target_runtime_ui_sdlrenderer2(<target>)`. The helper is idempotent and
does not compile another ImGui core or SDL2 platform backend, avoiding duplicate
symbols when the launcher and runtime menu share a binary.

`recomp_runtime_ui_render_argb8888()` is a compatibility presentation for
games that expose a writable CPU framebuffer. It is intentionally compact and
works well for low-resolution framebuffer consoles, but it is not the visual
baseline for every platform. Both presentations drive the exact same menu
state, descriptors, callbacks, and navigation.

The host continues to own the game loop: while
`recomp_runtime_ui_is_open()` is true it should consume menu input before
emulated input and decide whether to pause simulation/audio. See
[`docs/RUNTIME_UI.md`](docs/RUNTIME_UI.md) for the integration boundary and
rollout matrix.

```c
static const RecompRuntimeUiItem rows[] = {
    { "fullscreen", "Display", "Fullscreen", "Choose the window mode.",
      RECOMP_RUNTIME_UI_CHOICE, 0, 2, 1, modes, 3, NULL },
    { "reset", "System", "Reset game", "Reset the emulated machine.",
      RECOMP_RUNTIME_UI_ACTION, 0, 0, 0, NULL, 0, NULL },
};

RecompRuntimeUiConfig menu = {0};
menu.title = "My Game";
menu.subtitle = "SETTINGS";
menu.items = rows;
menu.item_count = sizeof(rows) / sizeof(rows[0]);
menu.callbacks = callbacks;
menu.theme = "n64"; /* same id used by launcher_profile_apply() */
/* Optional for a physically small, high-density touchscreen. */
menu.presentation_flags =
    RECOMP_RUNTIME_UI_PRESENTATION_TOUCH_FRIENDLY;
RecompRuntimeUi *ui = recomp_runtime_ui_create(&menu);
```

New integrations should zero-initialize `RecompRuntimeUiConfig`, then assign
its fields. Set `theme` to the same system id passed to
`launcher_profile_apply()` (`"snes"`, `"n64"`, `"gba"`, `"genesis"`, ...),
so pre-boot and in-game UI cannot drift visually.

The API deliberately does not prescribe settings. Backend swaps that require a
restart can be omitted or exposed as actions; safe live values can be applied
immediately in `set_value`. This keeps game-specific state and policy in the
game while making the menu implementation reusable.

### Optional netplay surface

Netplay is enabled by the game developer, not by an end-user setting. Set
`RecompLauncherCGameInfo.netplay_supported` and provide a
`RecompLauncherCNetplayCallbacks` table to expose the Netplay button. The host
owns player-name and lobby-server persistence, LAN/remote lobby discovery,
password checks, member ordering, and synchronized launch signaling. The UI
only presents that state and returns a `RecompLauncherCNetplayLaunch` result
after the host starts the lobby.

Hosts with more than one local network interface may implement the optional
`local_address_get` callback to enumerate labeled address choices. The launcher
prefills the first address, preserves the user's selection across refreshes,
and falls back to the legacy single-address `local_ip` callback when the new
callback is absent or returns no choices.

The initial waiting-room UI supports two players. Hosts always bind UDP on
`0.0.0.0`. **LAN/Direct IP** (unchecked by default) enables the interface
dropdown and port so hosts can advertise a chosen LAN address to joiners; when
unchecked those controls stay visible but disabled (selection preserved) —
create ignores the greyed port field, prefers UDP `7777`, and auto-picks a
nearby free port (`7777`..`7808`) for lobby-server rewrite / ICE. Before
`join()`, the UI fills `guest_bind` the same way (prefer `7778`..`7809`) so
online guests advertise a real UDP port — hosts must pass that buffer through
to the lobby client rather than rewriting to `:0`. Direct / LAN join still
receives a prepared bind; games may ignore it for file-registry LAN rooms.

**Soft-return rematch:** closing the launcher after a match calls `SDL_Quit()`
(see `launcher_platform_close`). Hosts that `goto` a mid-`main` rematch label
must re-`SDL_Init` video/audio/gamecontroller before opening the game window —
otherwise rematch fails with `Audio subsystem is not initialized`. Full host
checklist: [`docs/HOST_NETPLAY.md`](docs/HOST_NETPLAY.md). Engine-side notes:
snesrecomp `docs/RECOMP_NET.md` → "Soft-return rematch checklist".

---

## Feature surface (per console, capability-gated)

- **Game / verification** — box art, ROM CRC/SHA verification, or PSX disc
  verdict (serial / region / ISO header) via the host `disc_verify` callback.
- **Controllers** — none/keyboard/gamepad per player, per-console pad art +
  button vocabulary, PSX analog/digital/hybrid pad modes or a custom mode list
  (Genesis 3-Button / 6-Button, which also sets the visible rebind-row count),
  deadzone, keyboard rebinding that writes each runtime's native keybind format,
  and an optional per-row **GAMEPAD** bind column (Genesis) alongside the key.
- **Video** — window scale/size, renderer, supersampling, aspect (4:3/16:9/21:9),
  widescreen 16:9 with an optional "extra cells / side" stepper (Genesis),
  texture filtering, antialiasing (Off/2×/4×/8×), screen model, frame
  interpolation, and more — each shown only when the console exposes it.
- **Save** — SRAM Import/Clear (with `.bak` backup) or PS1 memory cards (per-slot
  enable, Browse / New-formats-a-blank-card, real block-usage grid via the host
  `memcard_inspect` callback).
- **MSU-1** — dashboard IPS auto-patching for SNES MSU-1 titles.
- **Hotkeys** — per-console subset of the emulator hotkey catalog, editable.
- **Mods** — default-off, host-provided package catalog with local archive
  installation, enable/disable, version rollback, removal, and schema-generated
  boolean/choice/integer controls. The host owns package formats, defaults,
  resolution, and committing changes before launch; recomp-ui never executes
  package code.
- **Footer** — PLAY, skip-launcher-on-boot (+ confirm modal), gamepad navigation.
- **Optional host pages** — an Assist Tools opt-in backed by
  `RecompLauncherCSettings.assist_tools`, plus host-owned read-only Credits
  text. Games that do not supply these capabilities retain the original three
  views.

---

When `RecompLauncherCGameInfo.default_settings` is non-NULL, the Settings
footer also exposes a confirmed **Restore Defaults** action. The snapshot is
copied at launcher initialization; resetting never changes the separately
owned ROM selection or deletes save files.

`RecompLauncherCGameInfo.has_assist_tools` adds an Assist Tools page and
persists its checkbox through `RecompLauncherCSettings.assist_tools`.
An opt-in `settings_bindings` host can keep keyboard and standard-controller
bindings directly in the settings structure instead of pointing the launcher
at a runtime-specific bind file. The same mode can supply named global Assist
actions; they appear on the Assist page and are returned to the host as SDL
scancodes plus portable standard-controller button/axis encodings.
`credits_text` adds a Credits page. Both are additive host capabilities:
recomp-ui defines presentation and navigation, while the game host defines
the meaning of Assist Tools and owns the UTF-8 credits text.

---

## Build configuration reference

There are three different kinds of configuration in a recomp-ui integration:

- **CMake cache variables** select one implementation for the build tree.
- **Arguments to `recomp_target_launcher_ui()`** configure one target and its
  staged assets.
- **Preprocessor definitions** are generated by the helper. Consumers should
  set the corresponding CMake option instead of injecting these definitions
  manually.

### CMake cache variables

| Variable | Type and default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS` | `BOOL`, `OFF` | Exposes a non-null host mod provider to the launcher model and defines `RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS=0/1` on every integrated target. It does not create a provider or a catalog. |
| `RECOMP_UI_SDL3` | `BOOL`, `OFF` for a generic include | Selects `launcher_platform_sdl3.c` plus Dear ImGui's SDL3 backend and defines `LNG_SDL3=1`. `OFF` selects the SDL2 compatibility sources. Ignored as an independent choice when `SNESRECOMP_SDL_BACKEND` is defined. |
| `SNESRECOMP_SDL_BACKEND` | `STRING`, `SDL3` in recomp-ui's standalone project | Ecosystem-level backend selector. Valid values are `SDL3` and `SDL2`; when defined before `recomp_ui.cmake`, it takes precedence and forces `RECOMP_UI_SDL3` to match. |
| `RECOMP_UI_ROOT` | `PATH`, directory containing `recomp_ui.cmake` | Lets a host use a checkout outside `${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/recomp-ui`. Set it before `include()`. |
| `BUILD_TESTING` | Standard CTest `BOOL`, `ON` for the standalone project | Builds recomp-ui's model, asset-staging, and runtime-UI tests. It matters when recomp-ui is the top-level project; consuming games normally own their test policy. |

All of these are configure-time values. CMake caches them in the build
directory, so switching branches or updating the submodule does not reset an
old selection. Pass an explicit `-Dname=value` to change it, use a new build
directory, or remove the single cache entry with `cmake -Uname -S ... -B ...`
when you intentionally want the project's default to run again.

### SDL backend examples and precedence

Standalone recomp-ui build, SDL3 and Mods frontend:

```sh
cmake -G Ninja -S . -B build \
  -DSNESRECOMP_SDL_BACKEND=SDL3 \
  -DRECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS=ON
cmake --build build
```

Standalone SDL2 compatibility build:

```sh
cmake -G Ninja -S . -B build-sdl2 \
  -DSNESRECOMP_SDL_BACKEND=SDL2
cmake --build build-sdl2
```

Generic consuming host that does not define `SNESRECOMP_SDL_BACKEND`:

```sh
cmake -S path/to/game -B build -DRECOMP_UI_SDL3:BOOL=ON
```

When `SNESRECOMP_SDL_BACKEND` exists, it wins over
`RECOMP_UI_SDL3`. This lets an ecosystem choose SDL once for the game, runtime,
and launcher instead of allowing the UI submodule to drift to another ABI.
The host still owns finding and linking the matching SDL target; the integration
helper adds recomp-ui's platform/backend sources but intentionally does not
guess how the host obtained SDL.

### Per-target helper arguments

```cmake
recomp_target_launcher_ui(game-target
    CONSOLE psx
    BOXART "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/art/boxart.tga"
    BOXART_NAME "my-game-boxart.tga"
    PAD "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/art/pad.tga"
    BRAND "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/art/brand.tga")
```

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `CONSOLE <id>` | Required asset family: `psx`, `snes`, `n64`, `nes`, `gba`, `genesis`, `gb`, or `gbc`. `all` is reserved for an intentional multi-profile target such as the standalone preview. |
| `BOXART <path>` | Optional per-game TGA copied next to the executable. |
| `BOXART_NAME <name>` | Optional destination basename when several targets share one output directory. Pair it with `GameInfo.boxart_path`. |
| `PAD <path>` | Optional controller-art override staged as `assets/img/pad.tga`. |
| `BRAND <path>` | Optional top-left brand override staged as `assets/img/brand_mark.tga`. |
| `HOST_IMGUI` + `IMGUI_DIR <path>` | Reuse Dear ImGui already compiled by the host, avoiding duplicate core/backend symbols. `IMGUI_DIR` must contain `imgui.h` and the backend headers. |

`RECOMP_UI_HOST_IMGUI=ON` plus `RECOMP_UI_HOST_IMGUI_INCLUDE=<path>` remains
available as a global compatibility route for existing hosts. New integrations
should prefer the per-target `HOST_IMGUI IMGUI_DIR ...` arguments.

### Definitions added to the target

`recomp_target_launcher_ui(target ...)` adds definitions with `PRIVATE`
visibility:

| Definition | When | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `RECOMP_LAUNCHER` | Always | Lets host source in the same target compile its launcher call sites. |
| `RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS=0` or `1` | Always | Mirrors the CMake Mods option consistently across C and C++ launcher sources. |
| `SDL_MAIN_HANDLED` | Always | Keeps the host's real `main()` as the entry point instead of SDL redirecting it. |
| `LNG_SDL3=1` | SDL3 selected | Chooses SDL3 types, events, and Dear ImGui platform glue. Absence means SDL2. |
| `LNG_GLES2=1`, `IMGUI_IMPL_OPENGL_ES2=1` | Android | Selects the GLES2 renderer path. |

Because the definitions are `PRIVATE`, they do not propagate to libraries that
link the game target. The public provider ABI does not need
`RECOMP_UI_ENABLE_MODS`; a separately built mod manager can always implement
`RecompLauncherCModProvider`. Only the target containing recomp-ui and the
launcher call needs the generated frontend definition.

## Build & self-test

recomp-ui builds a standalone harness that fabricates the same C ABI a real host
passes, so you can iterate on the UI without a game:

```sh
cmake -G Ninja -S . -B build
cmake --build build -j
# Preview a console: LNG_VARIANT = psx | snes | gba | genesis | ...
LNG_VARIANT=genesis ./build/recomp-ui-launcher
```

`LNG_SCRIPT` drives it headless for screenshot regression, e.g.
`LNG_SCRIPT="wait:40;view:settings;shot:out.png;quit"` (see
[`src/launcher_debug.h`](src/launcher_debug.h)).

Requires SDL3 (`find_package(SDL3 CONFIG)`) by default, OpenGL, and a C++17
compiler. Configure with `-DSNESRECOMP_SDL_BACKEND=SDL2` to exercise the
supported SDL2 fallback.

---

## Layout

```
src/common/             launcher core (.c/.h), Dear ImGui backend, C ABI header
src/common/launcher_model.*   UI-toolkit-free view-model (state + behavior)
src/consoles/<id>/      per-console unit: <id>_profile.h (SystemProfile row) +
                        any native bridge (e.g. genesis_binds.c, psx_binds.c)
src/launcher_system.h   aggregates the console units + by-id / infer lookups
src/third_party/        vendored Dear ImGui, stb, tinyfiledialogs
assets/common/          fonts + chrome art shared by every console
assets/consoles/<id>/   per-console art (pad_genesis.tga, pad_gba.tga, ...)
recomp_ui.cmake         reusable recomp_target_launcher_ui() integration helper
docs/ARCHITECTURE.md    composition + inheritance design
CMakeLists.txt          standalone self-test build (recomp-ui-launcher)
```

Adding a console = one directory under `src/consoles/<id>/` (profile row +
optional native bind bridge) registered in `src/launcher_system.h`, a theme in
`src/common/launcher_theme.h`, per-console art under `assets/consoles/<id>/`,
and its `.c` files + assets wired into `recomp_ui.cmake`.

packaged_documentation.Docs/Story/README.md:
# Writing for the story

Weltall loads story additions from plain text files at startup. You can change scripts, add dialogue
or create playable scenes without recompiling. These guides use the files in `Content/Story` as
examples.

Keep original game scripts and text out of these files. Reference the map, instruction offset or
message you need, and include only your additions. Weltall reads the original content from your disc.

## Packs and documents

Each folder in `Content/Story` is a pack, and each `.txt` file is a document. Packs load in folder-name
order, with documents in filename order. If a document can't be read, the game stops at startup and
shows the filename and line number.

| Pack | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `additions` | Small changes controlled by individual settings, such as the RPS helper and staging fix |
| `disc2` | Disc 2 expansion examples, used when the player selects "Extended" at the start of Disc 2 |

The first line identifies the document type:

| First line | Purpose | Guide |
|---|---|---|
| `map 7` | Patch an existing map's scripts and messages | [Changing a map](changing-a-map.md) |
| `map 732 from 382` | Reuse a disc map's assets with entirely new scripts | [A map of your own](a-map-of-your-own.md) |
| `map 730 over 613` | Reuse a disc map's assets and scripts, then patch them | [A map of your own](a-map-of-your-own.md) |
| `battle event 19` | Change where battle narration starts and add an introduction | [A battle's narration](a-battles-narration.md) |
| `world map 8` | Add locations, names and arrival points, or temporarily hide the ship | [The world map](the-world-map.md) |
| `way back` | Map expansion saves to a compatible point in the original story | [A stretch of story](a-stretch-of-story.md) |
| `subtitles` | Add titles within the original chapters | [Subtitles](subtitles.md) |

[A stretch of story](a-stretch-of-story.md) explains how these fit together: branch from the original
story, play through new scenes and maps, then return with the game state matching the original.

## Script and message syntax

Scripts use the instruction names and operands printed by `WeltallMapText`.
`Source/WeltallCore/Public/Field/EventAssembly.h` describes labels, `If`, operands, `define` and `data`.
`Source/WeltallCore/Private/Field/EventInstructionRows*.cpp` lists the instructions and their operands.

For message syntax, see `Source/WeltallCore/Public/Text/MesText.h`. Messages use plain characters,
line breaks and markup such as `{page}`, `{wait 0A}` and `{name 00}`.

## Inspecting existing maps

`WeltallMapText` builds alongside the core tests (see the main README). It prints a field map from
your discs in the same format used by story documents:

```sh
WeltallMapText 616        # map 616 from the first disc, as text
WeltallMapText 369 369 1  # map 369, numbered 369, from disc 1
```

The listing includes instruction offsets for `expect` and `detour`, and messages named `msg0`,
`msg1`, etc. It contains original game scripts and text, so use it as a reference without committing it.

Use the entrance coordinates and actor positions (`SetPosition`, `WalkTo`) in the listing to place
characters and doors. Placing an actor off the walkmesh stops the game with an error identifying the actor.

## Checking your work

The core tests read each document against your discs. They check that:

- Patches match their target maps, with bug fixes both enabled and disabled.
- New maps can be built and entered.
- Expansion sequences start from the original scenes and return to the same game state.

Run the tests as described in the main README. Story tests use the `[Story]` tag. If a document no
longer matches its target, the test reports its filename and line number.

You can preview a scene with the editor's `RenderScreen` commandlet. It runs headlessly from a chosen
map and story value, saving images as it goes:

```sh
UnrealEditor-Cmd Weltall.uproject -run=RenderScreen -AllowCommandletRendering -RenderOffscreen -unattended
    -Screen=Field -Map=616 -FieldEntrance=1 -FieldStory=252 -StoryMode=Expanded
    -Reader=0.6,0.055 -Seconds=70 -Every=1 -Size=1280x720 -Out=Saved/Renders/shot.png
```

`-Reader` advances dialogue at a reading pace. `-Route=x,z;x,z;!x,z` walks the party through the listed
points and presses confirm at points marked `!`, such as a door. `-SoundOut=sound.wav` records audio,
and `-Every=0.016` captures every frame for a video. Run the commandlet without options to see the rest.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact supported originals
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Xenogears USA PlayStation discs. Source identifies Disc 1 SLUS_006.64 executable SHA1 560bbdbeb9264c935294ecad5a3d4ab230a006a9 and Disc 2 SLUS_006.69 a378608389f04456925c6afaccb644ab90eaff30. These are executable fingerprints, not whole-image signatures. Keep full CUE/BIN or CHD images for movie audio; upstream accepts ISO/IMG but movies are silent with those representations. Supported independently permitted undubs/text patches are separate inputs. Japanese retail discs can be inspected upstream but are not playable originals for this route.

persistence.title: Preserve player data and both disc paths
persistence.instruction: Keep the actual %LOCALAPPDATA%/Weltall tree, including Saves, settings, Saved/Crashes and logs, plus the complete package, Games/ originals, optional Assets/ replacements and any configured external paths. Options can import individual or memory-card saves and export .mcr cards under Saves/Cards; these are upstream operations, not observed conversion/restore compatibility. Disc swaps and Disc 2-only starts follow the original progression requirements. Keep independent old/new recovery before replacing or importing data; this guide performs no import, conversion, backup, restore, migration or deletion.

limitations: Keep the full Unreal package, supported originals and actual Weltall data. Select the native Shipping entry; bootstrap, optional patches, movie-audio formats and save imports have separate scope.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: What exact Japanese Rev0 ROM digest is accepted by the selected Marchwind64 release?

content_selection.unselected_members: full physical/logical index checks only; no full CRC or ABI claim

pe_prefix.scope: bounded header only; no execution, complete imports, ABI or dependency resolution

SRW64 Chapter Title (content/fonts/SRW64ChapterTitle.ttf)
=========================================================

The brush lettering of the Super Robot Taisen 64 chapter title cards as a font,
for the Japanese title cards the host draws natively. Every glyph is traced from
the cards' own images in the game ROM: tools/content/build_title_fonts.py cuts
the cards into characters by their transcription and traces each with potrace.
It holds only the 344 characters the cards use.

The lettering is part of Super Robot Taisen 64 (c) BANPRESTO 1999; it is not
covered by this project's GPL licence.

SRW64 Symbols (content/fonts/SRW64Symbols.ttf)
===============================================

This font holds the symbols the SRW64 text needs that HarmonyOS Sans lacks:
U+25B6 ▶, U+25B7 ▷, U+25C0 ◀, U+1F527 🔧, and the weapon markers in the Private
Use Area: U+E0F1 circled P, U+E0F2 circled B, U+E0F3 the ranged-attack gunsight,
U+E0F4 the melee fist and U+E23F the MAP badge. It is built by
tools/content/build_symbol_font.py.

- The three triangles are outlines taken from DejaVu Sans (Book), rescaled and
  repositioned. DejaVu Sans is covered by the licence reproduced below: Bitstream
  Vera copyright and licence, DejaVu changes in the public domain. As that licence
  requires for modified fonts, this font's name contains neither "Bitstream" nor
  "Vera", and the notices below travel with every copy.
- The wrench and weapon marker glyphs were drawn for the SRW64 project after the
  original game's icons and are distributed under the same terms as the rest of
  this font. The letters in the P, B and MAP markers are outlines taken from DejaVu
  Sans Bold, under the same DejaVu licence. The fist (U+E0F4) was traced from an
  image generated for the project with Qwen Image 3.0 Pro from the original icon
  (content/fonts/marker-fist.svg).

==============================================

Yukari "Shinmera" Hafner, available at https://shinmera.com/promptfont
(PromptFont is based on the Xolonium font by Severin Meyer).

route.title: Attach the already configured normal player
route.instruction: Select Marchwind64.exe, use the complete Marchwind64-windows-x64 directory as working directory and leave arguments empty after upstream setup. Review the exact intent and request Play separately. The native desktop entry uses the remembered/validated original and continues into the linked runtime/UI. Complete missing-ROM, preparation or conflicting-data prompts upstream before retrying; do not add debug-server, sample campaign, probe, save-export or mod-preparation arguments to normal Play.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact Japanese Rev0 original
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Super Robot Taisen 64 Japan Rev0 N64 ROM. The selected variant pins normalized ROM SHA256 ee5f4a21d8e5f7827d21199e27800edf250df9a8e4d10befb1a6992df597b13e and XXH3-64 bb8703e9d7c77f4f, game ID srw64-jp-rev0. Upstream normalizes accepted N64 byte orders; these are not identical raw-file hashes for every representation. Finish upstream original selection and derived-data preparation first. No ROM, converter, helper, compiler, art/voice pack or game is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Preserve system, local and synchronized copies
persistence.instruction: Without an existing portable choice, Windows uses %LOCALAPPDATA%/SRW64Recomp. An already existing user-data/ beside the program opts into local precedence; missing settings and complete absent save/campaign groups can be imported from the system root, while existing local groups are not silently merged. Normal exit can synchronize present local groups back to the system root, with confirmation and sync-backups before replacing different data. Keep both roots, sync-backups, presentation.json, rules.json, input.json, saves/, campaigns/, retained/derived ROM data and actual external paths. An existing --user-dir selects one root without automatic import/sync. This guide creates no marker and performs no synchronization, conversion, backup, restore or deletion.

limitations: Select the 0.5.2 player, not a voice-mod release. Keep both system and existing user-data roots with sync-backups; explicit user-dir and normal-exit synchronization differ.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Select recommended user beta rather than performance-test release and bind correct regional disc and preparation route.

content_selection.unselected_members: full physical/logical index checks only; no full CRC or ABI claim

# Skies of Arcadia Legends: Recompiled

A native port of **Skies of Arcadia Legends** (GameCube) for Windows, Linux, macOS and Android, made by static
recompilation. It doesn't contain the game: you supply your own copy of the disc, and the game's
data is read from it.

This is a **beta** (v0.83). Please report what you run into.

## What you need

- Your own dump of the **USA**, the **European** or the **Japanese** GameCube disc (game ID `GEAE8P`,
  `GEAP8P` or `GEAJ8P`, the original release; the Japanese one is *Eternal Arcadia Legends*). The
  European disc has English, German, French and Spanish (the **Language** tab in Settings and in the
  in-game menu, which can restart the game in the new language at once); the Japanese disc is in
  Japanese (the port's own menus stay in English). The import checks the game.
- As RVZ, ISO, GCM, GCZ, WIA or CISO.
- **Windows:** 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1703 or later) or 11.
- **Linux:** 64-bit (x86_64) with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 36, SteamOS,
  Bazzite or later), and a Vulkan or OpenGL driver.
- **macOS:** macOS 13 or later on an Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or newer).
- **Android:** a 64-bit (arm64) device with Android 7 or newer. Tested on a Retroid Pocket 5
  (Snapdragon 865), which runs it at full speed at 60 fps. Slower devices may not.

## Getting started

**Windows:** unzip, run `Skies of Arcadia Legends.exe`, choose **Select Disc** and pick your disc image. The
launcher imports it (a few seconds), patches it and starts the game. After that, **Start Game** or
**Continue** start it directly.

**Linux:** the `.AppImage` is one file with the libraries it needs inside: make it executable
(`chmod +x`, or the file's Properties) and run it. Or extract the `.tar.gz` and run
`./SkiesOfArcadiaLegends` from inside the folder. The rest is as on Windows.

**macOS:** unzip, and open **Skies of Arcadia Legends** (move it to Applications if you like); the
rest is as on Windows. The app isn't notarized by Apple, so the first time macOS says it can't check
it: open **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and choose **Open Anyway** (or Control-click the app
and choose **Open**). If the keyboard does nothing in the game, allow it in **Privacy & Security →
Input Monitoring**.

**Android:** install the APK, open **Skies of Arcadia Legends** and pick your disc image when asked.

**Updating from an earlier version:** saves, save states and settings carry over. On Windows and
Linux, if the launcher asks for your disc once more, choose **Select Disc** and pick the same disc image
(it updates your earlier import in a few seconds). On Android, install the new APK over the old one;
the app updates the imported disc by itself.

Your saves and settings are kept in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Skies of Arcadia Legends` (Windows),
`~/.local/share/Skies of Arcadia Legends` (Linux), `~/Library/Application Support/Skies of Arcadia
Legends` (macOS) or in the app's own storage (Android). Uninstalling the Android app deletes them, so make a backup first
(**Settings → Saves → Back up saves**), or move them out of the app's storage.

**Settings → Disc → Data folder → Change...** moves them to a folder or drive of your choice; the
launcher starts again on it. On Android (11 or later) it asks for All files access first (the game reads its files
by name there), and the data then stays when the app is uninstalled. On Windows and Linux, an empty
`portable.txt` beside the program keeps everything in a `User` folder beside it instead; the first start
in portable mode offers to move the data you already have into it.

### Bringing your saves

**Settings → Saves → Import a save** takes a save you already have and puts it where the game finds
it. It asks first, then opens a file picker. It takes:

- **A memory card save** from Dolphin or a real GameCube: `.gci` (Dolphin's GCI folders, e.g.
  `GC/USA/Card A`), `.gcs` or `.sav` (memory card tools such as GameShark or MaxDrive).
- **A whole memory card** from Dolphin (`MemoryCardA.USA.raw`) or a card dump (`.gcp`): its Skies of
  Arcadia Legends saves are taken, nothing else.
- **A save state** from this port (`.sav` from the `StateSaves` folder), e.g. from your other device.
  Save states only work in the same version of the port; memory card saves work in every version.
- **A backup** made with **Settings → Saves → Back up saves** on Android (`.zip`): every save in it.

A memory card save replaces the file with the same number here; the one it replaces is kept beside
it as a `.pre-import.bak` file (`.pre-import.2.bak` and so on if you import over it again). A save state is added to the ones you have. **Continue** then starts
from what you imported. A save has to be from the same version as your disc (USA, European or
Japanese).

## What it adds

- **Widescreen** 16:9 with the HUD at the screen edges, **Match screen** for any other shape
  (ultrawide 21:9 up to 32:9, 16:10, a phone's 20:9), or the original 4:3 (identical to the
  original game). On an ultrawide, a higher Resolution keeps the picture sharp across the width.
- **HUD placement** on a wide picture: at the screen edges, in a centred 21:9 or 16:9 area (easier to
  take in on an ultrawide), or the original 4:3 layout in the middle.
- **60 fps** by frame interpolation, or the original 30.
- Internal resolution and anti-aliasing; texture filtering (smooth or sharp pixels), anisotropic
  filtering, and **Scaling**: Sharp keeps the original resolution (640x528) crisp on a large screen.
- **Camera control:** hold Z and use the C-stick to tilt, and R / L to zoom out / in (towns, dungeons
  and the world map; on the world map Z + C-stick left / right also turns around the ship).
- **Battle speed** up to 4x: tap Z during a battle. Spells and special attacks, ship battles' too,
  still play at normal speed, so their sound stays with the picture.
- **Field speed** 1.5x, 2x or 3x for cutscenes, towns, dungeons and sailing: hold Z and press X
  outside battle. A desktop PC holds 2x everywhere; 3x needs a fast one. Where a device can't keep
  up, it steps down by itself to what that device holds (a Retroid Pocket 5: about 1.25x-1.5x).
- **Options:** random encounter rate (off to 4x), Hold B for no random battles, EXP / gold / magic
  EXP (off to 4x), and Invincible (press L3 or R3 to toggle).
- **Romhacks** that change the game's data, such as Maeson's rebalance: see below.
- **Keyboard and button mapping:** play with the keyboard on Windows and Linux, and change any
  button or key (see *Controls*). Any controller you press is picked up without setup.
- **Save states:** five slots, plus an auto-save every 10 minutes on the field (the newest three are
  kept). Your memory card saves are never touched by a state.
- **Continue** in the launcher starts from your newest save state or memory card save, whichever is
  newer. A memory card save loads straight into the game, without the intro or title screen.
- **Import a save** from Dolphin, a GameCube memory card or another device (see *Bringing your
  saves*).
- **Dreamcast music** (optional), from your own Dreamcast disc: see below.
- **Uncensored** (optional), the original Japanese models and textures, from your own Eternal
  Arcadia discs: see below.
- **HD textures** (optional), from a texture pack you downloaded: see below.

### Dreamcast music

**Settings → Dreamcast → Import a Dreamcast disc...** in the launcher takes your own Skies of Arcadia
Dreamcast disc as a **GDI** (with its track files beside it) or a **CHD** (Android: CHD). Either
disc has most of the music; import both for all of it (they can be from different regions). Then set **Music** to **Dreamcast**
(there, or in the settings menu's Dreamcast tab in game). The Dreamcast's sound driver plays the songs
from your disc on an emulated sound chip, in place of the GameCube music. The two streamed songs
that differ on the Dreamcast (the intro's, disc 1, and a story scene's, disc 2) play the disc's
recordings too, converted once the first time they're needed. **Intro music** (below the import)
picks the intro's: the Dreamcast recording is a different cut that doesn't line up with this intro's
scenes; GameCube keeps them in step. Music imported with an earlier version has no streamed songs:
import the disc again. **Remove** deletes the imported music and Eternal Arcadia files.

### Uncensored

The Western releases (and every GameCube version) changed some art; only the Japanese Dreamcast
release, **Eternal Arcadia**, has the originals. Import your own Eternal Arcadia **disc 1** and **disc
2** the same way (**Settings → Dreamcast**; v1.009, the regular release), then set **Uncensored** to
**On** there or in the settings menu's Dreamcast tab. It brings back Dyne's and Gilder's cigars, Don's
cigar and bottle, Bellena's outfit, the tavern sign, the red-faced drunks and their drinks, and
Gilder's victory pose with his smoke (one of his three) and Vigoro in Aika's cell, from the next
area or scene the game loads.
The models are converted for your GameCube disc into `DreamcastUncensor` in the data folder; each
file is checked first and keeps its original's size, so save states work either way. Not yet: the
cut or rewritten scenes (the drunk sailor, Ramirez's blood, "loqua").

### HD textures

Texture packs made for Dolphin work, for example **Skies of Arcadia HD** by Bighead and frozenwings
(Dolphin forums). None is included. **Settings → Graphics → Import a texture pack...** takes the
`.7z` or `.zip` you downloaded (on desktop, **Import a folder...** an unpacked one) and turns **HD
textures** on; switch it there or in game. Only the pack's `GEA` textures are copied when it has
that folder, without its optional extras; else all of its textures. Each import adds to what is
imported, so a pack in several archives (the **HD Texture Pack 4x Upscaled** comes as six) can be
imported one archive at a time, or all at once: pick them all in the Android picker, or put them in
one folder or `.zip` / `.7z` and import that. **Remove** deletes everything imported. On Android,
take a pack's **PNG** download where there is one: most phones can't show BC7 DDS textures (with
their own driver; a Turnip driver can). BC1 and BC3 DDS textures work.

### Romhacks

A romhack of the game that changes its **data** plays like the original disc: patch your own disc
image with the romhack's patch (DeltaPatcher for an `.xdelta`, Lunar IPS / Floating IPS for an
`.ips`), then pick the patched image with **Select Disc** (Android: **Change Disc**). The launcher
shows *modified* beside the game's name. Enemy and item stats, encounter tables, scripts, text,
textures and models all count as data; so do the tables inside `main.dol`.

A romhack that changes the game's **code** can't run on this port's recompiled code, and the import
says so. One code change is recognised and replaced by an option of the port's own: the **hold B for
no random encounters** patch (cleartonic's, also built into **Maeson's rebalance**, which therefore
plays) becomes **Settings → Gameplay → Hold B**.

A romhack's save states are kept apart from the original game's (a state brings back the game's
item and magic tables, so they mustn't mix): Continue, the menu's slots and the auto-saves only see
the disc you play. Its memory card saves sit beside the original game's (the romhack keeps the disc
ID), which the romhack's author says is fine.

## Controls

On Windows and Linux the keyboard and a controller both work, together or on their own. The game
uses whichever controller you press, so a controller plugged in later or a second one needs no setup
(started from Steam with Steam Input, Steam's controller works the same way; the Steam Controller
shows as "Steam Controller"). On Android the built-in controller, or
the first one you connect, is set up for you, and the game also switches to whichever controller you
press, so a Bluetooth controller works next to a handheld's own; without one, the game shows touch
controls (the in-game **Back** menu turns them on and off).

| GameCube | Controller (Xbox / PlayStation) | Keyboard |
|---|---|---|
| A / B | A / B (Cross / Circle) | Space / Left Shift |
| X / Y | X / Y (Square / Triangle) | F / R |
| Z | RB (R1) | Tab |
| L / R | LT / RT (L2 / R2) | Q / E |
| Start | Start (Options) | Enter |
| Control stick | Left stick | W A S D |
| C-stick | Right stick | I J K L |
| D-pad | D-pad | Arrow keys |

The face buttons go by name, not position: Xbox A is GameCube A. Every button and key can be
changed: **Settings → Controls** in the launcher, or **Controls → Button mapping** in the in-game
menu (on Android too). The controller's A and B can be changed but not cleared, so the menu always
works. On Linux the keyboard needs an X11 session or XWayland (what most desktops run games in).

The game's own controls are unchanged; on top of them:

| Input | What it does |
|---|---|
| Esc, the controller's Back / View (Create) / Select, or hold Z and press Start | the settings menu (L / R switch tabs; B, Start or Esc close it). Its Saves tab saves and loads states |
| Hold Z + C-stick up / down | tilt the camera |
| Hold Z + R / L | zoom out / in |
| Tap Z in battle | battle speed: Normal, 2x, 3x, 4x |
| Hold Z and press X outside battle | field speed (cutscenes, walking, sailing): Normal, 1.5x, 2x, 3x |
| L3 or R3 (a stick click) | Invincible on / off (a key for it can be set in Button mapping) |

Every setting is also in the launcher's **Settings** window, with a short description of each.

## Known issues

- On Android, battles top out at about 2.5x speed on a Snapdragon 865; 3x and 4x settle at 2x.
- On Android, the field speed tops out at about 1.25x-1.5x on a Snapdragon 865 (1.5x on foot, 1.25x on
  the world map and in cutscenes).
- An auto-save can cause a brief hitch on Android.
- If you change Picture while the world map's menu (Start) is open, the flight meter and compass keep
  the old shape until you close that menu.
- At the widest shapes (32:9), a few scenes show unfinished scenery at the far edges.
- **macOS: the PS button opens Apple's Game Overlay** and the game stops responding until it's
  closed (press PS or Esc again). Use **Create** for the game's settings menu.
- **"Game files missing" when the game starts (Windows / Linux / macOS):** extract the whole zip again and keep
  its files together; if the file named there disappears again, your antivirus removed it.

## Reporting a problem

Please say what happened and where in the game. On Android, open **Settings → About → Copy device
info** and paste it into the report: it names the phone, its chip and the graphics driver.

**Android GPU drivers:** on Adreno devices, **Settings → Graphics → GPU driver** can load a driver
package (for example Mesa Turnip) when the device's own driver crashes or draws things wrong. This is
unsupported; if the game doesn't close normally with a new driver, the app goes back to the device's
own driver by itself, and after the first normal session it asks whether to keep the new one.
On any Android device, **Settings → Graphics → Renderer** can switch from Vulkan to OpenGL ES if the
game crashes or draws things wrong with Vulkan.

**Windows / Linux graphics:** when the graphics driver can't start Vulkan ("Failed to create Vulkan
device" or a similar message), the game switches to OpenGL by itself and keeps it (**Settings →
Display → Graphics backend**). If neither starts, install the latest driver for your graphics card.

**60 fps on slower devices:** if 60 fps can't keep full speed for a while, the settings menu opens
once by itself on Frame rate, so you can switch to 30 fps. Nothing changes unless you choose it.

# Third-party software

Skies of Arcadia Legends: Recompiled is distributed under the GNU General Public License, version 3
(`COPYING`). It includes or links the following:

- [ModernGekko](https://github.com/ExpansionPak/ModernGekko) (runtime and launcher): GPL-3.0
- [DolRecomp](https://github.com/ExpansionPak/DolRecomp) (static recompiler; its runtime support
  code is linked into the game module): GPL-3.0
- [Dolphin](https://github.com/dolphin-emu/dolphin) (video, audio, input and hardware code, through
  ModernGekko's RecompCore fork): GPL-2.0-or-later, used here under GPL-3.0
- [{fmt}](https://github.com/fmtlib/fmt): MIT
- [Highly Theoretical](https://github.com/kode54/Highly_Theoretical) by Neill Corlett, maintained by
  kode54 (the Dreamcast sound chip, AICA with its ARM7, for the Dreamcast music option): GPL-3.0
- [libchdr](https://github.com/rtissera/libchdr) by Romain Tisserand (reads CHD disc images for the
  Dreamcast music import):
  BSD-3-Clause (`licenses/libchdr-LICENSE.txt`), with its bundled LZMA SDK (public domain), miniz (MIT)
  and Zstandard decoder (BSD-3-Clause)
- The [LZMA SDK](https://www.7-zip.org/sdk.html) by Igor Pavlov, version 23.01 (its 7z decoder, which
  reads `.7z` texture packs for the HD textures import): public domain

Dolphin's own third-party components (SDL, Dear ImGui, zlib-ng, Zstandard, cubeb, mbed TLS and others)
are listed with their licences in `THIRD-PARTY-DOLPHIN.md`, a copy of Dolphin's `Externals/licenses.md`.

The source code for this release, including every change made to the projects above (`patches/`), is
available from the project's repository, https://github.com/ogdanimal/SkiesOfArcadiaLegends-Recomp, at
this release's tag.

Fonts are not bundled: the launcher and the in-game menu use the system's own fonts (Segoe UI on
Windows, Roboto on Android).

The launcher background art (I_LIKE_SONIC) and the app icon art (Reckoner) are from SteamGridDB and
belong to their artists; they aren't covered by the GPL.

route.title: Attach the supported waiting launcher
route.instruction: Select Skies of Arcadia Legends.exe, use the complete extracted player directory as working directory and leave arguments empty after import. Review the intent and request Play separately, then use its Start Game/Continue action. The source launcher starts its matching sibling runner, hides its window and waits for the game process; Windows self-restarts also wait for their replacement. Keep that complete waiting route rather than guessing a private cache or runner argument. End the game normally and close any returning launcher when the session is finished. Complete disc changes, repairs, language restarts or updates upstream before retrying.

source_setup.title: Prepare the supported regional GameCube original
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own original Skies of Arcadia Legends USA GEAE8P, Europe GEAP8P or Japan GEAJ8P GameCube release. Upstream accepts RVZ, ISO/GCM, GCZ, WIA or CISO, checks/imports the selected disc and applies its local port patch. Only one regional disc is installed at a time; Change Disc replaces that selection. Finish upstream import/settings first and keep independent originals and recovery. No disc, patcher, helper, compiler, game or optional content is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Preserve the actual data selection and compatible save sets
persistence.instruction: Normally keep %LOCALAPPDATA%/Skies of Arcadia Legends with imported/patched game data, region-specific cards, save states, settings, caches and logs. An existing portable.txt selects User/ beside the program; the upstream Data folder setting can move data elsewhere and restart, so retain the actual selected external root and all former roots before maintenance. Roms/hacks have separate save states even where card files live beside original saves. Dolphin/real-card imports and cross-region transfers are distinct upstream operations. This guide performs no import, patching, conversion, move, backup, restore or deletion.

limitations: Use the complete user beta and matching regional import. Keep the selected data root, original discs, regional cards and separate state sets; optional Dreamcast content remains separately supplied.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

packaged_documentation.RUNTIME-NOTICES.md:
# Third-Party Dependency Status

The root MIT license covers original project contributions. Existing third-party
copyright and license notices retain their separate scope. It does not relicense
game content, generated ROM-derived output, or third-party code. Distribution of
a combined work must also satisfy every applicable dependency license, including
GPL requirements where GPL-covered components are used.

Third-party font files are vendored under `launcher/ui/fonts`, with their
SIL Open Font License notices and source/hash manifest. The launcher statically
links RmlUi and FreeType, fetched at the revisions in `launcher/ui/CMakeLists.txt`.
Their retained notices are indexed in [launcher notices](launcher/ui/THIRD-PARTY.txt)
and [notice provenance](launcher/ui/licenses/provenance.json).

Other external repositories are cloned locally under the ignored `tools/`
directory at commits recorded in `dependencies.lock.json`. These local build
and research dependencies are distinct from the components bundled in the
launcher release archive.

The tracked N64Recomp patch series necessarily contains limited context from
the MIT-licensed upstream source. Its required copyright and permission notice
is preserved byte-for-byte from the locked upstream revision in
`patches/n64recomp/LICENSE.upstream`. That notice applies to the upstream
material represented in the patch payload; it does not change the license of
project-authored material.

The RT64/Plume compatibility edits embedded in `CMakeLists.txt` retain
the exact pinned MIT notices in `patches/rt64/LICENSE.upstream` and
`patches/plume/LICENSE.upstream`.

The CIC-NUS-6105 challenge-response algorithm in
`src/runtime/cic_nus_6105.cpp` is conservatively attributed to X-Scale (2011).
The complete upstream copyright, redistribution conditions, disclaimer and
views paragraph are retained both in that source and in
`patches/cic/LICENSE.upstream`. The source was inspected at BizHawk commit
`bdddf4a58aa1a022afb11dc73294a81a5aa7bbd5`, path
`libmupen64plus/mupen64plus-core/src/memory/n64_cic_nus_6105.c`.
The project integration uses C++ types and packed PIF RAM. This notice applies
to the upstream algorithm; the project license does not override upstream rights.

## Components and attribution

| Component | Status |
|---|---|
| N64Recomp | MIT; local build tool; tracked patch context carries `patches/n64recomp/LICENSE.upstream` |
| LLVM/Clang | Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception; ignored local compiler toolchain |
| OpenSSH `ssh-keygen` | BSD-style/component-specific notices; OS-provided signature tool only |
| N64ModernRuntime | GPL-3.0-only; evaluated runtime reference, not the project's native bridge |
| RT64 | MIT; renderer |
| SDL 2.26.3 | Zlib; controller API and existing runtime DLL; [retained notice](launcher/ui/licenses/SDL2-zlib.txt) |
| Plume | MIT; embedded compatibility patch context carries `patches/plume/LICENSE.upstream` |
| CIC-NUS-6105 algorithm | X-Scale (2011), permissive two-condition notice retained in source and `patches/cic/LICENSE.upstream` |
| Jet Force Gemini decompilation | No root license found; consulted facts-only for libultra identification (see attribution below) |

## Launcher dependencies

| Component | Retained notice |
|---|---|
| RmlUi 6.3 | [MIT](launcher/ui/licenses/RmlUi-MIT.txt) |
| RmlUi's robin_hood and itlib containers | [MIT notices](launcher/ui/licenses/RmlUi-Containers-MIT.txt) |
| RmlUi Debugger's Courier Prime Code fonts | [OFL notice](launcher/ui/licenses/RmlUi-Debugger-OFL.txt); retained for the aggregate target, including assets that the linker may omit |
| FreeType 2.14.1 | [FreeType License](launcher/ui/licenses/FreeType-FTL.txt) and [component notices](launcher/ui/licenses/FreeType-ThirdParty.txt), including BDF/PCF, The Open Group, hashing, zlib and HarfBuzz-derived source |
| Barlow | [SIL OFL 1.1](launcher/ui/fonts/Barlow-OFL.txt) |
| Chakra Petch | [SIL OFL 1.1](launcher/ui/fonts/ChakraPetch-OFL.txt) |

The launcher package includes these complete notices under `licenses/`, along
with font and notice provenance manifests. The package builder checks that
every license path referenced by `THIRD-PARTY.txt` exists in the archive inputs.
The launcher uses Win32/DX11; optional RmlUi backends and external FreeType
compression/shaping libraries are not enabled by this build configuration.
FreeType's internal zlib and HarfBuzz-derived source notices are still retained.

## Attribution: Jet Force Gemini decompilation (facts-only consultation)

The Jet Force Gemini decompilation project
(https://github.com/Ryan-Myers/Jet-Force-Gemini) was **consulted** during
Phase 6 for the sole purpose of identifying which addresses in our own
generated set correspond to libultra (N64 SDK) functions. Only factual
symbol data — libultra function names (public SDK API) mapped to ROM
addresses — was used, to guide independently authored HLE implementations.
**No decomp source, headers, or implementation was copied.** The libultra
HLE code in this project is original work authored to the public SDK
contract (see `src/boot/PROVENANCE.md`).

The decomp carries no observed license, so this is a maintainer-approved
research consultation of factual metadata, not a grant of copy rights; it
does not affect the underlying game copyright.

Pinned dependency records and build-tool inventory are in the
[dependency inventory](docs/legal/dependency-license-inventory.md).

## Original device timing

The instruction/cache timing model in `include/jfg/boot/original_timing_cache.h`
and `include/jfg/boot/original_timing_fast.h`, and the cartridge DMA duration
formula in `include/jfg/boot/original_timing_pi_dma.hpp`, are adapted from ares, as vendored in BizHawk revision
`bdddf4a58aa1a022afb11dc73294a81a5aa7bbd5`,
`waterbox/ares64/ares/ares/n64/cpu/` and `n64/pi/dma.cpp`. The copyright and ISC permission
notice are retained in the source, and the complete upstream notice is in
`patches/ares/LICENSE.upstream`.

## Prebuilt beta Microsoft runtime

The local prebuilt beta includes the unmodified x64 Microsoft.VC143.CRT
runtime libraries from the maintainer Visual Studio redistributable folder.
They retain Microsoft licensing; the project MIT license does not apply to
them. See [runtime notice and build input hashes](launcher/runtime-licenses/Microsoft-Visual-Cpp.txt).
The application loads these DLLs locally, without a development-tool installer.

route.title: Attach the prepared normal launcher
route.instruction: Select JFG-Launcher.exe, use its complete extracted player directory as working directory and leave arguments empty. Review the intent and request Play separately, then use its normal Play action with the prepared profile. Source keeps the native frontend and supervised session handle while the game runs; it is not a short-lived compiler wrapper. Keep the matching native runtime/helper/resources together. Do not select the bare jfg-native-boot.exe with its default finite probe, add private child flags, diagnostic replays or developer scene selectors as normal Play. End the actual game normally, then close the returning launcher to finish the session.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact supported N64 original
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Jet Force Gemini US big-endian .z64 ROM: 33,554,432 bytes, SHA1 493ced9008dbe932d6e91179b68e8630cf23a023. The released importer checks the whole file and stores its verified copy as roms/jfg-us.z64 under the selected profile. Other regions, modified originals and byte-swapped files are not admitted by this route. Finish Select ROM and normal profile/settings preparation upstream; keep the independent original. No ROM, converter, helper, compiler or game is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Preserve profiles, copied ROMs and storage selection
persistence.instruction: Normally keep %LOCALAPPDATA%/JFGRecomp with profiles/default and any selected profiles, verified roms/, native profile/configuration, saves, controller-pak data, settings, shader caches and helper/support data. Game > Settings can choose another storage directory, copying existing profile data without overwriting destination files, then restarting the launcher. Existing portable.txt/userdata and storage-location.txt affect that selection. Keep the actual active root, the locator beside the launcher, old roots, originals and recovery together when moving/updating. Cartridge saves and controller paks are different objects; this guide performs no import, migration, backup, restore or deletion.

limitations: Keep the prebuilt launcher/runtime unit, exact imported US ROM, profiles and storage-location.txt. Do not attach a finite-probe default or infer campaign/device acceptance from upstream testing mods.

packaged_documentation.UrbanReignPC-1.4.1/README.txt:
URBAN REIGN - PC PORT 1.4.1
======================================
Created by / Criado por thiagordsfx
GitHub:  https://github.com/thiagordsfx
YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@thiagordsfx

EN
- Open "Urban Reign.exe". In the Game tab pick your own Urban Reign disc image (USA, SLUS-21209, .iso).
  The game is not included: you need your own copy.
- Graphics, controllers (PCSX2 style, multitap, vibration) and mods are set in the launcher.
- Mods: each mod is a folder in game\mods; turn them on in the Mods tab, their options are in the in-game menu (F2).
  CoopTool comes with it: Multiplayer with up to 8 fighters (up to 8 humans) and Free Mode missions with up to 4
  players. For 6 to 8 players switch the multitap on in both ports (launcher, Controls tab).
- Widescreen: real 16:9 by default (the camera shows more). For the original 4:3, set AspectRatio=4:3 in
  game\config.ini, [Video].
- HD textures: put a PCSX2 texture pack in game\textures\SLUS-21209 (the folder with "replacements").
- In game: F11 fullscreen, F3 FPS counter, F5/F9 quick save/load state.
- Needs Windows 10/11 64-bit, a DirectX 11 graphics card and a CPU with SSE4.1.

PT
- Abra o "Urban Reign.exe". Na aba Jogo escolha a sua imagem do Urban Reign (EUA, SLUS-21209, .iso).
  O jogo não vem junto: você precisa da sua própria cópia.
- Gráficos, controles (estilo PCSX2, multitap, vibração) e mods são configurados no launcher.
- Mods: cada mod é uma pasta em game\mods; ligue na aba Mods, as opções ficam no menu do jogo (F2).
  O CoopTool já vem junto: Multiplayer com até 8 lutadores (até 8 humanos) e missões do Free Mode com até 4
  jogadores. Para 6 a 8 jogadores ligue o multitap nas duas portas (launcher, aba Controles).
- Widescreen: 16:9 de verdade por padrão (a câmera mostra mais). Para o 4:3 original, coloque AspectRatio=4:3 no
  game\config.ini, em [Video].
- Texturas HD: coloque um pacote do PCSX2 em game\textures\SLUS-21209 (a pasta com "replacements").
- No jogo: F11 tela cheia, F3 contador de FPS, F5/F9 salvar/carregar estado rápido.
- Precisa de Windows 10/11 64 bits, placa de vídeo DirectX 11 e processador com SSE4.1.

Fan project, not affiliated with Bandai Namco. / Projeto de fãs, sem ligação com a Bandai Namco.

packaged_documentation.UrbanReignPC-1.4.1/game/resources/README:
# Recursos do GS do PCSX2

Copiados de `bin/resources` do PCSX2 (github.com/PCSX2/pcsx2, commit `2954ebe6965669219f1bbd256e958fbd8f83a85d`) e
copiados para `bin/resources` ao lado do `urban.exe` no build (`thirdparty/pcsx2-gs/CMakeLists.txt`).

- `shaders/dx11/`: shaders HLSL dos renderizadores DX11 e DX12 (lidos e compilados em tempo de execução, com cache em
  `bin/shadercache_pcsx2`). GPL-3, como o PCSX2.
- `shaders/common/`: `fxaa.fx` (FXAA, GPL-3 no PCSX2) e `ffx_a.h`/`ffx_cas.h` (AMD FidelityFX CAS, licença MIT no
  cabeçalho de cada arquivo).
- `fonts/Roboto-Regular.ttf`: fonte do OSD (Apache 2.0, ver `fonts/Roboto-Regular-copyright`).

- `shaders/vulkan/`: shaders GLSL do renderizador Vulkan (build do Linux, `docs/LINUX.md`), compilados em tempo de
  execução pelo shaderc, com cache em `shadercache_pcsx2/vulkan_*.bin`. GPL-3, como o PCSX2.

O GS do PCSX2 procura `shaders/dx11` (Windows) ou `shaders/vulkan` (Linux) e `shaders/common`; os de OpenGL ficaram de
fora.
HD texture packs go in SLUS-21209\ (PCSX2 format: SLUS-21209\replacements\...).
Pacotes de texturas HD vão em SLUS-21209\ (formato do PCSX2: SLUS-21209\replacements\...).

route.title: Attach the explicit native game command
route.instruction: Select game/urban.exe and use its complete game/ directory as working directory. Set --iso followed by the quoted absolute path to your already prepared supported ISO. Use the actual original path, not a literal placeholder, and keep that file in place. Review the intent and request Play separately. Source mounts and verifies that ISO, prepares its local game_data cache and runs the linked native game in the selected process. Do not attach the outer browser launcher and assume its child lifetime, add --write-settings as Play or substitute a generated ELF/module DLL.

source_setup.title: Prepare the exact supported original upstream
source_setup.instruction: Use a complete player/components you are independently permitted to use, with your own Urban Reign PS2 USA SLUS-21209 ISO. Source requires SYSTEM.CNF to boot SLUS_212.09 and checks that ELF’s SHA256 60399090fc69ffdb4c39afd30977ab50890b0e33ed6bd9374e4d9497f4246081. This is an executable/revision contract, not a whole-ISO cryptographic fingerprint or other-region admission. Finish the upstream disc and settings flow first, preserving independent originals. No disc, BIOS, importer, helper, compiler, mod or game is obtained or executed here.

persistence.title: Preserve the actual executable-side player roots
persistence.instruction: Normally keep game/config.ini, controls.ini, memcards/mc0/, states/quick.state, game_data/ including derived disc/cache data, mods/, textures/ and the selected ISO. Source defaults writable data to urban.exe’s directory; an established URBAN_USER_DIR chooses another root, URBAN_MC_DIR can select external cards and an explicit quick-state path remains authoritative. Older config/control files can be converted with retained copies; keep all old/new roots and actual paths. Memory-card saves and whole-runtime states differ; do not merge other revisions. This guide performs no import, conversion, backup, restore, migration or deletion.

limitations: Select the native game/urban.exe with the real supported ISO path and preserve its actual card/state roots. Browser-launcher tracking and optional packs/multiplayer remain separate.
rows.closure_boundary: Finite source/setup and existing non-owning registration outcome; independent review and delivery required. No Supported/native/managed-operation acceptance.

rows.canonical_next_action: Review official player setup and data/persistence boundaries for the specific offered route; metadata alone does not qualify execution.

content_selection.unselected_members: full physical/logical index checks only; no full CRC or ABI claim

pe_prefix.scope: bounded header only; no execution, complete imports, ABI or dependency resolution

packaged_documentation.fm4.toml:
game_data_root = "game"
user_data_root = "user"
log_file = "fm4.log"
mount_cache = true
gpu_plugin = "xenos"
gpu_allow_invalid_fetch_constants = true
allow_game_relative_writes = true
resolution_scale = 1
# Build 94 validation baseline: native 1x, ROV, full resolve readback, and a
# synchronous copy into the host-visible guest-RAM alias. This is the first
# tested combination with correct car shadows, road lighting, car textures,
# and trackside assets. Do not add a vblank override to the correctness preset.
readback_resolve = "full"
d3d12_readback_resolve_host_copy = true
render_target_path_d3d12 = "rov"
# The host has no D3D12 debug layer installed; command-prefix diagnostics
# isolated the failure without it.
d3d12_debug = false
# FM4 creates BC textures with packed sub-block mip tails. This host rejects
# their placed-footprint uploads at command-list Close(), so use the existing
# decompression load path for the complete BC mip chain.
d3d12_decompress_unaligned_block_textures = true
d3d12_break_on_error = false
d3d12_break_on_warning = false
occlusion_query_enable = false
query_occlusion_fake_sample_count = 100
mnk_mode = true
# FM4's validated profile requires full readback. Automatic readback caused
# flickering and recurring texture corruption.
# Disc 2 packages are accepted only after their STFS metadata identifies FM4
# marketplace content. The dedicated launcher supplies its package folder with
# FM4_DISC2_ROOT; this cvar provides the equivalent direct configuration path.
# Normal launches use the files installed in user data.
fm4_auto_install_disc2_content = true
fm4_disc2_content_root = ""
keybind_a = "Space"
keybind_start = "Escape"

packaged_documentation.README.md:
# FM4 Recompiled for Windows x64

Extract the complete win-x64 player ZIP into a local folder, such as `D:\Games\FM4-Recompiled`.
No compiler, SDK installation or PowerShell is required to play.
Use Windows 11 x64, an AVX2-capable CPU and a Direct3D 12 GPU; other systems are untested.

Copy the contents of your own extracted FM4 Europe Game of the Year Disc 1 into a `game` folder beside `fm4.exe`.
The complete game tree is required, including `Media` and these three files directly inside `game`:

- `default.xex`: SHA-256 `B34DFB88978819CCCDA6DAFD755E7139970A58FBF6707DFBCBA06846857F52BD`
- `XMediaFacade_default.xex`: SHA-256 `2E82A8D08A59E79F4D68E68B744C2872855BFDD583EB39AD0A9C54E5B3FA1492`
- `SpeechFacade_default.xex`: SHA-256 `49D506A2F8556836943D8BAB3A50B6CD3877524500509EF462FB6E9802F2F4BF`

Double-click `Launch FM4.bat`. Saves and caches stay in the package's `user` folder.
Keep that folder when updating. The player ZIP contains no game files, DLC, Xbox system files or saves.
For optional Disc 2 content, put your own four FM4 packages in `disc2-content` beside `fm4.exe`; the game validates and installs them at startup.

The default is native 1x, D3D12 ROV and full synchronous readback.
Stable 60 FPS is not achieved; heavy scenes can run around 30 FPS, and fresh profiles can cache blank car thumbnails.
The binary package has build/dependency checks, not a new full gameplay qualification.
See [current status](https://github.com/Alexbeav/fm4-recomp/blob/main/docs/STATUS.md).

Project source: [alpha.2](https://github.com/Alexbeav/fm4-recomp/tree/v0.1.0-alpha.2).
SDK source: [f16992c](https://github.com/Alexbeav/rexglue-sdk/tree/f16992c92e610c2d71773994436b442d9946f4e1).
Packaging scripts and current instructions are in the [repository](https://github.com/Alexbeav/fm4-recomp).
Licenses and third-party notices are included beside the executable.

    - `vf_cover_rect.c`

    - `vf_lensfun.c` (GPL version 3 or later)
    - `vf_mcdeint.c`
